skills.name: Analyze YouTube thumbnails from channel analytics
skills.prompt: Using my YouTube analytics for [channel name], compare the click-through rate of my top [10] videos' thumbnails against my channel average. Tell me what the best ones have in common, then suggest [5] new thumbnail ideas for upcoming videos on [topic]. You're finished when I have a short comparison table and written descriptions of each idea.
skills.summary: Grok Bot connected to YouTube analytics compared top-video thumbnails' CTR against the channel average and offered new thumbnail ideas.

skills.name: Analyze a piano recording's BPM, structure and stems
skills.prompt: I have a piano recording at [path to MP3 file]. Install whatever you need (such as ffmpeg and librosa), then analyze it and write me a report covering the BPM, the song structure with approximate timestamps for each section, and separated stems if possible. Save the report as [report filename] in the same folder and tell me when it's finished and where the output files are.
skills.summary: With a skill installed, Claude Code installed ffmpeg and librosa and ran a Python pipeline on a local MP3, producing a report on BPM, structure and stems.

skills.name: Audit and rewrite marketing copy to strip unverified claims
skills.prompt: Read my marketing copy in [file path for landing page, cold email, or pitch deck]. Score each section against a strict rubric: every claim must be specific and verifiable, with no fluff, superlatives, or unsupported numbers. Then write a revised version that removes or flags every unsupported claim, and give me a table of what you changed and why.
skills.summary: A dual-agent system scores landing page, cold email and pitch deck copy against strict rubrics, then rewrites it to remove fluff and unsupported claims.

skills.name: Auto-post blog summaries to Bluesky from RSS
skills.prompt: Watch this RSS feed: [your blog RSS URL]. When a new post appears, write a short summary of under [300] characters in my voice with a link to the post, and draft it for [Bluesky account]. Show me the draft and wait for my approval before posting anything; the job is done when approved posts go live once per new article.
skills.summary: A Zapier agent watches an RSS feed and posts content summaries to Bluesky, helping manage blogging across Medium, Buy Me a Coffee and Bluesky.

skills.name: Automate LinkedIn content creation
skills.prompt: Help me set up a LinkedIn content workflow for [topic or product]. Look at the top posts in my niche, suggest [number] post ideas for the week, and draft each one in my voice: [describe tone]. Show me the drafts and wait for my approval before posting or scheduling anything.
skills.summary: The author used Comet to automate their LinkedIn content workflow and reports 5 unexpected Gumroad sales.

skills.name: Automate technical blog post production
skills.prompt: Build a Make scenario that takes a topic and notes from [Google Sheet or Notion row] and uses ChatGPT to produce an outline, then a full technical blog post draft in [my brand voice], and saves the draft to [Google Docs folder]. The finished job is a draft doc plus a Slack or email message linking to it for my review. Do not publish anything; stop at the draft and show me the result.
skills.summary: The Basilica team built a Make and ChatGPT workflow to produce technical blog posts faster, reporting about 6 hours saved per post.

skills.name: Build a 3D Blender model from a concept image
skills.prompt: I have a concept image at [image path] of [object, e.g. a Fabergé egg]. Using Blender's Python API installed at [Blender path], build a 3D model that matches the image, including [key details, e.g. gold filigree, gems]. Render a preview image and save the .blend file to [output folder]. Stop once the model is saved and you have described what you approximated.
skills.summary: The author pasted a concept image of a Fabergé egg and had a coding agent use a local Blender skill to create a Blender model of it.

skills.name: Build a Great Gatsby lesson plan in a spreadsheet
skills.prompt: Build a [number]-week lesson plan for [book or unit] for [grade level] students in one spreadsheet. Include a tab for weekly topics, a tab with assignments aligned to [standards, e.g. Common Core], and a tab for rubrics and due dates. You are done when every week has at least one reading, one assignment and one assessment, and show me the finished file before I share it.
skills.summary: Ethan Mollick had Claude computer use build a high school Great Gatsby lesson plan with Common Core-aligned assignments in one spreadsheet.

skills.name: Build a balloon-camel simulator for an LED Burning Man totem
skills.prompt: Help me build a simulator of [object or creature made of balloons or lights] for my [art project] with a web frontend. Use my reference images in [folder] and build a basic physics model, then take screenshots of the result, compare them to the references, and refine until it looks right. Finished means I can open the page locally, rotate the camera, and see the model respond. Check with me before installing new tools.
skills.summary: Author used ChatGPT for reference images and Claude Code to build a Go balloon physics simulator with a web frontend, with Claude looping on screenshots and camera control.

skills.name: Build a benchmark image collage in Canva
skills.prompt: Create a one-page collage in [Canva or other design tool] showing [the results, charts, or images I'm attaching]. Use a clean [style] layout with a title and short labels. Give it a time limit of [20 minutes]. If the design tool is not cooperating, stop and tell me what you tried, and don't sign in to anything new or publish or share the design without showing it to me first.
skills.summary: The author had ChatGPT Agent log into Canva and build a collage of benchmark results; after over 75 minutes the result was poor as it fumbled the interface and drew shapes in Python.

skills.name: Build a company structure with Claude Code agents
skills.prompt: Help me set up [company or project name], which [what it does and who it's for], as a small team of agents. Create separate agent definitions for [roles, e.g. marketing, operations, research], and have the marketing agent propose a brand identity with a name rationale, tone of voice, and three color palettes with hex codes. Save everything in a folder called [folder name] and summarize each agent's job. Stop when each role has a working definition and the brand brief is written.
skills.summary: The poster used Claude Code agents to set up a company, including a marketing agent that handles brand identity and color palettes.

skills.name: Build a consultancy-style deck from a vague prompt
skills.prompt: Research [topic, e.g. generative AI trends in 2025] and build a [number, e.g. 16]-slide consultancy-style deck in [UK or US] English. Start with an outline for me to see, use credible cited sources, and put the sources on the final slide. Finish with an exported deck and a note on any claims you are less sure about.
skills.summary: The author had Manus Slides research sources and build a 16-slide outline on 2025 generative AI trends in UK English.

skills.name: Build a newsletter and podcast site with Replit
skills.prompt: Build a simple website for my [newsletter / podcast] called [name] about [topic], with a home page, an archive of [issues / episodes], and a signup form for [email list tool]. Use placeholder content I can replace later. When the clickable prototype works, walk me step by step through publishing it on my custom domain [yourdomain.com], and pause before any step that changes DNS settings or costs money.
skills.summary: A creator got a clickable prototype in 10 minutes but spent 10+ hours failing to put it on a custom URL, until Val Town staff helped launch the MVP.

skills.name: Build a newsletter-to-social content agent (it failed)
skills.prompt: Build a structured Zapier workflow, not a free-roaming agent, that takes my latest newsletter at [URL or doc] and turns it into [3] social posts for [LinkedIn/X]. Use only facts and numbers that appear in the newsletter, and flag any claim without a source instead of making one up. Save the posts as drafts in [Google Doc/Buffer] and don't schedule or publish until I approve. You're done when one newsletter yields three accurate drafts.
skills.summary: The author built a content agent to research, write and schedule social posts, but it invented statistics, so they rebuilt it as a structured workflow.

skills.name: Build a slide deck from a single prompt
skills.prompt: Build a [number]-slide PowerPoint deck on [topic, e.g. quarterly cloud review] for [audience]. Include [key sections or data], simple diagrams where they help, and speaker-friendly titles. Save it as a .pptx in my Downloads folder and tell me when it's done, without sharing or emailing it.
skills.summary: Scout used its pptx skill to build a 5-slide quarterly cloud review deck saved to Downloads, with diagrams and HTML artifacts also covered.

skills.name: Build an automated podcast website that creates companion resources
skills.prompt: Build a website for my podcast [podcast name] where, when I publish a new episode with a title and transcript or notes, it automatically generates companion resources like [show notes, summary, quotes, and a checklist]. Set up the pages and the automation using sample episodes. You're done when I can add a test episode and see the generated resources on its page; ask before deploying publicly.
skills.summary: A podcaster built and deployed a podcast site with Replit over a weekend that automatically generates companion resources when an episode is published.

skills.name: Build an explorable 3D starship with agents
skills.prompt: Build me an explorable 3D model of [a fictional ship, building, or place from a story I love] that I can open in my browser and walk through. Start with [number] decks or rooms, with simple labeled areas and basic camera controls, and add a short personalized story passage at each location featuring [my character's name]. Finish by giving me the command to open it and a list of what each area contains.
skills.summary: A hobbyist used agents to design multiple decks of an Excelsior-class starship as a 3D explorable model and to write personalized fanfic prose around it.

skills.name: Build and deploy an interactive online training course
skills.prompt: Build an interactive online training course on [topic] for [audience]. Plan [number] modules with lessons and short quizzes, build the course as a website, and deploy it live. Then review it with screenshots and fix any styling problems, and send me the link and a short summary of the module structure. Ask me before using any real domain, collecting user data, or publishing it publicly.
skills.summary: An educator had Manus plan modules, build the site and deploy it live, then fix styling problems from screenshots.

skills.name: Build interactive HTML presentations for history classes
skills.prompt: I teach [grade level] history and my next unit is [topic/period]. Create a single self-contained interactive HTML presentation with [number] slides, including a clickable timeline, [maps/primary source viewers/quiz questions], and discussion prompts for students. Keep the text readable on a classroom projector and give me the finished file so I can open it in a browser, with a short list of facts I should double-check.
skills.summary: A history teacher has Claude create interactive HTML presentations for class and used Gemini for lesson-planning brainstorming, freeing time for students.

skills.name: Build small custom agents such as one in a music player
skills.prompt: Help me build a small agent inside [app I use, e.g. my music player or note app] that does one job: [e.g. suggest the next song based on my mood, or tag my library]. Keep it under [number] lines, use [language] and [LLM API], and explain how to run it. Finished means I can run it once on sample data and see the result.
skills.summary: The author writes lots of little agents, for instance inside their music player, noting they are trivial as code.

skills.name: Build your own video-editing agents on a canvas
skills.prompt: Build me a small node-based video-editing pipeline in [my project folder] using [ffmpeg or another tool]. Nodes should include trim, caption, and combine steps that I can chain, and I'll describe the video as [what I want]. Finished means running the pipeline on [sample clip] produces an output file, and you should ask before overwriting any existing files.
skills.summary: Mosaic lets you create and run multimodal video-editing agents in a node-based editor.

skills.name: Compose and produce music through conversation
skills.prompt: Help me write and produce a [genre] song about [topic] through conversation. Start by drafting lyrics and a chord progression, then build a script that turns them into [MIDI or a project file for my music software, e.g. Bitwig]. Check in with me after each section so I can steer it, and stop when we have a complete track I can open and play.
skills.summary: The author used Claude Code to write music and lyrics and build tooling integrated with Bitwig; one honky-tonk song was made entirely by conversation.

skills.name: Compose songs by writing synthesis code
skills.prompt: Write a Python script that synthesizes a short [genre] song from scratch, with a [mood] feel, a clear melody, bass, and drums, and render it to a WAV file. If you can, add sung lyrics about [topic] using the macOS say command. Finish by playing or exporting the file and telling me what to tweak to improve it.
skills.summary: The author ran one-shot experiments where Claude Code wrote Python to synthesize music, including a rock song with sung lyrics via macOS say; sampling a song failed.

skills.name: Create a full music video with lyrics, music and visuals
skills.prompt: Make a music video about [theme or story] in the style of [genre or mood]. Write the lyrics, produce the music, generate the visuals, add audio effects, and assemble everything into one video file at [output folder]. Show me the lyrics and a visual preview before the final render, and stop once the video is exported.
skills.summary: Alex C. had Hermes Agent write lyrics, produce music stems, generate visuals and add audio effects to make a music video on its own.

skills.name: Create a presentation on AI career and salary trends
skills.prompt: Research current trends in [field, e.g. AI careers and salaries] and build a [number]-slide presentation with sourced figures. Keep tables short and readable, using charts or simple visuals instead of dense grids. Finish when the .pptx is ready, and flag any slides whose layout you think still needs manual cleanup.
skills.summary: A tester had ChatGPT Agent build a generative AI careers deck; the result was basic with hard-to-read tables, and the Canva connector was read-only so it couldn't improve it.

skills.name: Create a presentation on agentic AI in retail
skills.prompt: Create a presentation on [topic, e.g. agentic AI in retail] for [audience], about [number] slides. Research it first and show me an outline, and I may add a slide mid-way. When done, export it and check for overlapping text or cut-off content, fixing any you find.
skills.summary: The author had Manus Slides research and build a deck, added a slide mid-run, and fixed some overlapping text after export.

skills.name: Create a subtitled video from one prompt
skills.prompt: Make a [length]-second video about [story or topic] in Grok Imagine's Agent Mode. Plan a short storyline, generate matching scenes of the same subject from different angles, and add subtitles that follow the story. Finish with one exported video and the subtitle text so I can edit it.
skills.summary: Agent Mode in Grok Imagine made a 36-second video with matching scenes from different angles, a storyline and subtitles.

skills.name: Create and publish YouTube videos from script to upload
skills.prompt: Build an n8n workflow that takes a topic from a Google Sheet row, writes a script for a [length]-minute YouTube video about [my niche], generates a voiceover, pulls matching stock footage, assembles the video, and writes the title and description. Update the sheet with the status and file link. Stop before uploading and show me the finished video and metadata so I can approve the YouTube upload.
skills.summary: An n8n pipeline writes a script, adds a voiceover and stock footage, assembles the video, uploads it to YouTube and updates a Google Sheet.

skills.name: Create and schedule social content through Blotato
skills.prompt: Connect to my Blotato account and create a LinkedIn post with an infographic from [topic or data], plus turn this YouTube video [link] into a carousel. Show me drafts and scheduled times across platforms, and pause for my approval before anything is actually scheduled or published.
skills.summary: Cowork with the Blotato connector produces a LinkedIn post with infographic, turns a YouTube video into a carousel, and schedules posts across platforms.

skills.name: Create social media visuals with Canva MCP
skills.prompt: Using the Canva MCP connection, create [number] social media visuals for my app [app name] in [size or platform format], using these brand colors and tone: [colors, tone]. Make one first and show it to me before generating the rest. Keep notes on what the tool could not do well, and stop once I have the set or you hit a clear limit.
skills.summary: The poster tried Canva MCP in Claude Code to produce app marketing visuals and found it a disaster.

skills.name: Create, schedule and post content across platforms automatically
skills.prompt: Build me an n8n workflow that creates [number] social posts per week about [my topics], schedules them for [days and times], and posts them to [platforms, e.g. Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok] through [Blotato or my posting tool]. Have it save each draft to [Google Sheet or Notion] and pause for my approval before any post is published. The job is done when one approved test post appears on every platform at its scheduled time.
skills.summary: An n8n system handles content creation, scheduling and cross-platform posting, with a social upload agent posting via Blotato.

skills.name: Critique blog post drafts for technical errors
skills.prompt: Create a custom Gemini CLI command called /critique that reads the blog draft at [path to draft file] and reviews it for technical errors, such as wrong facts, incorrect code, outdated advice and unclear explanations. It should return a numbered list of issues, each with the quoted passage, why it is wrong and a suggested fix. Do not edit the draft file; just report findings so I can revise and run it again.
skills.summary: A developer built a custom Gemini CLI command that reads a blog draft from disk and critiques it for technical errors, used in an iterative editing loop.

skills.name: Curate a weekly newsletter from RSS feeds
skills.prompt: Monitor these RSS feeds: [feed URLs]. Each week, score items for relevance to [topic/audience], pick the top [10], and write a digest with a short intro and one line per item. Send me a preview on [Telegram], and only send it to [newsletter tool/list] after I reply approve.
skills.summary: OpenClaw monitors RSS feeds, scores items, compiles a digest with intros and sends a Telegram preview; the owner approves and it sends.

skills.name: Curate industry news and draft posts from it
skills.prompt: Build two Zapier Agents. The first runs [daily], picks the [3-5] most relevant news stories about [my industry], summarizes each in a couple of sentences with the link, and adds them to an [Airtable table]. The second reads that table and drafts [LinkedIn/X] posts in [my voice], saved as drafts only, and never posts publicly without my approval. Stick to facts from the stored summaries and don't invent statistics. You're done when one run fills the table and yields draft posts.
skills.summary: One Zapier agent picks industry news, summarizes it, and logs it to Airtable as memory; a second agent drafts posts from that table.

skills.name: Curate local playlists and strip ads from videos with a local agent
skills.prompt: Set up a local workflow on my computer that manages my video playlists. Download the videos from [playlist URLs or channels], cut out ads and sponsored segments, and rank them by how interesting they look based on [my interests, e.g. topics or creators I like]. Finish by giving me a short list of the top [number] videos with a one-line reason for each, and ask me before deleting any files.
skills.summary: The author runs a local LLM agent on a consumer GPU that manages playlists, downloads videos, strips ads and sponsored content, and surfaces the most interesting ones.

skills.name: Design UI pages and explainer videos by voice
skills.prompt: Design a set of UI pages for [type of product, such as a dashboard for my team] based on what I describe: [features and style preferences]. Create the page mockups and a short animated explainer video showing how it works. Finish with the images and video in one folder and a list of design choices you made so I can give feedback.
skills.summary: A user directed Grok Bot by voice to create UI/UX pages for a financial desk, images, animated designs and explainer videos.

skills.name: Design a personal website from a markdown spec
skills.prompt: Read the design spec in [path to your markdown spec file] and use it to design a [personal site / landing page] for [your name or project] in this folder. Build a first version, then show me how to preview it and wait for my feedback before changing anything big. Once I approve a version, list any rules from the spec that should be updated so I can reuse it on other projects.
skills.summary: The author had Codex CLI read a design spec and iterated on it to design his personal site, and he can reuse the spec on other projects.

skills.name: Draft a film script outline, biography book and business card
skills.prompt: Research [subject] and produce [a film script outline, a roughly [number]-word biography of a person or company, or a business card design for [my name and role]]. Cite sources for factual claims and keep the tone [tone]. Deliver one finished document or design file, and tell me what you were unsure about.
skills.summary: A TechRadar writer compared Manus with ChatGPT on script research, a 10,000-word Adobe biography and a business card design.

skills.name: Draft and publish LinkedIn posts from voice notes
skills.prompt: Here are 5 of my past [LinkedIn posts or writing samples] so you can learn my voice. I'll send you a voice note about [topic]; turn it into a LinkedIn post that sounds like me, in under [200] words. Show me the draft and wait for my approval before publishing anything.
skills.summary: A bot learned the developer's voice, turned a voice note into a LinkedIn post and published it; the X bot stalled for lack of a token.

skills.name: Draft and publish blog posts with an SEO-aware agent
skills.prompt: Learn my writing voice from these posts: [URLs or folder]. Then find [5] SEO gaps for my site [domain] on the topic of [topic] and draft one post for the best one. Send the draft to me on [Telegram] and wait for my approval before publishing anything to [CMS].
skills.summary: An author's OpenClaw agent learns his voice, finds SEO gaps, drafts posts, publishes on his Telegram approval and drafts revision briefs when rankings drop.

skills.name: Draft and schedule a weekly newsletter
skills.prompt: Set up a reusable /newsletter command for me. When I run it, it should find the posts I published this week in [folder or site URL], draft a newsletter in my voice using [2-3 past newsletters as style examples], and show me the draft for edits. Do not create or schedule anything in [email tool, e.g. Kit] until I approve; before that step, pause and show me exactly what will be sent and when.
skills.summary: A /newsletter command in Claude Code finds the week's posts, drafts in the author's voice, gets approval, then creates and schedules the broadcast in Kit in about two minutes.

skills.name: Draft articles quoting Kindle highlights and notes
skills.prompt: My Kindle highlights and event notes are in [Obsidian folder path]. Draft an article on [topic] of about [word count] words, quoting relevant highlights with the book title and author named for each. Mark which notes you used. Finish with one clean draft in [file name] and do not change my source notes.
skills.summary: The author saves Kindle highlights and event notes in Obsidian and has Cursor reference them to quote past reading when drafting articles.

skills.name: Draft newsletters and social posts in your own voice
skills.prompt: Load a few of my past newsletters or posts as style examples, then take these raw notes [paste notes] and draft a newsletter or LinkedIn post in my voice. Revise until the tone and structure match how I actually write, and stop once you have a polished draft ready for me to review.
skills.summary: A marketer built a Cursor workflow that learns from his content and scraped posts to write newsletters, LinkedIn posts and threads from raw notes.

skills.name: Draft social posts from trending topics for approval
skills.prompt: Each weekday at [time], check trending topics in [my industry] on [LinkedIn, X, or news sites] and pick the three most relevant to my audience. Draft a LinkedIn post for each in my brand voice, using [link to past posts] as examples. Send the drafts to me at [email or Slack] for approval, and do not post anything yourself. It's done when I have three drafts to review.
skills.summary: A reviewer tested Lindy's browser-driving Computer Use to check trending topics each weekday, draft three LinkedIn posts in brand voice and send them for approval.

skills.name: Edit a full video in Descript with a Dot
skills.prompt: I recorded narration for a video at [path or link to my narration/script]. Find suitable B-roll for each section, build a first-cut edit in [Descript or my editor], add captions, and arrange the visuals over my narration. Share the draft with a short note on what you chose, then revise based on my feedback; stop when I say the edit is final, and don't publish or export anything without asking.
skills.summary: The author had a Dot find footage, build the B-roll edit, add captions and arrange visuals over several review passes, working from his recorded narration.

skills.name: Edit and migrate Substack posts with a browser agent
skills.prompt: Open my Substack dashboard in this browser and do these tasks: [task 1: edit a live post, e.g. fix the headline of post X], [task 2: migrate a post from URL Y], [task 3: insert a note]. Keep formatting and links intact. Before you publish or save any change to a live post, pause and show me what will change. When finished, list each post you touched with its link.
skills.summary: The author gave Claude in Chrome three Substack tasks (live edit, post migration, note insertion), walked away, and returned to find all three published correctly.

skills.name: Edit existing video clips with plain-English instructions
skills.prompt: Edit my existing video clip [describe or attach clip] using these changes: [e.g. change the sky to sunset, remove the person on the left]. Keep the original lighting, camera angle, and motion. Give me the edited version plus a note on anything that did not turn out well, and offer one retry with adjusted instructions.
skills.summary: A creator tested Gemini Omni Flash over 36 hours, editing clips in place from typed instructions while preserving lighting and camera angle, with variable quality.

skills.name: Edit keynote videos with motion graphics using a video agent
skills.prompt: Edit my raw video at [path to video file] into a polished clip. Transcribe it, cut out mistakes and dead air without clipping any words, then add captions, simple motion graphics for key points, my branding from [logo or color details], and background music from [music folder]. Render a 16:9 version and a 9:16 version into [output folder], and stop once both play cleanly. Show me the cut list before you render the final files.
skills.summary: A marketer built a Claude Code video agent that cuts a keynote take without clipping words, adds motion graphics, captions, branding and music, and renders 16:9 and 9:16 versions.

skills.name: Edit raw footage by describing the video you want
skills.prompt: I have raw footage in [folder or Google Drive link]. Review it and produce an edit plan for a [length]-minute video about [topic and tone]: which clips to keep, the order, cuts, and suggested captions. Finished means a clear shot-by-shot list with timestamps I can follow in [my editing app]. Don't delete or change any original files.
skills.summary: Cardboard goes from raw footage to an edited video from natural-language instructions.

skills.name: Edit video through chat with subtitles and export
skills.prompt: I'll send you a video file and an editing request in chat, like [add Chinese subtitles and export as mp4]. Run it through [video editing tool or ffmpeg], then send back the finished file. Show me the planned edits first, and don't overwrite my original file.
skills.summary: A developer built an OpenClaw skill that sends chat requests like Chinese subtitles and mp4 export to a backend video editor and returns the result.

skills.name: Explore code to write technical documentation
skills.prompt: Explore the code in [path or module] and write technical documentation for [feature or API] aimed at [audience, e.g. new developers]. Cover what it does, how to set it up, the main functions or endpoints with examples, and common pitfalls, and mark anything you're unsure about so I can verify it. Save the result as [file name] and show me the draft before committing anything.
skills.summary: A technical writer uses Devin to explore code before documenting it, plus a Slack writing agent built on Devin, reporting about 20,000 lines of docs per month.

skills.name: Find trending articles and generate LinkedIn post variations
skills.prompt: Search Google for trending articles about [topic, e.g. eCommerce] from the past [week], pick the most relevant one and tell me why. Then open [post generator tool, e.g. EasyGen], pause so I can log in, and generate 10 LinkedIn post variations based on that article. Finish by listing all 10 in one place, and do not publish anything to LinkedIn.
skills.summary: A tutorial shows Operator searching Google for trending eCommerce articles, picking one, and using EasyGen to generate 10 LinkedIn post variations, pausing for the user to log in.

skills.name: Generate LEGO CAD models in LDraw with AI agents
skills.prompt: Write an LDraw file (.ldr) for a LEGO model of [object, e.g. a small red sports car] using real LDraw part numbers and colors, and place the parts so they connect properly. Then validate the file, render a preview image if you can, and fix any floating or overlapping parts. Finish by giving me the final .ldr file and a parts list.
skills.summary: A toolset and docs let ChatGPT and Claude agents write LDraw source files that become LEGO CAD models, packaged as a dockerized web app.

skills.name: Generate a daily podcast briefing from newsletters
skills.prompt: Every morning at [time], gather the newsletters I received in [email or Readwise source], pick the most important stories on [my topics], and write a [number]-minute podcast-style script. Save it to [folder] as a text file, and turn it into audio if a tool is connected. Tell me which steps worked and which didn't.
skills.summary: The author tested Cowork on a morning podcast from newsletters via Readwise and n8n MCP, plus video and 3D print design, noting what worked and what failed.

skills.name: Generate ads from a website URL
skills.prompt: Go to [my website URL] and learn my brand, product and audience. Then produce 5 ad concepts, written copy and a visual brief for each of 3 static ads, and 2 short UGC-style video scripts. Stop when you have a single document with all of it. Do not publish or submit anything to ad platforms.
skills.summary: Arcads agents take a website URL, learn the brand, and produce ad ideas, static ads and AI UGC videos.

skills.name: Generate an animated musical autonomously with Claude Code
skills.prompt: In a new folder, build a fully programmatic animated short musical about [premise], with the music, characters, and animation all generated by code and rendered to a video file. Start with a working first version of [one song and one scene], then keep improving it in rounds, such as better visuals, more songs, and cleaner code, committing to git after each round. Stop after [number] rounds or when I say so, and give me a summary of what changed and how to render the latest cut.
skills.summary: The author runs Claude Code with permissions skipped to autonomously generate and keep improving a fully programmatic animated musical, 500,000+ lines of code, rendering around the clock.

skills.name: Generate custom interactive HTML lessons for students
skills.prompt: Build me a single self-contained interactive HTML lesson file from this passage: [paste passage]. The students are at [level], and the vocabulary to cover is [word list]. The learning goals are [goals]. Include flip cards for the vocab, comprehension questions with instant feedback, and a short wrap-up. The job is finished when I can open the file in a browser and everything works. Save it as [filename].html and don't touch other files.
skills.summary: A teacher gives Claude Code a passage, level, vocab list and goals, and gets back a full lesson file with flip cards and comprehension questions, replacing hours of weekly worksheet work.

skills.name: Generate illustrations in a learned visual style
skills.prompt: Study the reference images in [folder] and describe the visual style in detail: colors, line work, composition, and mood. Save that description as a reusable skill, then use it to write prompts and generate [number] illustrations of [subjects] with [image generator]. Save the images to [folder] and stop when I have a set that matches the references.
skills.summary: A designer Hermes profile learns a style from reference designs, writes a skill for it, then crafts prompts and generates and saves images via Nano Banana.

skills.name: Generate live-coding music with Claude and perform it
skills.prompt: Write me a live-coding music piece in Strudel in the style of [describe genre, mood, tempo, and artists]. Use only sample names that exist in Strudel's default sample library and check each one rather than guessing. Then restructure it into sections I can trigger live, such as [intro, build, drop, outro], and save it as [filename] with a short note on how to perform it.
skills.summary: An author had Claude write Strudel music code from a style description, hand-fixed hallucinated sample names, then restructured it for live performance and recorded it.

skills.name: Generate long-form text content with Manus and Gemini Deep Research
skills.prompt: Research [topic] in depth using multiple reputable sources, then write a long-form [article, report, or guide] of about [word count] words for [audience] in a [tone] style. Include a source list and flag any claims you could not verify. Finished means a complete draft I can edit, with an outline up front.
skills.summary: A self-taught creator used Manus together with Gemini 2.5 Pro Deep Research for long-form text content generation work.

skills.name: Generate slide decks from titles and a branded template
skills.prompt: I will give you a list of slide titles and an uploaded PowerPoint template. Find the content for each slide and build the deck in my template, keeping its fonts, colors, and layouts. Finish with a PPTX I can edit, with sources in the speaker notes, and tell me anything that did not fit the template.
skills.summary: A reviewer had Manus find content for slide decks and produce a monthly marketing report in an uploaded PPTX template; editing tools were limited.

skills.name: Generate websites, a course and a 318-page ebook
skills.prompt: Create a [website, interactive course or ebook] about [topic] for [audience]. Plan the structure first and show it to me, then produce the full thing with [length or number of sections] and a consistent style. Finish with the files or a live link and a short list of anything you were unsure about or had to assume.
skills.summary: A newsletter author used Manus over three days to produce websites, interactive courses and a 318-page ebook from simple prompts.

skills.name: Guide a music video project from concept to deliverables
skills.prompt: Guide me step by step through making a music video about [concept]. Produce the lyrics, a Suno prompt, image prompts, video prompts, and YouTube title, description, and tags, asking me to approve each step before moving on. Finish with all deliverables collected in one document, and do not upload anything.
skills.summary: A Hermes agent walks a creator through an 8-step workflow producing lyrics, Suno prompts, image and video prompts, and YouTube metadata.

skills.name: Index a newsletter archive and repurpose writing
skills.prompt: Index all the writing in [folder path of newsletter archive or notes vault] so you can answer questions about it. Then give me a short audit of recurring themes and any gaps, and turn [essay filename] into a newsletter draft file and a thread draft file in [output folder]. Don't edit or delete any of my original files; stop when the two drafts and the audit are saved.
skills.summary: Per the guide, Casey Newton used Claude Code to index 818 newsletter editions in under 30 minutes, and writers audit note vaults and turn essays into newsletter and thread files.

skills.name: Keep a personal website's content updated automatically
skills.prompt: Look at my personal website repo at [path or URL] and set up automation so its content ([blog, projects, or reading list]) updates from [source such as Notion, GitHub, or RSS]. Use an MCP server if it helps. Finished means one command refreshes the content and shows me a diff of the changes, and nothing gets deployed or committed until I approve.
skills.summary: A developer's setup for automating their site's content with agents and MCP.

skills.name: Let AI agents design in Figma
skills.prompt: Using a Figma CLI tool such as figma-use, create a [type of design, e.g. pricing page layout] in my Figma file [file link] with frames, text, and reusable components for [button, card, etc.]. Follow this style: [colors, fonts, spacing]. Finish when the layout and components exist on a new page and describe what you made. Do not modify or delete my existing pages.
skills.summary: A CLI that lets coding agents create shapes, text, frames and components in Figma, so agents can build layouts and component systems.

skills.name: Make a music video from a reference
skills.prompt: Make a music video using my song [audio file], the lyric timing data [file], these images [folder], and this reference video for style [link or file]. Add transitions and text effects that follow the lyric timing. Finish with a rendered video file and tell me what you'd tweak if I want a second version.
skills.summary: Given a song, lyric timing data, images and a reference video, Grok Bot produced a music video with transitions and text effects in minutes of hands-on time.

skills.name: Make an AI trends presentation
skills.prompt: Make a [number, e.g. 12]-slide presentation on [topic, e.g. AI trends for 2026] for [audience]. Research current sources first, then vary the slide layouts so it does not look repetitive, using charts or images where useful. Finish with an exported deck and a list of the sources used.
skills.summary: The author had Manus 1.6 Lite build a 2026 AI trends deck; research was deep but generation took over 10 minutes and slides were monotonous.

skills.name: Make music videos, portfolio sites and sorting scripts
skills.prompt: I have [number] AI-generated images and videos in [folder or location]. Write and run a script that sorts them into folders by [criteria such as theme, date, or style] and renames them consistently. Show me a preview of the planned moves before changing any files, and finish with a report of what ended up in each folder.
skills.summary: A creator used Grok Bot for a full music video, a prompt engine, portfolio site code, scripts to sort 158 AI images and videos, and a career page.

skills.name: Orchestrate video generation from the command line
skills.prompt: Using command-line tools, generate [number] short Grok Imagine clips for [video concept], then assemble them in order into one video with background music and simple effects. Keep the clips and the final file in [folder]. Stop when the final video plays start to finish, and tell me the command to rerun it with different clips.
skills.summary: Grok was connected to an agent via CLI to generate Imagine clips, assemble the video and add music and effects.

skills.name: Plan article topics and draft web articles
skills.prompt: I write web articles about [topic area]. Using my past articles in [folder or list of URLs], build a table of [15] new topic ideas with a target keyword, search intent, and a note on any overlap with what I've already published. Once I pick a topic, draft the article in my style, and keep a notes file of corrections I make so future drafts improve. Stop after the topic table and wait for my pick.
skills.summary: A web writer uses Cowork for keyword selection, building a topic table that checks overlap with past articles, and drafting articles that learn from corrections.

skills.name: Post a rendered video to Slack when integration fails
skills.prompt: Read the feedback in the Slack thread [channel or thread link], make the requested edits to my video project at [project path], and re-render it to [output file]. Then use computer use to open Slack, click Add file, and attach the new render to the same thread. Before posting, show me the final file name, the destination channel, and the message text, and wait for my approval.
skills.summary: Codex read Slack feedback, edited and re-rendered a video, then used Computer Use to click Add file and post it in Slack.

skills.name: Produce a finished music release from one chat
skills.prompt: Help me make a short music release about [theme or mood] in the style of [genre]. Write the lyrics, generate the song with my connected music tool, create cover art, and make a 10-second video clip to go with it. Save all the files in one folder and list what you made. Do not publish or upload anything anywhere. Show me the results and wait for my feedback.
skills.summary: Claude Code wrote lyrics, generated and mastered the song, made cover art and a 10-second video via an MCP connector in about 6 minutes; clip joined with ffmpeg outside.

skills.name: Produce a full video with an agent assistant
skills.prompt: Help me make a [length]-long video about [topic or story] in Grok Imagine. Suggest three concept ideas first, then once I pick one, organize the shot list, generate the clips, and assemble them into a finished video. Stop when you have one complete video file and tell me what you would tweak next.
skills.summary: Grok Imagine's agent mode suggested ideas, organized and assisted through making a full video in one hour.

skills.name: Produce a short-form video from research to captions
skills.prompt: Make a vertical short-form video about [topic]. Research it using reliable sources, write a 45-second script, generate visuals, build motion graphics, add a voiceover, background music, and captions. Show me the script for approval before you generate assets, and finish by saving the video to [folder].
skills.summary: Hermes Agent researched a JWST topic, wrote the script, generated assets, built Remotion motion graphics, added voiceover, music and captions for a vertical video.

skills.name: Produce a track in Ableton Live by talking
skills.prompt: Help me connect an MCP server for [Ableton Live or my music software] so you can control it from chat. Then create a [genre] track of about [length] with [instruments or mood], adding the drums, bass, and melody and doing a basic mix. Stop when the song plays through start to finish, and tell me what you changed before deleting or overwriting any existing project files.
skills.summary: An MCP server that lets Codex drive Ableton Live, used to write and mix a full song from chat messages.

skills.name: Produce cinematic video with three custom agents
skills.prompt: Act as a three-part production team for a cinematic short about [story idea]. First, write the visual prompts shot by shot. Second, write the audio script with narration, sound design, and music cues. Third, write a character sheet with fixed details for [character names], so they look the same in every shot. Give me all three as a numbered shot list for [number] shots.
skills.summary: The poster built a cinematic studio in Grok Imagine using three custom agents for prompt direction, audio scripting and character-consistent video.

skills.name: Produce short WeChat videos with OpenClaw agents
skills.prompt: Act as my short-video producer for [platform, e.g. WeChat Channels]. Suggest 5 topics in my niche of [niche], and once I pick one, write a [length, e.g. 60-second] narration script in my voice. Generate the voiceover with [my TTS or cloned voice setup] and render a video with Remotion using [visual style]. Send me the finished file in Telegram and do not publish anything until I confirm.
skills.summary: A creator uses OpenClaw agents with Remotion and a cloned voice to suggest topics, write narration, generate TTS and render videos, confirming in Telegram in about 15 minutes.

skills.name: Prototype a promo video and design work with bots
skills.prompt: I need a prototype of an animated promo for [product or launch]. Based on this description of the animation [paste spec or notes], build a small interactive playground I can click through and list any design tasks you'd handle in [Figma]. You're done when I can preview the prototype and see a short list of next steps.
skills.summary: An xAI designer used bots to prototype an animated promo, build a playground from the animation spec, and handle Figma and prototype tasks.

skills.name: Publish AI-written blog posts from trending news to WordPress
skills.prompt: Build an n8n workflow that pulls news from [RSS feeds about my topic], skips any story already covered by checking a log sheet, and writes an original article with SEO title, meta description and a featured image that adds [my own angle or opinion] rather than a generic rewrite. Save it as a WordPress draft, not published, and log it. Finish when one test article appears as a draft for me to review.
skills.summary: An n8n pipeline turns RSS news into AI articles with SEO metadata and images, publishes to WordPress and logs them; the author notes generic content and duplicates as problems.

skills.name: Publish a daily YouTube video and route form leads automatically
skills.prompt: Set up a Make scenario with two parts. First, every day at [time], use Gemini to come up with a video idea about [topic], write a title and description, and put them in [Google Sheet or Doc] for my review. Second, when someone submits my Google Form [form name], add them to [CRM or sheet] and draft a follow-up email. Pause and show me the draft video details and follow-up emails before anything is published or sent.
skills.summary: Reviewers use Make workflows with Gemini to generate ideas, create and title a daily YouTube video, and route Google Form responses into a CRM with follow-ups.

skills.name: Publish free game giveaway posts automatically
skills.prompt: Build an n8n workflow that runs every [day/week], checks [Epic Games Store, Prime Gaming, Steam] for newly free games, and collects each game's title, description, image and store link. Have it create a WordPress post for each game as a [draft/scheduled] post on [my WordPress site]. Don't publish anything live until you've shown me a sample post and I've approved it. The job is done when one test run produces a correct draft for each current giveaway.
skills.summary: n8n workflows track free games on Epic, Prime Gaming and Steam, then create and publish WordPress posts with details, images and store links.

skills.name: Rebuild a math curriculum into a one-year plan with materials
skills.prompt: Here is my current [grade level] math curriculum: [paste or attach files]. Restructure it into a one-year plan of [number] weeks, and create for each unit a worksheet, a short test, and a game or activity, plus a week-by-week schedule. Put everything in [folder] and build a simple website to browse it. You're done when every unit has its materials and the schedule covers the full year.
skills.summary: Claude restructured an accelerated math curriculum into one year, writing tests, games, worksheets, a schedule, and a hosted site integrated with a teacher planner.

skills.name: Recreate a video ad as a JavaScript animation
skills.prompt: I have a video file at [path to ad video]. Use ffmpeg to analyze its frames and audio, then recreate it as a pure JavaScript animation in a single HTML file, keeping the original audio track in sync. Work on your own and compare against the original as you go. Stop when I can open the HTML file in a browser and it matches the video's look and timing, and do not upload or publish anything.
skills.summary: The author had Claude recreate a downloaded ad video as a pure JavaScript animation with the original audio, working autonomously with ffmpeg in under an hour.

skills.name: Repurpose a newsletter into social content
skills.prompt: Take my finished newsletter at [paste text or link] and turn it into a carousel outline, a short reel script, a LinkedIn post and a Substack note, each matching my usual voice. Organize the outputs into a Notion page or folder so I can review and edit before anything goes out. Stop once all four formats and the hub page are ready for my review.
skills.summary: One Cowork prompt turns a finished newsletter into a carousel, reel script, LinkedIn post and Substack note; it also built a Notion hub.

skills.name: Research newsletter ideas into a Notion backlog
skills.prompt: Research this newsletter idea: [your idea]. Look across YouTube, the web, and X for what people are already saying, the best sources, and gaps I could cover. Add a new entry to my Notion content backlog at [Notion database name] with a summary, links, and a suggested angle. Stop once the entry is saved and show me the link.
skills.summary: A Content Researcher Bot researches an idea across YouTube, the web via Tavily and X, and adds findings to the author's Notion content backlog.

skills.name: Run a creative workflow from brainstorm to video
skills.prompt: Take my idea for [topic or project] through a full creative workflow: brainstorm five angles, write a short script for the one I choose, generate the images, and edit them into a [length] video. Check in with me after the brainstorm and after the script before moving on. Stop when I have a finished video I can post.
skills.summary: Grok's Agent Mode handles brainstorming, writing, image generation, editing and video production in one place.

skills.name: Run content creation with specialized bots
skills.prompt: Act as my content team for [YouTube channel or newsletter on topic]. First research [5 outlier videos or top posts in my niche] and tell me what made them work, then draft [a script or issue] and an edit pass based on that. Give me a proposed schedule and don't publish or send anything until I approve it.
skills.summary: Creators use bots to study outlier YouTube videos, and run newsletters with research, drafting, editing and scheduling bots; one experiment made 44 thumbnail proposals.

skills.name: Schedule 60 short videos in YouTube Studio
skills.prompt: Open YouTube Studio in my logged-in browser and schedule these [number] short videos from [folder or list] to publish one at a time starting [date] at [time], with [number] per day. Use the titles and descriptions from [file or list], and set the audience and visibility as [settings]. Before you confirm the first schedule, show me the plan, and report any video that failed to upload or schedule.
skills.summary: Claude via the Chrome extension scheduled 60 generated short videos in YouTube Studio after suggesting the task itself.

skills.name: Script Shorts, post X threads and repurpose content
skills.prompt: I create content about [topic] for [audience]. Take this source material [link or pasted text] and turn it into a 45-second YouTube Shorts script, a thread of [number] posts for X, and [number] other repurposed pieces. Put everything in one document with a suggested posting order for the next [number] days. Show me everything before posting anything.
skills.summary: An agent scripts YouTube Shorts, posts X threads and repurposes content so the creator avoids touching a content calendar.

skills.name: Take a video from thumbnail to published with promo posts
skills.prompt: I have a finished video at [file path] about [topic]. Propose a thumbnail design in Figma, write a YouTube title, description and tags, and draft promo posts for [platforms such as X, Bluesky and LinkedIn]. Show me everything before uploading the video or scheduling any posts, and wait for my approval.
skills.summary: Cowork proposes a Figma thumbnail, uploads the video to YouTube with metadata, and drafts and schedules X, Bluesky and LinkedIn promo posts.

skills.name: Turn AI newsletters into a daily podcast
skills.prompt: Every night at [time], collect the newsletters in my [Gmail label or folder, e.g. AI Newsletters] from the past 24 hours and pull out the key stories. Turn them into a [10-minute] podcast script with a conversational tone, then produce the audio and save it to [folder or podcast app] so it is ready for my morning walk. You are done when the episode file exists and you have sent me a short list of the stories covered.
skills.summary: An agent runs overnight, collects the author's AI newsletter subscriptions and produces a daily podcast to listen to on walks.

skills.name: Turn PDFs and textbooks into interactive courses
skills.prompt: Read the PDF or textbook at [file path] and turn it into an interactive course for [audience]. Plan the lesson structure, then for each lesson write the content and add quizzes, flashcards or exercises. Review the full course for accuracy against the source and consistency. Finish with the course as [format, e.g. HTML files] in [folder].
skills.summary: Hassan's agent parses source documents, plans lesson structure via tool calls, picks interactive components, and a Lesson Reviewer agent checks the final course.

skills.name: Turn a Telegram message into researched, designed social posts
skills.prompt: Build me an n8n workflow that starts when I send a message to my Telegram bot with a topic. It should research the topic on the web, write a post for [platforms, e.g. LinkedIn and X] in [my brand voice], and generate a matching image. Before anything is published, send me the drafts back in Telegram and wait for my approval; the job is done when an approved post goes live on my accounts.
skills.summary: An n8n agent takes a Telegram message, researches the topic, designs the posts and publishes them to social media.

skills.name: Turn a blog post into an animated infographic
skills.prompt: Using Canvas, turn this blog post into an animated infographic coded in HTML: [paste post or link]. Use my brand colors [hex codes] and write for [audience]. Highlight the [5] key points with simple animations. Finish when I can preview it in Canvas, and tell me how to export or embed it.
skills.summary: A content creator fed a blog post into Gemini Canvas, which produced a coded animated infographic using brand colors and audience details from the chat thread.

skills.name: Turn a keyword into approved Instagram content
skills.prompt: Build a scenario that takes a keyword from [Google Sheet or form] and uses AI to write an Instagram caption and image idea for [my brand and tone]. Email the draft to [my email] for approval, and log each keyword, draft and approval status in Google Sheets. Don't publish anything to Instagram until I approve, and show me the first draft to review.
skills.summary: A Make.com pipeline takes a keyword, generates AI content, sends it for email approval, and logs it to Google Sheets.

skills.name: Turn a week of GitHub activity into a blog post
skills.prompt: Build a weekly workflow that pulls my commits and pull requests from [GitHub repo or username] for the past 7 days, has one step summarize the changes, a second draft a blog post in [tone], and a third format it for [Notion and DEV]. Save the output as a draft in Notion. Finished means I can review a draft each week, and the workflow must pause for my approval before publishing anything publicly.
skills.summary: A three-agent pipeline that drafts weekly posts from commit history and publishes to Notion and DEV.

skills.name: Turn ideas into finished videos
skills.prompt: Turn this idea into a finished video: [describe idea, audience, and length]. Generate the footage, add motion, write and record a voiceover in [tone of voice], and edit everything together. Finish with one exported video and a short note on what you'd change in a second version.
skills.summary: Grok Bot acts as a video production assistant that generates and edits video, adds motion and voiceovers, and finishes content.

skills.name: Turn newsletters into branded LinkedIn carousels
skills.prompt: Build me a reusable skill that takes a newsletter URL or pasted text and turns it into a 5 to 10 slide LinkedIn carousel as HTML and CSS. Use my brand colors [hex codes], font [font name], and a tone that's [tone description]. Finish by generating one carousel from [newsletter URL] and saving the slides as files I can open and export.
skills.summary: A newsletter writer built a Claude Code skill that converts a newsletter URL or text into 5-10 slide HTML/CSS carousels in under 5 minutes.

skills.name: Turn videos and company research into slide decks
skills.prompt: Watch this video [YouTube URL] and turn it into a [number, e.g. 10]-slide deck that captures the key points, with a slide for any data or quotes worth keeping. Finish with an exported presentation and a short list of timestamps for the main claims.
skills.summary: The author describes Manus watching a YouTube video to make a slide deck and researching companies for investment potential into a presentation.

skills.name: Upload content to a company YouTube channel
skills.prompt: Help me upload videos to our company YouTube channel [channel name]. The videos are in [folder or link], and the titles, descriptions and tags are in [file]. Prepare each upload as a private draft with the right metadata and thumbnail, then give me a list of what's ready. Don't publish anything, change channel settings, or sign in in a way that may look suspicious; if there's any login or verification prompt, stop and ask me.
skills.summary: A user gave Grok Bot access to the company YouTube channel to help upload, but Google suspended the account for suspicious activity.

skills.name: Write a beginner book on programming with AI
skills.prompt: Write a beginner-friendly book on [topic] of about [number] chapters, each with a short explanation, an example and a practice exercise. Give me the outline first for approval, then the full manuscript as a single document. Finish with a list of claims I should fact-check before publishing.
skills.summary: A blogger used Manus free credits to write a book on programming with AI for beginners and plans to publish it on Amazon.

skills.name: Write a novel chapter by chapter with a subagent
skills.prompt: I'm writing a [genre] novel called [title]. My outline is in [outline file path] and my chapters so far are in [folder]. Create a reusable /write-chapter subagent that reads the outline and all earlier chapters, then writes the next chapter in my established voice at about [word count] words and saves it as [filename pattern]. Start by writing just chapter [number], and stop there so I can review it before you do any more.
skills.summary: A author had a custom /write-chapter Claude Code subagent read outlines and prior text, then write and save 10 chapters in 17 minutes.

skills.name: Write a weekly AI marketing newsletter automatically
skills.prompt: Every [day and time], research the past week's top news in [my topic or industry] and draft a newsletter in my voice, using [link to a past issue] as a style example. Also create [three] social posts to go with it. Save everything to [Airtable or Google Docs] and email me the drafts. Don't publish or send to subscribers; stop once the drafts are in my inbox.
skills.summary: A scheduled Lindy agent researches the week's news, drafts the newsletter plus social posts and scripts, stores them in Airtable and emails the result.

skills.name: Write and send AI newsletters automatically
skills.prompt: Build me an n8n workflow that runs every [day/week], finds a trending topic in [niche, e.g. AI] from [sources], and uses Gemini to write a newsletter in this voice: [tone description]. Format it as clean HTML and prepare it to send to my subscriber list in [email tool or sheet]. Before the send step is enabled, pause and show me the full draft and recipient count so I can approve it.
skills.summary: An n8n agent finds a trending AI topic, writes a newsletter with Gemini, formats it and emails it to subscribers without manual work.

skills.name: Write, design and post social content from a Google Sheet
skills.prompt: Build a scenario that reads rows from my Google Sheet [sheet link] containing post topics, writes captions in [brand voice] using OpenAI, creates an image for each, and queues them in Buffer for [platforms]. Mark each row as done once it's queued. Run it on one test row and show me the caption, image and scheduled time before anything is posted publicly.
skills.summary: An automation built with Make, OpenAI, Cloudinary and Buffer writes captions, designs content and posts it across social platforms from a sheet.

skills.name: Add 61 kid-friendly mini-games to an app
skills.prompt: I have a game collection app called [app name] with [current number] games. Add [number] new kid-friendly mini-games for ages [age range]: no ads, no in-app purchases, no violence, and no external links. Build them one at a time, test that each one loads and plays, and stop when they are all in the collection and listed on the home screen with a short description.
skills.summary: Two users had Replit Agent autonomously add 61 child-friendly, ad-free mini-games to their game vault, growing it from 40 to 101.

skills.name: Add a battle-of-Alesia expansion to a 1990s game remake
skills.prompt: I have the source for my remake of [classic game] in [project path]. Add an expansion scenario based on [historical battle, e.g. the Battle of Alesia] using this research brief: [paste notes]. Implement the map, units, and win conditions, then let me playtest and iterate on my feedback until I say it's done. Keep changes on a separate branch.
skills.summary: Nate Combs used ChatGPT for research and a prompt, and Claude Code implemented the expansion, iterating on his playtest feedback.

skills.name: Build Godot games with paired design and coding agents
skills.prompt: Help me build a small Godot game: [describe game idea]. First write a short design doc and a prioritized task list in the project folder at [path]. Then implement the tasks one at a time in GDScript, run the project to check it works, and commit each finished task to git. Stop after [number] tasks and summarize what to playtest.
skills.summary: Cowork handles design docs, task queues and playtests while Claude Code writes GDScript and runs Godot and git.

skills.name: Build a 2D platformer game without coding
skills.prompt: I have no coding experience. Build me a 2D platformer in a single HTML file with a [art style, e.g. black-and-white] look and [core mechanic, e.g. waves of enemies to fight]. Use simple controls like [keys], explain how to open it in my browser, and keep improving it based on my feedback. You're finished when I can play a full level from start to finish.
skills.summary: A content creator with no coding experience used Claude Code to build a black-and-white wave-combat platformer in HTML canvas and played it live.

skills.name: Build a 3D browser game in 24 hours
skills.prompt: Build me a 3D browser game using Three.js where [describe gameplay, e.g. I fly a spaceship through an asteroid field]. Get a playable core loop with controls, a score and a restart option working first, then improve visuals. You're done when I can play it in the preview from start to game over, with no local setup needed.
skills.summary: A developer used Replit's agent to build a 3D browser game entirely in the browser with no local setup.

skills.name: Build a Rust game engine with spawned agents
skills.prompt: Spawn separate agents to build a game engine in [Rust] with [scripting language] scripting, multi-threading and [weather, lighting, hot reloading]. Give each agent one subsystem, have them integrate their work, and make sure the whole thing compiles and runs a demo scene. Stop when the demo scene runs and report which features work and which are incomplete.
skills.summary: OnXStephen had Grok Bot spawn agents that built a Rust game engine with .NET scripting, multi-threading, weather, lighting, and hot reloading.

skills.name: Build a browser 4X strategy game with LLM coding help
skills.prompt: Help me build a browser-based [game genre] game called [game name] in [HTML/JS or framework]. Start with [first system, e.g. map generation, combat engine, or fog of war], write it in small testable pieces, and run it so I can try it. skills.prompt: Act as my work assistant for this week's tasks: [list tasks such as schedule a meeting with X, triage my inbox, find flights and hotels to [city] for [dates]]. For each task, finish the prep and show me the result. Pause and show me details before sending any invite or email, or booking or paying for anything.
skills.summary: Authors use Cowork or Claude Code to schedule invites, triage email, book flights and hotels, pull Airtable data and scrape exhibitor lists.

skills.name: Delegate tab-juggling work to ChatGPT Agent's virtual computer
skills.prompt: I need to [task that normally means copying between tabs, e.g. pull data from several sites into one spreadsheet]. Use these sources: [links or sites] and put the result in [format]. Work through it on your own and finish with the completed file plus notes on anything you couldn't get. Pause before logging in, sending, submitting, or purchasing anything.
skills.summary: After a week of testing, the poster used ChatGPT Agent's virtual computer to avoid copy-pasting between tabs and came back to finished work.

skills.name: Delegate to-do items to AI agents
skills.prompt: Set up a task inbox where I can assign you to-do items like [example tasks]. For each task, mark it in progress, do the work, and return it to a review list with the result and any questions. Don't send messages, spend money, or delete anything until I approve it from the review list.

skills.name: Deliver scheduled article digests to Telegram with OpenClaw cron jobs
skills.prompt: My scheduled job that sends [N] article digests to [Telegram] at [time] runs but nothing arrives. Check the cron job settings and logs, find why delivery fails (try turning thinking mode off), and fix it. Finish by running it once so the digest actually shows up in Telegram, and ask before changing other jobs.
skills.summary: A developer fixed OpenClaw cron jobs that ran without delivering by turning thinking mode off, after which six articles reached Telegram in 30 seconds.

skills.name: Design product labels and produce SDS sheets
skills.prompt: I sell [product type] and need print-ready label designs for [product names], using my brand colors [colors] and logo [attach file]. Also fold in these customer testimonials [paste or attach] to produce an updated marketing file, and draft Safety Data Sheets for [products] using the ingredient details I attach. Deliver everything as downloadable files and flag any safety or regulatory information I should verify before use.
skills.summary: A seller used Manus to design product labels, turn customer testimonials into an updated file, and create SDS sheets.

skills.name: Draft and send an email through Gmail
skills.prompt: Draft an email in Gmail to [recipient] about [topic], in plain text with no markdown symbols, in a [tone] tone. Save it as a draft and show me the full text. Do not send it until I tell you to.

skills.name: Draft email replies and LinkedIn posts with n8n workflows
skills.prompt: Build me an n8n workflow that watches my Gmail for new emails matching [label or sender], drafts a reply in my tone using [short tone description], and saves it as a draft for me to approve. Add a second branch that extracts any tasks from the email into [Google Tasks or Notion database]. You're done when a test email produces both a draft and a task. Never send an email automatically; leave everything as a draft.
skills.summary: The author built n8n workflows that draft Gmail replies for approval, generate LinkedIn posts from a topic, and extract tasks from emails into Google Tasks or Notion.

skills.name: Draft email replies and add calendar invites
skills.prompt: Every [weekday morning or schedule], check my Gmail for new emails that need a reply and draft responses in my voice, using [a sample of my writing or tone notes]. If an email mentions a meeting or event, add it to my Google Calendar as an invite for [time zone]. You're done when drafts are saved and events added; do not send any email, and tell me about each calendar event you added.
skills.summary: A writer built a scheduled Claude agent using Gmail and Calendar connectors to draft replies and add invites to the calendar.

skills.name: Draft follow-up emails automatically when no reply arrives
skills.prompt: Build a flow that watches my sent emails in [Gmail or Outlook] for messages to [type of recipient, e.g. clients or prospects]. If there's no reply after [number] business days, draft a short, polite follow-up in my voice that references the original message, and save it as a draft in my inbox. Never send anything automatically; show me the first draft and the flow setup before you turn it on.
skills.summary: A user set up a Lindy flow that watches sent emails, waits for a reply, and drafts a follow-up if none comes.

skills.name: Draft lesson plans and school paperwork for teachers
skills.prompt: I teach [subject] to [grade/year level]. Using the curriculum notes in [folder or description], draft a lesson plan for [topic] lasting [duration], plus a short slide outline, a reflection template, and a parent-facing note about the upcoming assessment. Save each as its own document in [folder] and stop when all four are done for my review.
skills.summary: A teacher used ChatGPT for lesson plans, reflections, PowerPoints, assessment notifications, and marking, saving hours of planning.

skills.name: Draft parent-teacher communications
skills.prompt: I'm a [grade/subject] teacher. Draft parent emails for these situations: [e.g. progress update, behavior concern, upcoming event], using a [warm/professional] tone and the details in [notes or file]. Save each draft in [folder] and do not send anything; show me the drafts so I can edit and send them myself.
skills.summary: A teacher says ChatGPT handled all their parent-teacher communications for a month, and they also tried it for lesson planning.

skills.name: Draft replies to podcast listener emails and log story ideas
skills.prompt: Create a Zapier Agent that watches [my Gmail label or address] for emails that arrive from [my website contact form]. For each one, draft a reply in a [warm and concise] tone and save it as a Gmail draft, and add the original message as a new entry in my [Notion database of story ideas]. Never send an email automatically; leave every reply as a draft for me to review. You're done when a test email gets both a draft reply and a Notion entry.
skills.summary: Blake Oliver's Zapier Central agent watches Gmail for contact-form emails, drafts replies, and copies each original into a Notion database of story ideas.

skills.name: Draft transactional documents with Claude in Word
skills.prompt: I'm drafting a [type of transactional document, e.g. purchase agreement] in Word. Using the term sheet and notes I've pasted below, draft the [section names], follow the defined terms and style in [precedent document], and flag any open points or assumptions in brackets. Finish with a clean draft I can review, plus a short list of questions you need answered. [paste terms and precedent]
skills.summary: The poster used Claude inside Word and coworking tools to handle the drafting grunt work of transactional documents.

skills.name: Drive desktop apps with an agent to move files
skills.prompt: Using the desktop app [app name], move the files in [source folder] to [destination folder]. After each step, check the result, for example by listing the destination folder, rather than trusting the app's own success message. If a dialog or modal appears that you didn't expect, stop and tell me what it says. At the end, report how many files you moved and how many you verified in the destination, and ask me before deleting anything.
skills.summary: A poster describes months of driving desktop agents against real apps; in one task the agent misread a modal and kept reporting success while moving nothing.

skills.name: Email a weekly digest of payment notification emails
skills.prompt: Build an n8n workflow that every Sunday reads emails under Gmail label [payment notifications] from the past week, has AI pull the top three takeaways from each, and compiles them into one digest. Send the digest to [my email]. It's finished when a test run produces a digest from the last week's labeled emails.
skills.summary: An n8n AI workflow reads labeled payment emails in Gmail, pulls the top three takeaways from each and sends a Sunday digest.

skills.name: Email daily ClickUp digests to stakeholders
skills.prompt: Build a scenario that runs every day at [time] and pulls tasks from my ClickUp [space or list] that are [due soon, changed, or blocked]. Format them into a clean email digest and send it to [stakeholder emails] who don't have ClickUp accounts. Send a test digest to me first and don't send it to stakeholders until I approve.
skills.summary: A Make.com scenario sends a daily email digest from ClickUp to stakeholders without ClickUp accounts, and adds contacts to a selected action item.

skills.name: Email scheduled project summaries with Codex
skills.prompt: Create a scheduled automation that runs every [day and time], reads the files in [project folder], and writes a short weekly summary of progress, open issues, and next steps. Email it to [recipient address] using my Gmail plugin. Before the first send, show me the draft and the schedule so I can approve them.
skills.summary: A guide sets up a Codex automation that reads project files on a schedule and emails a weekly summary via the Gmail plugin.

skills.name: Enrich and store contacts in a personal CRM
skills.prompt: I'm going to give you a person's name and LinkedIn URL: [name] and [LinkedIn URL]. Enrich the profile using my connected enrichment tool, then save a record to the [contacts table name] table in my connected database with name, company, role, location, and profile link. Show me the record before you write it, and stop once it's saved and you've confirmed the row exists.
skills.summary: Claude, connected to Supabase via MCP, takes a name and LinkedIn URL, enriches the profile through Harmonic, and writes the record to a personal CRM database.

skills.name: Evaluate hiring candidates against competency levels
skills.prompt: I'm attaching our competency framework with definitions and levels for [role or job family]. For each candidate in [folder or file of interview notes and résumés], assess evidence against each competency and suggest a level with quotes from the notes. Flag gaps where there's not enough evidence. Finish with a comparison table and a short summary per candidate, treating it as input for my decision and not a final call.
skills.summary: A commenter built a basic hiring agent loaded with competency definitions and levels for HR evaluation work.

skills.name: Extract RFQ and BOQ requirements into Excel
skills.prompt: Read the RFQ and BOQ documents in [folder path], including their attachments, and extract every requirement into an Excel file. Use columns for item number, description, quantity, unit, specifications, deadline, and source file with page or section. When done, list anything ambiguous or missing for me to review. Do not edit the original files.
skills.summary: A commenter uses Cowork at work to read RFQs and BOQs with attachments and pull the requirements into an Excel file; another used it to clean folders.

skills.name: Extract action items from Teams and schedule meetings
skills.prompt: Go through my Teams threads in [channels or tenants] from the last [time period] and list the action items assigned to me, with who asked and when. Find any buried request for a meeting with [person or topic], check both our calendars for a good slot, and show me the proposed invite. Wait for my OK before sending the invite or confirmation.
skills.summary: An early Scout user had it summarize Teams threads across tenants, find a buried meeting request, check calendars, schedule it and send confirmation.

skills.name: Extract expenses from receipt photos sent via chat
skills.prompt: Build a workflow that triggers when I send a receipt photo to my [Telegram/Discord] bot. It should extract vendor, amount, tax, category, and date, then append a row to my [Google Sheet name]. Test it with [3] sample receipts and show me the rows it created. Flag any receipt it cannot read clearly instead of guessing.
skills.summary: A bookkeeping assistant for freelancers and small businesses reads receipt photos sent through Telegram or Discord and extracts vendor, amount, tax, category and date.

skills.name: Extract invoice data and file it into a bookkeeping sheet
skills.prompt: Build a self-hosted n8n workflow where I upload receipts or invoices to [folder or form], and OpenAI extracts vendor, date, totals, tax and invoice number. Show me the extracted data for review, then on approval file the original in [Drive folder] and append a row to my [year] bookkeeping sheet. It's done when a sample invoice flows through; do not file or write anything until I approve.
skills.summary: A self-hosted n8n workflow extracts accounting data from uploaded receipts and invoices with OpenAI, then after user review files the originals and appends data to a yearly sheet.

skills.name: Extract purchasing-card receipt data into a report cover sheet
skills.prompt: I have purchasing-card receipts as PDFs in [folder path]. Extract vendor, date, amount and the business purpose from each one, and fill a cover sheet in the format of [template file or describe columns]. Process the files one at a time and save results to an outputs folder so progress isn't lost. List any receipts that couldn't be read.
