skills.name: Extract supplier invoice PDFs into a monday.com board
skills.prompt: Build a Make scenario that watches my Google Drive folder [folder name] for new supplier invoice PDFs and extracts supplier, invoice number, date, line items, and total using AI extraction. Create one item per invoice on my monday.com board [board name], mapping fields to columns [column names], and flag any PDF with missing or unclear fields for my review. Test with [number] sample PDFs and show me the results before enabling it.
skills.summary: A Make workflow watches a Google Drive folder for supplier invoice PDFs, extracts data with AI Extractors, and writes it into monday.com.

skills.name: Extract vendor PDFs and create QuickBooks invoices

skills.name: File roofing permits and inspection forms online

Pause and show me everything before you submit any form or send any email, and stop when each one has been submitted or sent with my approval.

skills.name: Fill out 50 forms from public information

skills.name: Hand a one-person business to AI agents for a week

skills.name: Handle a client project across Gmail, Calendar and Notion
skills.prompt: Connect to my Gmail, Google Calendar and Notion and help me manage the project for [client name]. Find the overlapping meetings about [project] this week and propose how to merge them, draft the invites, and compile a summary of the research on [topic] into a Notion page. Show me the merged meeting plan and invite drafts before sending or changing anything; you're done when the Notion page exists and I've approved the calendar changes.

skills.name: Handle a personal mailbox daily with a local model
skills.prompt: Set up a daily job that runs at [time, e.g. 7am] and goes through my personal mailbox at [email provider/account], using my local model through [Ollama model name]. Sort new messages into [categories, e.g. needs reply, newsletters, receipts, junk], and write me a short digest of what needs my attention along with draft replies for anything urgent. skills.name: Handle executive admin: email drafts, bookkeeper questions, insurance forms
skills.prompt: Handle these admin tasks from my inbox and files: decline the invitation from [sender/event], draft an email to [lawyer name] about [topic], answer the bookkeeper's questions from [bookkeeper name] using [documents like lease or budget], and fill in the [insurance broker] form using the same documents. Show me every draft and the completed form before anything is sent or submitted, and list which documents you used for each answer. You're done when each task has a draft or filled form waiting for my approval.

skills.name: Handle incoming emails with automatic triggers

skills.summary: Grok Bots watch incoming email, summarize, research, draft replies, extract invoice details, flag urgent items and complete next steps with connected tools.

skills.name: Handle office-day tasks and social posting

Also prepare [number] social posts for [Reddit community/Instagram account] about [topic]. Before you send any email, create any meeting, or publish any post, show me the exact content and wait for my approval.
skills.summary: A user has Grok Bot post on Reddit and Instagram, check email and set Teams meetings.

skills.name: Handle pharmacy refill calls with a voice agent
skills.prompt: Set up a voice agent for [pharmacy name] that answers refill calls, verifies the caller using [name, date of birth, phone number], and looks up the prescription in [system]. Hand off to a human for [conditions, e.g. controlled substances or unclear identity], and send me a daily summary of calls handled.

skills.name: Handle post-meeting follow-ups automatically

Before sending any Slack message or creating any calendar invite, pause and show me exactly what you are about to send.
skills.summary: A demo agent finds the meeting transcript, extracts action items, messages teammates on Slack, and schedules the next meeting by checking calendars.

skills.name: Handle routine email tasks and follow-up reminders with a personal assistant
skills.prompt: Build an n8n personal assistant for my email at [email address] that sorts incoming mail, drafts replies for [routine types, e.g. scheduling, receipts, simple questions], and tracks emails where I'm waiting on someone. Have it save drafts only and never send any email without showing me the text first; you're done when it handles a week of sample emails correctly.
skills.summary: Author built an n8n personal assistant that handles about 70% of routine email tasks and sends reminders for tasks waiting on others, after fixing early quirks.

skills.name: Have Claude implement most of a day job's work

Finish with a checklist of the remaining steps I should handle myself.

skills.name: Interview candidates based on their resume

skills.name: Investigate and unblock stuck task cards

skills.name: Learn personal scripts from a tools folder
skills.prompt: Read the scripts in my folder [folder path] and write a plain-language summary of what each one does, such as email, CRM, research, or drafting. skills.summary: Claude Cowork read a folder of personal scripts for email, CRM, research and drafting, added them to memory, and carried the capabilities to a new interface.

skills.name: Let Claude Code drive your logged-in Chrome browser
skills.prompt: Using the Claude in Chrome extension, open my logged-in Chrome and do this task: [describe the task, e.g. find the latest invoice in [site name] and download it]. skills.name: Turn trip receipts into an expense report and triage files
skills.prompt: I have receipts from [trip or period] in [folder path]. Read each one, extract date, vendor, amount and category, and build an expense report spreadsheet with totals by category. Flag any receipts that are unreadable or missing details. Do not submit the report anywhere, just save it for my review.
skills.summary: The author used Cowork to build an expense report from 47 receipts, pick what to read from 4,992 files and make slide decks via Gamma.

skills.name: Turn voice notes into Linear tickets and review analytics
skills.prompt: Create a reusable skill that takes a voice note transcript I paste in and turns it into a formatted ticket for [Linear/Jira] with title, description, acceptance criteria, and priority using this template: [template]. Show me the drafted tickets for approval before creating anything in [project name]. Once that works, add a weekly routine that reviews [analytics source, e.g. YouTube analytics] and sends me a summary of what changed.
skills.summary: The author built Codex skills that convert voice notes into formatted Linear tickets, review YouTube analytics weekly, and run nightly self-improvement automations.

skills.name: Use AI as an internal recruiting assistant
skills.prompt: I'm a recruiter working on a [role] search for [client type]. Here are the candidate's resume and my notes: [paste]. Summarize the candidate in a structured profile (experience, key skills, achievements, gaps, compensation and availability if known), draft a concise client submission, and write a short client update email on the search's progress. Finish with 5 questions I should ask in the next meeting; don't send anything, just give me drafts to review.
skills.summary: Recruiting teams use AI to summarize profiles, prepare submissions, draft client updates and structure candidate information before meetings.

skills.name: Use Claude Code in a commercial real estate business
skills.prompt: I run a [type of business, e.g. commercial real estate development and syndication] business and keep my files in this folder: [folder path]. Look through them and pick one repetitive task such as [e.g. summarizing deal packages, building investor update drafts, or extracting rent roll data into a spreadsheet]. Build a script or workflow that does it, run it on one sample file, and show me the result and how to rerun it. Ask me before you modify or delete any of my existing files.
skills.summary: A commercial real estate developer and syndicator says Claude Code changed the game for their business workflow, with few specifics given.

skills.name: Validate invoices against inventory and create purchase orders
skills.prompt: Build me an n8n workflow that triggers when a new invoice arrives at [email inbox or folder], extracts the vendor, line items and quantities, and checks them against my inventory in [Google Sheets link]. If items are low or match a reorder rule, create a purchase order in [ERP or tool] and notify [purchasing contact] on [Slack or email]. Send anything it can't match to a review list instead of acting on it, and pause to show me the purchase order it is about to create before you enable the live version.
skills.summary: An n8n workflow built for a client matches invoice data to a Google Sheets inventory, creates ERP purchase orders and notifies purchasing; about 90% of invoices are handled automatically.

skills.name: Write and review contracts with ChatGPT
skills.prompt: I need a first draft of a [contract type, e.g. freelance services agreement] between [party A] and [party B] for [short description of the work, term, and payment]. Write it in plain, clear language, then review your own draft and flag any clauses that are vague, one-sided, or commonly disputed. Finish with a short list of questions I should answer or have a lawyer check before signing.
skills.summary: The poster used ChatGPT to draft and review contracts and was impressed with the results.

skills.name: Write end-of-sprint changelogs from completed tickets
skills.prompt: Read the tickets completed in [Linear project or team] during [sprint dates]. Pick the changes customers would care about, skip internal chores, and draft a changelog in plain language. Finished means one draft in [email or in-app] format plus a short note on why you left certain tickets out. Show me the draft before sending or posting anything.
skills.summary: A PM has Claude Cowork read completed Linear tickets, pick what matters, draft the update and suggest email or in-app format, replacing about an hour per sprint.

skills.name: Analyze 170k LLM logs overnight
skills.prompt: I have [number] log entries in [file or database path] that I want analyzed overnight. Using [tool, e.g. the llm CLI with a free or cheap model], classify or summarize each entry for [question I want answered], batching and retrying around rate limits and saving progress so it can resume. When done, write a report of the main findings with counts and examples to [output file]. Don't delete or modify the original logs.
skills.summary: A user left a Gemini agent running overnight to analyze 170k LLM logs with the llm CLI and a free model, and it finished the job despite limits.

skills.name: Automate a weekly arXiv paper triage
skills.prompt: Set up a weekly automation that searches arXiv for new papers matching [keywords or topics], logs them to a CSV with title, authors, date, link, and one-line summary, and sorts each into keep, skim, or drop based on [my research interests]. Stop when the CSV is updated and give me the keep list. Don't delete past entries.
skills.summary: A weekly Codex automation searches arXiv for keywords, logs new papers to a CSV, sorts them into keep/skim/drop buckets and can check claims against Zotero.

skills.name: Build a personal research wiki from papers and articles
skills.prompt: Read the sources in [folder of papers and articles] on [topic] and build a wiki of interlinked markdown pages in [wiki folder]: one page per [concept / paper / person], each with a summary and links to related pages. Add an index page. Finish when every source is covered and links resolve, and ask me before overwriting any existing file.
skills.summary: Cursor Agent writes and maintains interlinked markdown pages from user-supplied sources, summarizing and cross-referencing, with Obsidian used to browse.

skills.name: Build a student survey form with Manus
skills.prompt: Create a Google Form survey for [target group] about their views on [topic], with [number] questions mixing multiple choice and short answer. Give me the shareable link and the editing link when done. Don't fill in or submit any responses yourself, and don't send the form to anyone without showing me first.
skills.summary: Manus built a Google Form survey on undergraduates' views of AGI; the author hit a snag when asking it to fill the survey with synthesized student responses.

skills.name: Build data analysis reports and dashboards with a coding agent
skills.prompt: Help me build a data analysis report from [my data warehouse or data files, e.g. a Postgres database or a folder of CSVs]. First define a simple semantic layer in files, with the key tables, metrics and joins for [my business area]. Then query the data, answer [my main question], and publish a dashboard or report with charts as files in this folder. Stop when I can open the report and each chart lists the query behind it, and ask me before running anything that writes to the database.
skills.summary: A toolkit gives a coding agent a semantic layer and dashboard files so it can query data warehouses and publish in-depth reports and visualizations.

skills.name: Build data pipelines and analysis for a research paper
skills.prompt: Help me build the data pipeline and analysis for my research project on [topic]. The raw data is in [folder or file], and I want to [cleaning, merging, and statistical tests or models]. Write clean, documented scripts, run them, and save the outputs and figures to [output folder] with a README explaining each step so I can check the results. Ask me before deleting or overwriting any existing files.
skills.summary: A researcher used Claude Code as the main agent to build data pipelines and do the data analysis for a paper, generating over 98% of the code.

skills.name: Build searchable knowledge bases from videos and papers
skills.prompt: Set up two Markdown knowledge bases for me, one for videos and one for papers. When I send a [YouTube link or paper PDF/URL], summarize it in [200-300] words with key takeaways, save it as a .md file in the right folder, and update an index file listing title, date, and tags. Confirm each save with the file path, and ask before deleting or overwriting any existing file.
skills.summary: An OpenClaw agent runs a YouTube summariser and a paper-condensing tool, saving Markdown into two indexed knowledge bases for videos and papers.

skills.name: Catalog and summarize papers dropped into Drive
skills.prompt: Build an n8n workflow that triggers when a new PDF lands in my [Google Drive folder], extracts the title, authors, year and abstract, finds 3-5 related papers on Semantic Scholar and PubMed, and builds an APA citation. Log everything in a Google Sheet and create a Notion page with a plain-language summary and the related papers. Done when one test PDF produces a sheet row and a Notion page, which you show me.
skills.summary: An n8n workflow extracts metadata from new PDFs, finds related papers on Semantic Scholar and PubMed, builds an APA citation, logs to Sheets and creates a Notion summary.

skills.name: Collate WHO data into a multi-tab spreadsheet
skills.prompt: Go to [data source website, e.g. WHO data portal] and pull the latest figures on [indicator] for [list of countries]. Build a spreadsheet with tabs organized by indicator, country and trend over time, with source links and the date of each data point. Finish when it's complete, and list any pages you couldn't access because of logins or dynamic content.
skills.summary: Testers had ChatGPT Agent navigate the WHO site, extract the latest data and organise it by indicator, country and trend; it often fails on logins or dynamic pages.

skills.name: Collect financial data on 100 independent schools
skills.prompt: For each of these [type of organization, e.g. independent schools] in [region], collect [data points, e.g. tuition, endowment, revenue] from their public websites and filings: [list or source]. Put results in a spreadsheet with a source link per row and mark any missing values. Start with the first [25] and stop there so I can check quality before you continue.
skills.summary: A writer had Operator gather financial data for independent schools in the background; it was slow and was stopped after about 25 schools, then the data went to o1 for analysis.

skills.name: Collect international grant listings into Airtable
skills.prompt: Create an agent that searches the web each [week] for open grants for [type of organization or project] from [list of countries], and adds each one to my Airtable base [base name] with fields for name, funder, country, deadline, amount, eligibility, and link. Skip any grant already in the table and leave unknown fields blank rather than guessing. It's finished when a test run adds at least [number] new, accurate rows and I've reviewed them.
skills.summary: A user has a Zapier agent scrape the web for grants from different countries and upload them to Airtable, and is still tuning it.

skills.name: Compile a daily digest of Reddit AI tool chatter
skills.prompt: Every day at [time], search Reddit ([subreddits]) for conversations about new [AI tools or topic]. Compile the most popular topics with short summaries and links, and append them to [document] under today's date. Finish when the document is updated, and message me only if nothing new was found.
skills.summary: A Lindy agent searches Reddit for conversations about new AI tools, compiles popular topics and updates a document daily.

skills.name: Compile an annotated bibliography and draft a paper
skills.prompt: Search academic databases for recent open-access empirical papers on [research topic] published since [year]. Group them by [field or theme], write an annotated bibliography with a two-sentence summary each, list the research gaps you notice, then assemble a rough draft outline of a paper. Finish with a document containing the bibliography, gaps and draft, with links to every source.
skills.summary: ChatGPT Agent searched academic databases for recent open-access empirical papers, grouped them by field, wrote an annotated bibliography, noted research gaps and assembled a draft.

skills.name: Compile genealogy research into a spreadsheet and plan
skills.prompt: Take my genealogy notes from [file, link or pasted notes] on [family name or branch] and compile them into a spreadsheet with columns for name, birth, death, location, relationships and source. Then write a short research plan listing gaps and the next records to look for. Finish when the spreadsheet and plan are ready to download.
skills.summary: A commenter had ChatGPT build a spreadsheet for her genealogy research, and agent mode was recommended for compiling and formatting findings into a usable document.

skills.name: Compile journalist lists and search apartment listings
skills.prompt: Build me a list of [number] [reporters/contacts] who cover [topic] at [type of outlet], with name, outlet, recent relevant article, and contact info where it's public. Include only people you can verify, and mark any gaps clearly instead of guessing. Deliver it as a spreadsheet and stop when you have [number] complete entries or have run out of reliable sources.
skills.summary: A reporter tested Manus on building a reporter list, searching NYC rentals and finding award candidates; results were thin at first, and a three-hour search yielded only three full profiles.

skills.name: Compile recent LLM research papers into a Word doc
skills.prompt: Find the most important papers on [research topic] from the last [number] months. For each, give the title, authors, link and a two-sentence summary of why it matters. Compile everything into a Word document titled [title] and tell me where it was saved.
skills.summary: Comet found major LLM/agent training papers from six months with links and analysis, then saved them to a Word doc via Outlook.

skills.name: Do equity research with Claude Code without coding
skills.prompt: In my folder [path] of plain-text notes, research [company or ticker] by reading my existing notes, then pull key facts from [filings or sources I'll provide]. Write a new note with the business model, recent results, risks, and open questions, and link it to related notes. You're done when the note is saved as a new file; do not edit or delete my existing notes without showing me the changes first.
skills.summary: A non-engineer keeps research in a folder of plain-text files managed with Obsidian and uses Claude Code for equity research.

skills.name: Draft a dissertation lit review from uploaded sources
skills.prompt: I'm writing a literature review on [your topic] for my [dissertation or paper]. I'll upload [number] sources. Draft a structured review of about [word count] words grouped by theme, citing only the uploaded sources in [citation style], and mark any claim you cannot support from them instead of guessing. Finish with a list of gaps in the literature and any sources you could not use.
skills.summary: A doctoral writer used NotebookLM, which cites only uploaded sources, to handle citations and draft a literature review without invented references.

skills.name: Draft research by gathering many web sources
skills.prompt: Research [topic or question] by gathering information from at least [number, e.g. 15] web sources, including pages with data in images or tables. Write a structured summary with headings and a source list with URLs. Stop when you have covered [specific subtopics], and note which sources were thin or conflicting.
skills.summary: A G2 reviewer uses Manus to scrape sites, read images and gather many sources into a summary in the background, but says credits run out fast.

skills.name: Email a daily AI news brief and build slide decks from tabs
skills.prompt: Every morning, search for the latest news on [topic, e.g. AI], pick the top 5 stories, and write a short brief with a two-sentence summary and source link for each. Show me the draft email before sending it to [my email address]. Then, once I confirm, send it.
skills.summary: Comet searches the day's AI news, picks the top 5 stories and emails a brief, and merges tagged tabs and reports into a cited Google Slides deck.

skills.name: Extract CRM pricing and ratings into a spreadsheet
skills.prompt: Visit the websites of the top [number, e.g. 15] [product category, e.g. CRM] tools and build a spreadsheet with pricing tiers, free plan limits, and [review site, e.g. G2] rating for each. Include the source URL per row and mark any cell you could not confirm. Stop when every tool has a row, and tell me which ones failed.
skills.summary: A reviewer had Manus visit the top 15 CRM sites and pull pricing tiers, free plan limits and G2 ratings into a spreadsheet; long tasks were unreliable.

skills.name: Fetch and analyze economic data for research
skills.prompt: I'm researching [economic question, e.g. how homeownership rates changed by age group]. Find the right public data from [source, e.g. Census Bureau or SEC filings], download it, clean it, and store it in a DuckDB database in this folder. Then produce a chart and a short written summary of what the data shows, with the source links and any gaps or caveats noted. Stop when the chart, database and summary are saved.
skills.summary: An economist used Claude Code to find Census homeownership data, clean it and chart it, and to scrape SEC 10-K risk factors into a DuckDB database showing tariff-risk changes.

skills.name: Find Reddit threads on reader pain points
skills.prompt: I write a newsletter about [topic] for [audience]. Search Reddit for threads where people describe frustrations, questions, or unmet needs related to [topic], and collect [15] of the most useful ones. For each, give the link, a one-line summary of the pain point, and a standout quote, then group them by theme. Stop when you have the list and don't post or reply to anything.
skills.summary: A newsletter writer had Comet find Reddit threads on reader pain points, finding extra sources in about 15 minutes without intervention.

skills.name: Find connections across 100 non-fiction books
skills.prompt: I have a folder of about [number] non-fiction books as [epub/pdf/txt] files at [folder path]. Index them so you can search across them, then find connections between books on the theme of [topic or question]. Give me 5 trails of related excerpts, each with the book title, the quote, and one sentence on how it links to the next, and stop once I have those 5 trails.
skills.summary: Claude Code browses a personal library with CLI tools and surfaces trails of related excerpts across books.

skills.name: Find public data and build a business dashboard
skills.prompt: Find public data sources relevant to [my business or industry], such as [specific metrics], and download what you can into a folder called [folder name]. Then build a simple dashboard prototype from that data showing [key metrics]. You're done when I can open the dashboard locally and a README lists each data source and its URL.
skills.summary: A commenter used Claude Code to prototype a business dashboard and to gather public data into a folder instead of searching manually.

skills.name: Gather three years of meeting minutes into text files
skills.prompt: Go to [website where our meeting minutes are posted] and collect the minutes for [meeting body] from [start year] to [end year]. Save each one as a separate text file named with its date in [folder], and give me a list of any meetings you couldn't find or read. Work in batches of [20] and tell me when each batch is done so I can check it.
skills.summary: Jeff Adams used the Claude Chrome extension to collect meeting minutes into text files and load them into a notebook, taking 3-4 hours over three sessions.

skills.name: Generate deep research reports into Notion
skills.prompt: Build an n8n workflow that takes a research topic [topic] and runs up to three web searches with Tavily. An AI agent should then compile the findings into a Markdown report with headings, key findings and source links, and save it as a new page in my Notion [parent page or database]. You're done when one test topic produces a finished Notion page; confirm the Notion destination with me before it writes anything.
skills.summary: An n8n workflow turns a topic into up to three Tavily searches, compiles a Markdown report with an agent, and pushes it to a Notion page.

skills.name: Generate personalized literature reviews from a one-line topic
skills.prompt: Build me a reusable skill that takes a one-line topic like [example topic] and writes a literature review. It should find real papers, write the review in [language], and cite them in [citation style, e.g. APA or GB/T 7714] with a DOI or URL for every reference. Export it as Markdown, Word and PDF, and drop any reference you can't verify. Test it on [topic] and stop when all three files are saved.
skills.summary: A researcher built a literature-review Skill for an agent framework that outputs Markdown, Word and PDF reviews with GB/T 7714 references carrying DOIs or URLs, used by their team.

skills.name: Generate updated research reports on followed companies
skills.prompt: Build me a small research agent that, for each company on my list [tickers], pulls the latest filings, news, and price data from [sources] and writes an updated report in [folder]. Each report should cover what changed since the last one, key numbers, and risks. You're done when I can run one command to refresh all reports; test it on [two tickers] and show me the output first.
skills.summary: The poster built and open-sourced a custom stock-research agent that produces updated reports on companies they follow.

skills.name: Give a coding agent a paper corpus to find new techniques
skills.prompt: Before each attempt at improving [my project/benchmark], search the paper collection at [path or search tool] for techniques relevant to [problem], and note which paper inspired any idea you try. Then implement and test the idea against the current baseline score of [score]. Keep a log of ideas tried, source papers, and results, and stop after [number] experiments with a summary of what helped.
skills.summary: Poster gave a Claude Code agent access to about 2M papers to search before each attempt; it found techniques it otherwise wouldn't know and beat a baseline agent.

skills.name: Grade Cursor on a real data science project
skills.prompt: I have a data science project in [folder path] about [goal]. Try these tasks and grade yourself on each: [pandas transformations / data cleaning / web scraping / prototyping a model]. For each, tell me what worked, what you were unsure about, and what I should verify by hand. Finish with a short scorecard, and do not overwrite my raw data files.
skills.summary: A data scientist tested Cursor on a real project: weak on pandas, data cleansing and scraping, strong at prototyping.

skills.name: Have Claude collect names from a Wikipedia page into a file
skills.prompt: Open [browser] and go to the Wikipedia page for [topic]. Find every person's name mentioned on the page and save them, one per line with no duplicates, to a text file called [filename] in [folder]. Then tell me how many names you found and stop.
skills.summary: The poster tried Claude Computer Use to open Firefox, search Wikipedia, find all names on a page and save them to a text file.

skills.name: Investigate papers overnight with a bot research team
skills.prompt: Overnight, find new papers published this week on [research topic] from [sources such as arXiv or journals]. For each of the top [number], extract the main claims and note whether the methods look sound. Have my brief waiting for me by [time], with links to every source and a note on anything you could not verify.
skills.summary: Grok Bot roles read new papers and extract claims, rerun analyses, and scan sources, working overnight to produce briefs.

skills.name: Let Cursor maintain an Obsidian notes vault
skills.prompt: Open my Obsidian vault at [path] and review its structure. Suggest [5] useful connections between notes and folders I could reorganize, and answer this question using my notes: [question]. Then write a daily note in [folder] summarizing what was done today. Propose any file moves or deletions first and wait for my approval.
skills.summary: Cursor reviews vault structure, suggests connections, answers questions about notes and writes a daily done note documenting other agent sessions.

skills.name: Link journal entries and write book reviews in Obsidian
skills.prompt: Work in my Obsidian vault at [folder path]. For each journal entry in [folder or date range], add backlinks to related notes and create entity notes for people, places, and ideas that recur. Also, when I paste a brain dump about a book, turn it into a review using my template at [template path]. Show me a sample of your edits on three entries before doing the rest.
skills.summary: The author uses Claude Code in their Obsidian vault to add backlinks and entity notes to journal entries and to turn brain dumps into formatted book reviews.

skills.name: Look up and summarize web content from a browser extension
skills.prompt: On the page I'm viewing, look up the text or image I've selected and give me a short explanation with [number] trustworthy sources. Then summarize the whole article in [number] bullet points, noting the main claim and any weak spots. Finished means I get both the lookup and the summary in the side panel, and you do not click away or submit anything without asking.
skills.summary: A commenter built an agentic browser extension using Gemini that handles lookups on selected text or images and summarizes articles on a webpage.

skills.name: Measure how long jobs stay open at tech companies
skills.prompt: For each of these companies: [company names], look at their careers pages and sample about [25] open roles. Find out how long each role has been posted and report what share are older than [60] days. Give me a table per company and one sentence on what the numbers suggest. Stop once every company has a sample, and note any company where posting dates were not available.
skills.summary: An agent read 25 open jobs each at five companies and measured how long each had been posted, e.g. 21 of 25 at Figma were 60+ days old.

skills.name: Mine Reddit threads into structured Notion reports
skills.prompt: Build me an n8n workflow that takes a Reddit thread or search URL from [trigger, e.g. form or chat message], scrapes the posts and comments with [scraping service], and uses Gemini to extract the main concerns, recurring themes, and notable quotes. Write one structured report per run into my Notion database [database name] with fields for [fields, e.g. topic, themes, concerns, source URL]. Test it on [example Reddit URL] and show me the resulting Notion page before activating it.
skills.summary: An n8n workflow scrapes Reddit posts and comments via Bright Data, extracts concerns and themes with Gemini, and writes reports to Notion.

skills.name: Monitor public documents for changes affecting teaching materials
skills.prompt: Every [week] check these public documents for changes: [list of links, e.g. standards, syllabi, regulations]. Sort the changes by how much they affect my teaching materials on [topic], and check that the notation in [my article or handout] still matches the linked pages. Give me a ranked list of revision candidates with the passage and source link; only suggest, do not edit my files.
skills.summary: An educator's Dot checks public documents for changes, sorts them by impact, and verifies an article's notation against linked pages, offering revision candidates only.

skills.name: Monitor tech subreddits and competitors, draft emails and articles
skills.prompt: Every morning, scan [subreddits or sites] for posts relevant to [my work, product, or competitors], and summarize the top [5] items with links. Then draft [an email or short article] on the most important one for [audience]. Finished means one digest plus one draft saved in [folder]. Show me the drafts before sending or publishing anything.
skills.summary: Commenters use Cowork daily to scan Reddit tech subreddits for work items, monitor competitors and markets, generate articles and draft emails.

skills.name: Orchestrate academic research and writing workflows
skills.prompt: Act as the orchestrator for my research project on [topic] in this folder. Read my notes and sources in [folder path], then break the work into steps: summarize each source, build an outline, and draft sections of my [paper or thesis] in [LaTeX or Markdown], keeping citations tied to real files in the folder. Stop when a full first draft and a to-do list of open questions are saved, and ask me before deleting or overwriting any existing file.
skills.summary: Researchers use Claude Code as an orchestrator for research workflows and as their main tool for writing papers and theses in LaTeX or Markdown.

skills.name: Orchestrate the full research loop with parallel agents
skills.prompt: I want to run a small research project on [research question or topic]. Split the work across parallel sub-agents: one surveying existing literature, one proposing hypotheses, one running analysis or experiments on [data or sources I can provide], and one drafting the write-up. Finish with a short report that cites its sources, lists what was tested and what was found, and flags weak points, and show me the plan before you start.
skills.summary: Sakana's Agentic Scientist uses a scaffold of parallel agents to run the whole research loop, rather than one agent writing a paper.

skills.name: Produce a sourced research document with parallel agents
skills.prompt: Produce a thoroughly sourced research document on [topic or question] for [audience]. Split the work across several parallel agents to search and read sources, have them challenge each other's findings, then merge everything into one document with citations and a short executive summary. Stop when the document is complete and tell me how many sources you used and which claims are weakest.
skills.summary: Grok coordinated 16 specialized agents that searched and parsed 896 sources, debated and peer reviewed, and delivered a complete research document in one minute.

skills.name: Produce cited research briefs with simulated peer review
skills.prompt: Research [topic] and write a cited brief of about [length]. Search academic papers and the web, synthesize the main findings, then critique your own draft as a skeptical peer reviewer and fix the weak points. Verify every citation actually exists and supports its claim; you're done when I have the brief with a reference list and a note on any claims you couldn't verify.
skills.summary: Feynman multi-agent system searches papers and the web, synthesizes findings, runs simulated peer review, verifies citations, and outputs a cited brief.

skills.name: Query 600 GB of Hacker News, arXiv, and LessWrong in plain English
skills.prompt: I want to explore [public dataset or index, e.g. Hacker News, arXiv posts] using plain-English questions. Connect to [read-only index or database URL], write the SQL or vector queries needed, and answer this: [your question, e.g. what are people saying about X over the last year]. Show me the queries you ran along with a short summary of results. If I ask for email alerts, show me the alert setup and wait for my approval before turning anything on.
skills.summary: Claude Code writes the SQL and vector queries against a public read-only index, and can set email alerts for nuanced criteria.

skills.name: Query session records and build talk slides with Claude Code
skills.prompt: I have a database of recorded work sessions at [path to database]. Explore its structure, then answer these questions: [e.g. commit counts per week, a timeline of the project, the biggest changes]. Then build a slide deck for a [length]-minute talk to [audience] on [topic] using those findings. You're done when I have the numbers with a note on how you computed them, plus a slide file I can open. Don't modify the database.
skills.summary: A CS instructor used Claude Code to query his recorded session database for commit stats and timelines and to build slides for a faculty talk.

skills.name: Research AI training case studies and build a summary deck
skills.prompt: Research case studies on [topic, e.g. AI training programs] from major consulting firms and reputable sources like [firm names]. Build a slide deck summarizing [number] case studies with results, lessons and source links. Finish when the deck is ready, and check that images and text don't overlap before you hand it over.
skills.summary: A team had Agent Mode research case studies from McKinsey, PwC and similar firms and make a slide deck in 32 minutes, with some image and overlapping text issues.

skills.name: Research Reddit customer pain points with a skill
skills.prompt: Research customer pain points about [topic or product category] on Reddit. Find relevant subreddits, check they're active and on-topic, collect quotes with links as evidence, cluster the complaints into themes, and note any signs people would pay for a solution. Save the findings as a report in [file path], ranking the themes by strength of evidence.
skills.summary: The author replaced a Reddit research agent with a Codex skill that finds pain points, verifies communities, collects evidence, clusters problems, and analyzes commercial signals.

skills.name: Research US stablecoin adoption with an agent
skills.prompt: Run deep research on [topic, e.g. stablecoin adoption in the US in 2026]. Cover [key angles such as usage numbers, regulation, major players, and risks], use recent and credible sources, and cite each one. skills.name: Track daily arXiv papers into a Notion database
skills.prompt: Build an n8n workflow that runs every day at [time], fetches new arXiv papers matching the keyword [keyword], summarizes each in 2-3 sentences with an AI model, and adds them to my Notion database [database name] with title, authors, link and summary. Then send me one email digest listing the new papers. You're done when a test run adds the latest papers without duplicates; pause and show me the email before the first send.
skills.summary: An n8n workflow fetches arXiv papers daily for a keyword, summarizes them with Gemini 2.5 Flash, writes them to Notion and sends Feishu and Gmail notifications.

skills.name: Try Devin on research tasks (mostly failed)
skills.prompt: Research [author or topic] by finding their [number] most recent papers and writing a one-paragraph summary of each, with links to the sources. Then give me a short overview of the main themes across them. If a page can't be read, tell me which one and why instead of guessing, and stop once you have a cited summary I can check.
skills.summary: Answer.AI had Devin fetch an author's recent papers and research transcript summarization; it got stuck parsing HTML and returned generic results, rated a failure.

skills.name: Turn YouTube videos into cited research notes
skills.prompt: Take these YouTube video links [list of URLs] on [topic] and turn them into research notes in my Obsidian vault at [folder path]. For each video, write a summary with citations back to timestamps, then add a note linking the shared concepts across videos and a set of flashcards. Finish when every video has a note and the flashcards are saved in one file.
skills.summary: The author uses Claude Code with NotebookLM and Obsidian to turn 20 videos into cited notes, audio overviews, a knowledge graph and flashcards.

skills.name: Turn any URL into a structured Notion note
skills.prompt: Build an n8n workflow that starts from a webhook or form where I submit a [URL]. It should fetch the page, strip it down to readable text, ask an AI model to produce a title, a 3-sentence summary, key points and 3 tags, then create a new note in my Notion database [database name] with those fields. You're done when a test URL I submit produces a correctly filled Notion note; show me the draft workflow before you activate it.
skills.summary: An n8n workflow fetches a submitted URL, strips it to readable content, has OpenAI summarise it into structured fields, and saves a Notion note.

skills.name: Turn voice notes into structured Obsidian notes
skills.prompt: When I send a voice note to [Telegram chat], transcribe it and create a note in my Obsidian vault at [vault path] with the transcript, a cleaned-up version of the argument, links to related existing notes, and a short draft of [blog post or message]. Reply with the note title and path. Never delete or overwrite existing notes; create new ones only.
skills.summary: Voice notes sent over Telegram become Obsidian thought notes with transcript, cleaned argument, linked context and a draft; Hermes also tracks recipes.

skills.name: Tutor you through pen-and-paper math with a local agent
skills.prompt: Set up a local math tutor for me in this folder. Write a TUTOR.md brief telling you to teach [topic, e.g. algebra or calculus] at [my level] by giving me one problem at a time to work out on paper, then asking me to type or describe my answer and steps, and giving hints before solutions. The setup is done when I can start a session, receive a first problem, and get feedback on my attempt. Don't delete or overwrite any existing files without showing me first.
skills.summary: An open-sourced tutor app runs Codex locally with a TUTOR.md brief to teach math with pen and paper using the user's subscription credits.

skills.name: Use Claude Code as an agentic tutor in your learning environment
skills.prompt: Act as my tutor for [subject, e.g. Rust or linear algebra] inside this project folder. First write a CLAUDE.md that says: explain concepts at [my level], ask me questions before giving answers, and use the files, notebooks and exercises in this folder as teaching material. Then read the folder and start with a short lesson on [first topic] followed by one exercise for me. Don't change or delete my files without asking me first.
skills.summary: The author gave Claude Code a tutor role with a CLAUDE.md brief so it could explain concepts and interact with his learning environment.

skills.name: Use Cursor for academic paper writing with citations
skills.prompt: I am writing a paper on [topic] in markdown at [file path]. Use my bibtex file [path] to pick and insert citations in [citation style] where my claims need support, and flag any claim that has no matching reference. Then check that the document converts to Word with pandoc. Finish when the paper builds cleanly, and do not invent references that are not in my bibtex file.
skills.summary: Forum users write papers in markdown with Zotero citations and a bibtex file for Cursor to pick references from, converting to Word with pandoc.

skills.name: Use a persistent assistant for student research and daily tasks
skills.prompt: Act as my ongoing research assistant for [my field or course]. Keep notes on my topics, sources, and deadlines so each new chat picks up where the last one left off, and start by summarizing what you know about [current project]. Connect to my email only for reading, and before sending any message or deleting anything, show me exactly what you plan to do.
skills.summary: A student used a named dot for ongoing research and daily tasks with persistent context across chats, set up for email.

skills.name: Accelerate scientific research with Codex
skills.prompt: I'm researching [scientific question or topic]. Using the data and code in [folder path], reproduce [analysis or result], then run [next experiment or analysis] and summarize the findings with plots saved to [output folder]. Keep a log of assumptions and anything you couldn't verify. You're done when the scripts run end to end and I have a short write-up of the results and open questions.
skills.summary: A researcher uses Codex and ChatGPT extensively for scientific research, getting a week's work done in a day, though recent usage limits reduced output.

skills.name: Control and calibrate a robotic hand with OpenClaw
skills.prompt: Connect to my [robot hand/servo device] over [USB/serial port] and learn its joint list from [docs or config file]. Move each joint through a small safe range, check the result with my camera at [camera device], and note the calibration offsets for any joint that is off. Report progress to me in [Telegram/chat app], and ask me before sending any movement outside the safe range of [limits].
skills.summary: An OpenClaw agent running Claude drove a 16-joint printed hand, checked its actions with a USB camera, calibrated firmware and narrated in Telegram.

skills.name: Control robots with generated code and voice commands
skills.prompt: Help me build a simulated robot arm controller in [simulator or language]. Use a vision model to detect objects in [image or camera feed], then write code that calls my robot API [API description] to [task, e.g. pack items into a box]. Run it in simulation only, and show me the generated code before anything is run on real hardware. Stop when the task succeeds in simulation three times in a row.
skills.summary: Gemini detects objects and writes robot API code, and with 10 in-context demos an ALOHA robot packed boxes and folded a dress; voice commands became robot plans.

skills.name: Debug low-level cryptography code
skills.prompt: I have a failing test in my cryptography code at [path], where [describe the symptom, e.g. wrong output for certain inputs]. Investigate why it fails, compare against [reference implementation or test vectors], and propose a fix. Finished means the tests pass and you've explained the root cause, and you should show me the diff before changing any files.
skills.summary: Cryptography engineer Filippo Valsorda's write-up on Claude Code debugging low-level crypto.

skills.name: Design and build a robotic arm with no CAD experience
skills.prompt: Help me design a [N]-DOF robotic arm from scratch using FreeCAD via MCP, including part files ready for 3D printing and a servo control script, even though I have no CAD experience. Guide me through printing, assembly, and wiring, stopping to confirm before any step that involves ordering parts.
skills.summary: A builder used Claude Code with FreeCAD and Claude Vision to design, print, and assemble a 5-DOF servo arm with vision and voice control.

skills.name: Discover room-temperature magnetic semiconductor candidates with agents
skills.prompt: I want to find candidate room-temperature magnetic semiconductors for [application or material family, e.g. spintronics, oxide or 2D materials]. Search the recent literature and open databases such as Materials Project, then shortlist two candidates with their reported Curie temperature, band gap and the evidence for each. Finish with a short report that cites every source and flags which claims are computed versus experimentally measured.
skills.summary: Opus 5.5 agents were used to identify two candidate room-temperature magnetic semiconductors, per the post's headline.

skills.name: Drive a 7-axis robot arm with natural language
skills.prompt: I have a [robot arm model] with an SDK at [SDK docs link or path]. Read the docs and write a skill file with the safety rules: [joint limits, speed cap, workspace bounds]. Then, when I ask for a movement in plain language, write a Python script to do it and show me the script before running it on the arm. Finish when you can complete [simple test move, e.g. move to home position and back] safely.
skills.summary: OpenClaw is taught a skill and rules for the NERO arm, then writes and runs Python control scripts from plain-language movement requests.

skills.name: Explore open math problems with a multi-agent system
skills.prompt: Research the open math problem [name or description of problem] and survey what is currently known, including recent partial results. Then propose three promising approaches, try a small computational experiment for at least one of them, and report what you found. Finish with a summary that separates verified results from guesses, with links to your sources.
skills.summary: A paper on autonomous mathematical discovery in an open-world multi-agent environment.

skills.name: Find a Linux vulnerability hidden for 23 years
skills.prompt: In my local checkout of [open-source project or kernel subsystem] at [path], review the code in [directory or module] for memory-safety or logic bugs that could be security vulnerabilities. For each suspected issue, give the file, line, why it's a problem, and how to confirm it safely in a test environment. Finished means a ranked list of findings, and don't make changes or report anything publicly without asking me.
skills.summary: An account of Claude Code uncovering a long-standing vulnerability in Linux.

skills.name: Find exploitable bugs in smart contracts
skills.prompt: Audit the smart contract in [path or repo] for exploitable bugs such as reentrancy, access control, and arithmetic errors. Test each suspected bug only on a local fork or test network and write a short report with how to reproduce it and how to fix it. Finished means a ranked findings list, and never touch a live mainnet or send any transaction without my explicit approval.
skills.summary: Anthropic's red team reports agents finding $4.6M worth of blockchain smart contract exploits.

skills.name: Find security flaws in open-source software
skills.prompt: Clone [open-source repository URL] and review its [language] code for likely security flaws such as memory safety bugs, injection, unsafe input parsing, and hardcoded secrets. Write up each finding in a file with the file path, a short explanation, and how severe you think it is. Do not change any code or open any issues or pull requests. Stop once you have a ranked list of your top [number] findings.
skills.summary: Google's Big Sleep agent reported about 20 security flaws in open-source software, following its SQLite find.

skills.name: Formally verify software at large scale with Claude
skills.prompt: I want to formally verify that [a specific module or library in my codebase at path] is free of [a bug class, e.g. out-of-bounds access or integer overflow]. Pick a suitable verification tool for [language], write the specifications and proofs, and run them. Finish with a report listing what was proven, what failed, and any bugs found, and don't change my source code without showing me the diff first.
skills.summary: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team used Claude to formally verify software, proving code is free of certain bugs on codebases larger than was historically feasible.

skills.name: Generate a robot arm CAD model from one prompt
skills.prompt: Using a text-to-CAD approach with CadQuery, generate a model of [a robot arm / mechanism] with [number of joints, size, and constraints] in [folder]. Include the parts as separate STEP files and a simple viewer so I can inspect it. Finish by listing any parts you could not model well so I can handle them myself.
skills.summary: A text-to-cad skill let Codex produce a 7-DOF robot arm with kinematics, a GUI and STEP parts in one demo prompt, though not the gripper.

skills.name: Generate parametric CAD models from a prompt
skills.prompt: Write a parametric CAD script in [CadQuery or OpenSCAD] for [describe the part, e.g. a wall bracket for a 25mm pipe], with named variables for all key dimensions at the top. Run it and export an [STL or STEP] file to this folder. Stop when the file exports without errors and show me the list of parameters I can change.
skills.summary: An open-source text-to-CAD tool that produces 3D models from text and image references by generating CAD as code.

skills.name: Generate parametric geometry workflows with an agent
skills.prompt: Build a parametric geometry workflow in [Grasshopper or a Python library like CadQuery] that generates [describe shape, e.g. a lattice panel] from inputs like [width, height, density]. Run it with three different input sets and save the outputs. Stop when all three run cleanly and give me a short note on how to change the parameters.
skills.summary: GrassLobster uses agentic AI to generate parametric geometry workflows.

skills.name: Give agents a multi-engine math kernel via MCP
skills.prompt: Connect the MCP server for [math tool, e.g. MathKernel or a computer algebra system] to this project, then use it to solve [math problem or set of equations] and show the result along with which engine produced it and how it was verified. If engines disagree, flag it and explain. Done means I get the answer, the evidence for it, and a note on any assumptions you made.
skills.summary: MathKernel is an evidence-aware multi-engine mathematics kernel exposed as an MCP server for agents to use.

skills.name: Hunt business-logic flaws and open fix PRs
skills.prompt: Review my codebase [repo name] for business-logic flaws and authentication or authorization bypasses. Split it into parts and examine each, then try to confirm every suspected issue in a sandbox, not on production. Finish with a ranked list of confirmed findings, and open a draft pull request with a fix for each one. Do not merge anything or touch live systems.
skills.summary: Parallel Devin agents each read part of a codebase, find business-logic and auth bypass flaws, confirm them in a sandbox, then open remediation PRs (vendor description).

skills.name: Hunt for unpatched vulnerabilities in SQLite commits
skills.prompt: In this repo [path or URL], review the commits from the last [time period or number], starting with the fix for [known patched bug or commit]. Look for similar flaws that the fix may have missed, especially [bug class, e.g. memory safety]. Write a report listing each suspect commit, why it looks vulnerable, and how you'd confirm it. Don't modify the code or disclose anything publicly.
skills.summary: Google's Big Sleep agent reviewed recent SQLite commits starting from a patched bug and found an exploitable flaw, which was fixed before release.

skills.name: Mine biological datasets for new leads with thousands of agents
skills.prompt: I have a dataset of [type of biological data, e.g. gene expression CSVs] in [folder path]. Write and run analysis scripts to look for patterns, outliers, or correlations that could be new research leads about [your research question]. Finish with a ranked list of the five most promising leads, each with the evidence behind it, the method used, and caveats, and save the scripts so I can rerun them.
skills.summary: OpenAI describes running thousands of AI agents over complex biological data to uncover new research leads.

skills.name: Monitor and score CVEs with real-time alerts
skills.prompt: Build an n8n workflow that checks CVE feeds such as CISA and OTX every [interval], asks an AI model to score each new CVE for relevance to my stack [list of technologies] and severity, and logs them to my Google Sheet [sheet name]. High-scoring items should also alert me in [Slack channel or Gmail]. You're done when a test run logs new CVEs and flags the relevant ones; show me a sample alert before activating sending.
skills.summary: An n8n workflow monitors CVEs from sources like CISA and OTX, scores them with AI, and alerts via Slack, Gmail and Google Sheets.

skills.name: Open recent protein-ligand structures in PDB
skills.prompt: In the Protein Data Bank, find the [number] most recently released structures of [protein, e.g. GSK3B] bound to a ligand. Open each one in the Ligand Interaction view and give me the PDB ID, ligand name, resolution and a link for each. Stop when all are open.
skills.summary: A researcher had Comet find the three latest GSK3B protein-ligand complexes in the PDB and open each in Ligand Interaction view.

skills.name: Orchestrate a Spot robot through multi-step tasks
skills.prompt: Write a Python program that breaks the task [multi-step task, e.g. tidy the workbench] into steps for a robot or simulator I have called [robot or simulator name]. After each step, have it check a camera frame or video clip from [source] to confirm the step is done before moving to the next. Show me the plan and code before running anything on real hardware. Stop when the program completes all steps in a simulated run.
skills.summary: Gemini Robotics ER 2 drives a Boston Dynamics Spot, watching video to confirm tasks like tying a trash bag are done before moving on.

skills.name: Patch laptop BIOS to unlock hidden firmware menus
skills.prompt: I have a firmware dump for my own [laptop model] at [file path]. Disassemble it, explain how the settings menus are gated and where any signature check happens, and propose a patch to unlock the hidden options. Work only on a copy of the file and don't flash anything; show me the proposed patch and the recovery risks first so I can decide.
skills.summary: A Reddit user gave Claude Code a BIOS dump; it disassembled it, found the signature check and patched it, unlocking hidden settings after flashing (secondhand account).

skills.name: Program a sub-$2k personal robot
skills.prompt: Help me get started programming my [robot name or model] using ROS2. Look at the project in this folder, explain how it is structured, and write a simple node that makes the robot [simple task, e.g. drive forward 1 meter and stop]. Stop once the node builds and I have the exact command to run it in simulation, and ask me before running anything on real hardware.
skills.summary: MARS is a general-purpose robot with an open onboard agentic OS built on ROS2.

skills.name: Repair formal proofs for a verified garbage collector
skills.prompt: In my [Coq/Lean/Isabelle] project at [folder], the proof [file or lemma] is broken after [change you made]. Edit the files, run the build, and repair the proof with the smallest local changes. Do not weaken or change any specification or invariant without asking me first, and finish with a list of every statement you altered so I can review it.
skills.summary: Codex edited files and ran builds to repair CertiGC proofs; it handled local repair well, but humans had to check that its invariants preserved the specification.

skills.name: Reverse engineer Claude Desktop to find a path to Linux support
skills.prompt: Reverse engineer [the app or binary] by inspecting its minified or compiled code to understand how a specific feature works or why it's limited to a certain platform, then write up what you find including any architectural layers involved. Produce a clear technical summary and a proposed path forward, stopping short of modifying or redistributing the original software.
skills.summary: A maintainer pointed Claude at the minified Claude Desktop app to find why Cowork only runs on macOS; it found the VM and sandbox layers and mapped a route to Linux.

skills.name: Reverse engineer a Go binary with Ghidra via MCP
skills.prompt: Connect to Ghidra via MCP and analyze this Go binary [path/name] to identify its routes and endpoints, then look for vulnerabilities like path traversal or SQL injection. Give me a report of what it found, and flag anything uncertain for me to double check manually.
skills.summary: Huli had Cursor drive GhidraMCP to identify a Golang binary, list its routes and find a path traversal, but it missed the SQL injection check.

skills.name: Reverse engineer a classic game ROM via Ghidra MCP
skills.prompt: Connect to Ghidra via MCP and load this [ROM or binary file]. Analyze the disassembled functions, infer their purpose from behavior and strings, and rename them with descriptive labels, producing an annotated function map when done.
skills.summary: The author connected Claude to Ghidra through MCP to analyze and rename functions in an Atari River Raid ROM.

skills.name: Reverse engineer a patch into a full exploit chain
skills.prompt: Given this [software patch or diff], analyze what changed, decompile or inspect the relevant binaries, and identify the security vulnerability it fixes. Build a proof-of-concept exploit demonstrating the issue in a safe, isolated test environment, and stop before using it against anything outside that environment.
skills.summary: A researcher used Claude Opus in Claude Code with Playwright MCP to decompile code, find vulnerabilities, and build a working exploit.

skills.name: Reverse engineer an old game binary to crack a restriction
skills.prompt: I'm analyzing [old program or game binary] that I own, to understand how it enforces [restriction] for [research or preservation purpose]. Using Ghidra output in [project folder], trace the call graph from [function or string] and list every place the check is validated. Finish with a written map of the validation sites and a proposed patch plan; don't modify any files until I approve.
skills.summary: A poster used Claude Code alongside Ghidra to trace a call graph across many validation sites in a 13-year-old game binary and crack a restriction.

skills.name: Reverse engineer device hardware and write drivers
skills.prompt: I have an old [device, e.g. printer or scanner] that no longer works on [my OS and version]. Help me write a driver for it: tell me what to run or check on the device, I'll report back exactly what I see, and use that to work out how it communicates. Finished means working driver code, build and install steps, and a way for me to test that it works. Pause and ask before anything that could change the device's firmware or my system settings.
skills.summary: A user points Claude at their own electronics to write drivers, such as one for an old printer that stopped working on a new macOS, with the user acting as its hands for diagnosis.

skills.name: Reverse-engineer binaries in Ghidra
skills.prompt: Connect to the Ghidra MCP server I have set up and open the binary at [path to binary]. Identify its main functions, rename them based on what they do, and list any suspicious behavior such as network calls or file writes. Finish with a short written summary of what the program does and the functions that support that conclusion.
skills.summary: An MCP server exposing 110 Ghidra tools for AI-assisted reverse engineering.

skills.name: Run a home robot through Claude Desktop
skills.prompt: Connect to my home robot or smart device via [its control interface] along with my email and calendar, and have it carry out a simple routine like a patrol or check-in, logging what it observes into a journal file. Run one test cycle and show me the log before setting up anything recurring.
skills.summary: Tal Raviv controlled a robot via Claude Desktop with his usual email and calendar tools; it proposed patrolling the house and publishing a field journal, and did a test run.

skills.name: Run an AI agent on a Nokia 110 feature phone
skills.prompt: I have an old [device model, e.g. feature phone or small embedded gadget] with about [RAM amount] of RAM, and I want it to trigger a simple action: [e.g. send a text to a script that toggles a light]. Help me work out what the device can do, write the smallest working code or bridge to connect it to an AI agent, and test it. Stop when I can press [a key or send a message] on the device and see the action happen, and tell me each step to run on my own hardware before you change anything.
skills.summary: Author reverse-engineered a 48MB-RAM Nokia 110 to run an AI agent on it and automate a few actions.

skills.name: Solve open math problems autonomously
skills.prompt: Here is an open math problem I want to work on: [problem statement]. Search the literature to check whether it is already solved, then try to build a proof or find a counterexample, showing each step. Finish with a clear verdict: solved, partial progress, or stuck, and list any steps that I should verify by hand.
skills.summary: DeepMind's Aletheia agent on Gemini Deep Think was evaluated on 700 open Erdős problems and autonomously solved four.

skills.name: Sort waste using local recycling rules
skills.prompt: Write a program that takes a photo of items from [image folder] and sorts each into compost, recycling, or trash. Look up the rules for [my city or waste provider] online and cite the source page for each rule you use. Output a table of item, bin, and reason, and flag any items you are unsure about. Stop once every item in the photos is sorted.
skills.summary: Gemini Robotics-ER 1.5 looks up local recycling rules online, then plans and sorts objects into compost, recycling and trash bins.

skills.name: Verify SPICE simulations against a real oscilloscope
skills.prompt: I have a SPICE simulation of [circuit] at [file path] and an oscilloscope reachable at [address] through an MCP server. Run the simulation, capture the real measurement of [signal or test point], and compare them on rise time, amplitude, and frequency. Report the differences and suggest model tweaks. Ask me before changing any hardware settings or sending output to the circuit.
skills.summary: MCP servers for an oscilloscope and SPICE simulator let Claude Code compare simulated circuits with real hardware measurements, closing the loop.

skills.name: Add groceries, buy on Amazon, and price-shop flights
skills.prompt: Log in to my [Walmart] account in the browser and add these items to my next grocery delivery order: [list of items with brands or sizes]. Then search [site] for round-trip flights from [origin] to [destination] on [dates] and compare prices across [2-3 sites]. Stop and show me the cart and the best flight options before checking out or buying anything.
skills.summary: A commenter and their wife regularly use an AI agent to add items to Walmart grocery delivery orders, buy from Amazon, and compare flight prices.

skills.name: Auto-buy items when the price hits a target
skills.prompt: Track the price of [product name or Amazon link] and alert me when it falls to [target price] or lower. Don't buy it automatically. Pause and show me the product, price, seller, and payment method, and wait for my approval first. Tell me the current price and confirm the alert is set.
skills.summary: Alexa's shopping assistant sets price alerts and can auto-buy Amazon-fulfilled items at a target price with the default payment method, and schedules recurring purchases.

skills.name: Book a gym tour and compare memberships with Comet
skills.prompt: Find [number] [gyms or services] near [location], compare their membership prices, contract terms and fees in a table, and recommend one. Then start booking a tour at [chosen place] for [day and time]. Pause and show me the form details before submitting anything.
skills.summary: NBC tested Comet on job applications, shopping and a gym tour; it needed intervention, booked the tour after prodding, and built a price comparison chart.

skills.name: Build a BMW parts cart with a browser agent
skills.prompt: Go to [parts retailer website] and build a cart with the parts I need for my [year, make, model]: [list of parts]. Confirm each part fits my vehicle and choose [preferred brand or price range] where possible. Stop at checkout, show me the cart with prices and fitment notes, and pause for me to enter any login or payment details myself before anything is purchased.
skills.summary: A commenter says Operator completed a BMW 330Ci parts cart task well, paused for credentials at the site, and saved about 30 minutes.

skills.name: Build a grocery cart from purchase history
skills.prompt: Open my [grocery store or Instacart] account and look at my past orders from the last [number] months. Build a cart of about [number] items I buy regularly, plus ingredients for these dinners: [dinner ideas]. Flag anything that is out of stock and suggest substitutes. Stop with the cart filled and show it to me; do not check out or pay.
skills.summary: Instacart's AI assistant built a 27-item cart from the shopper's purchase history, turned dinner ideas into carts and flagged unavailable items.

skills.name: Build an Instacart grocery cart from a chat request
skills.prompt: Using my connected Instacart account, build a cart at [store name] for: [list of items, with brands or sizes if it matters]. Choose reasonable matches and tell me about any substitutions. Stop when the cart is ready and show me the full cart and total, and do not place the order until I confirm.
skills.summary: A reporter connected Instacart to ChatGPT, which assembled the cart for formula, ice cream and fruit and opened a checkout confirmation in chat.

skills.name: Build an Instacart list for a charcuterie board
skills.prompt: Open Instacart and build a cart from [store name] with everything I need for a [dish or party, e.g. charcuterie board] serving [number] people, about [number] items. Choose the cheapest or best-selling option for each item. When the cart is full, show me the list with prices and stop; do not check out.
skills.summary: Comet added about 20 items to an Instacart cart from ShopRite in about five minutes, choosing cheapest or bestselling items, and declined to purchase.

skills.name: Build an e-commerce agent with OpenClaw
skills.prompt: Help me build a small e-commerce workflow agent for my [store platform, e.g. Shopify] store. Start with one job: [e.g. checking inventory and drafting supplier reorder emails, or updating product listings from a spreadsheet]. Finished means one working run on [3 sample products] with a short summary of what it did. Pause and show me anything before it sends a message, changes a listing, or spends money.
skills.summary: Poster spent 100+ hours and 200M+ tokens building an e-commerce workflow agent with OpenClaw; post focuses mostly on the build effort.

skills.name: Build and order a grocery cart from an idea
skills.prompt: Build an Instacart cart for [meal idea, e.g. Taco Tuesday] for [number] people from [preferred store], avoiding [dietary restrictions] and staying under [budget]. Show me the full cart with quantities and total cost, and wait for my approval before checking out. Then use delivery time [window] to schedule it.
skills.summary: Through the Instacart connector, Muse turns an idea like Taco Tuesday into a cart at the preferred store, checks out and arranges delivery.

skills.name: Build group grocery carts through a Signal-based agent
skills.prompt: Set up an agent I can message in [Signal group] that drafts a grocery list from our past [store] orders and lets everyone in the group add or remove items. When I say the list is final, log into [store], build the cart, and check that every item is in stock. Stop before checkout and show me the cart and total so I can pay myself.
skills.summary: A self-hosted Signal agent drafts a grocery list from past orders, lets group members edit it, then logs into the store and builds and validates the cart; the author finishes checkout manually.

skills.name: Buy a microwave from Costco
skills.prompt: Find a [product, e.g. microwave] at [store] that fits [size, wattage, budget under $X], and show me your top two picks with prices and reviews. After I choose one, put it in the cart and pause on the checkout page so I can check the total, delivery or pickup, and address. Only place the order when I say so.
skills.summary: A user had Meta Muse buy a microwave from Costco.

skills.name: Buy headphones during a sale with an AI agent
skills.prompt: Find the best current price for [headphones model] across [retailers] and tell me if it is on sale. If it is under [$price], add it to the cart at the cheapest trusted seller. Stop before paying and show me the price, shipping, and return policy for approval.
skills.summary: An AI agent bought headphones for the poster; they also use a browser extension for sale purchases and price-drop alerts.

skills.name: Buy homemade pizza ingredients from Walmart
skills.prompt: Go to [store website, e.g. Walmart] and add the ingredients for homemade [dish, e.g. pizza] for [number] people to my cart, choosing items under [budget] total. Tell me if you need me to take over for a login or a verification check. Stop at the checkout page and show me the cart and total, and do not place the order without my confirmation.
skills.summary: A reviewer had ChatGPT Agent shop at Walmart for pizza ingredients, handing control back briefly for an anti-bot check.

skills.name: Buy items on Amazon from a photo
skills.prompt: I'm attaching a photo of [item or wrapper]. Identify the product, find the best match on [Amazon or retailer], and add it to the cart in the size and quantity I want: [quantity]. Stop at the checkout page and show me the item, price, and delivery address before buying anything.
skills.summary: Author used ChatGPT Agent to reorder an item from a photo of its wrapper, handling the whole Amazon purchase until Amazon blocked agents.

skills.name: Buy products online from a card photo
skills.prompt: Find the best price for [product] from [retailers or any reputable store] and prepare an order. Do not enter payment details or place the order yourself. Show me the item, merchant, total price, shipping and delivery date, then wait for my approval before the purchase step.
skills.summary: Musk said Grok Bot bought LEGO from the LEGO website, and that users can drop a credit card photo into chat so it finds the best deal and orders; plans and safeguards weren't specified.

skills.name: Buy products through an agent and track the order
skills.prompt: Find [product description] from a reputable seller, with a budget under [amount] and delivery to [address] by [date]. Show me the top options with price, shipping, and a link, and let me pick. Before you check out, pause and show me the item, total, and shipping address, then after I approve, place the order and check its status until it ships.
skills.summary: Per Rye, a user had his OpenClaw agent find products and check out via Rye's checkout API, with items delivered and order status polled afterwards.

skills.name: Call local stores to check toy stock
skills.prompt: Please call [number] local stores near [my city or zip code] and ask whether they have [item, e.g. a Labubu figure] in stock. For each store, find out availability, price and today's closing hours, and whether they can hold one for me. When you are done, send me a short summary listing each store with what you learned. Do not reserve or pay for anything without checking with me first.
skills.summary: A writer used Gemini's calling feature to phone local stores about a Labubu figure and got text or email summaries of availability, price and hours.

skills.name: Click add-to-cart button on a website with computer use
skills.prompt: Open [website URL] in the browser, find the [product name or description], choose [size/color/options], and click the add-to-cart button. Stop once the item is in the cart and tell me the item, price, and quantity shown. Do not proceed to checkout or enter any payment details.
skills.summary: Víctor Paytuvi had Claude computer use find and click a site's add-to-cart button on the first try after Gemini failed.

skills.name: Compare Coca-Cola prices across Belgian supermarkets
skills.prompt: Compare the price of [product, brand and size] across [country] supermarkets such as [store 1, store 2, store 3]. Tell me which store is cheapest and which is priciest, and flag any current promotions. If a captcha or login blocks you, hand the browser back to me, and stop once you've given me a short comparison list.
skills.summary: Grok Bot compared a bottle of Coca-Cola across Belgian supermarkets, named cheapest and priciest and flagged promotions, handing the browser to the user at a Carrefour captcha.

skills.name: Compare Costco and Amazon carts on price and delivery
skills.prompt: Add this shopping list to a cart at both Costco and Amazon: [list of items with sizes or quantities]. Compare item prices, delivery charges and delivery times, and tell me which cart is the better deal. If you hit a captcha or two-factor prompt, hand control back to me, and do not check out. You're done when you've given me a side-by-side comparison.
skills.summary: Grok Bot added items to carts at Costco and Amazon and compared prices, delivery charges and times, handing the desktop back to the user for CAPTCHA or 2FA.

skills.name: Compare Costco bag prices and savings from a jumbled request
skills.prompt: I have a few messy questions: compare the price of [product, e.g. a bag of coffee] at [store, e.g. Costco] with [other store or size], work out the cost per [unit, e.g. ounce], and tell me how much I'd save buying [quantity]. Give me a short comparison with a clear recommendation. Don't add anything to my cart or buy anything without asking me first.
skills.summary: The user gave Alexa+ a jumble of requests and it worked out a shopping comparison covering Costco bag pricing and savings.

skills.name: Compare grocery prices across stores from a list
skills.prompt: Here is my grocery list: [paste list or attach a photo of a handwritten list]. Compare prices for each item across [store 1] and [store 2], noting pack sizes and anything out of stock. Give me a table with the cheapest option per item and the total per store. Do not add anything to a cart or place an order without showing me first.
skills.summary: A tech worker built a Gemini browser agent that takes a typed or scanned handwritten grocery list and compares prices on Amazon Fresh and Flipkart Minutes.

skills.name: Complete online surveys for free stuff
skills.prompt: Fill out this survey for me using the answers I'd realistically give: [survey link]. Use my profile details [age range, location, interests] and don't invent anything unusual.
