Before you submit, show me the answers and whether it asks for payment or sensitive info, then tell me what reward to expect.
skills.summary: A user had Grok Bot fill out a survey to get free stuff; it has worked once so far.

skills.name: Customize and order a matcha drink for an event
skills.prompt: Order [drink or food item] for [event name] on [date] from [shop or ordering service], customized this way: [milk, sweetness, toppings, size, quantity]. Use the ordering tool or integration I've connected, and pick up at or deliver to [location or time]. You're done when the order is placed and you've given me the confirmation and total cost. Before you pay or place the order, pause and show me the full order summary for my approval.
skills.summary: Grace Ling connected API keys to Claude Cowork, which customized and ordered a coconut cloud matcha drink for an event via the Monid agent integration.

skills.name: Do your online shopping through Operator
skills.prompt: Buy [item or list of items] for me from [preferred retailers other than Amazon if possible], comparing at least [3] sellers on price, shipping time, and reviews. Add the best option to the cart and then stop. Show me the item, price, shipping address, and payment method, and wait for my approval before placing the order.
skills.summary: The author says using Operator via ChatGPT to handle buying changed their shopping habits and cut their dependence on Amazon.

skills.name: Draft refund emails from a photo and Gmail receipt
skills.prompt: I want a refund for [product] that [describe the problem]. Find the receipt in my Gmail from [store/approximate date], pull out the order number and purchase date, and draft a polite refund request email to [store support address if known]. Leave it as a draft and show it to me; do not send it.
skills.summary: Cowork finds the receipt in Gmail, extracts the order number and date, and drafts a refund email for the user to review and send.

skills.name: Email Houston dealerships to shop for a car
skills.prompt: Help me shop for a [car make and model] in [city]. Build a tracking sheet of [number] nearby dealerships with contact details, then draft outreach emails asking for out-the-door pricing on [trim, color, budget]. Pause and show me the emails and any web forms before sending or submitting them, then log replies in the sheet and summarize the best offers.
skills.summary: Cowork built a dealership tracking sheet, sent outreach emails, filled web forms and managed replies; a separate 100+ receipt expense job hit limits and moved to Claude Code.

skills.name: Fill a grocery basket from a regular-items sheet
skills.prompt: Open my Google Sheet of regular groceries at [sheet link] and add each item to my basket at [grocery store site]. If an item isn't available, list it at the end instead of substituting. Stop with the basket full and give me a list of items that need my attention. Do not check out or pay.
skills.summary: Claude in Chrome added about 24 items to an ASDA basket from a Google Sheet, but the user still had to fix items and check out.

skills.name: Fill a supermarket cart from regular purchases and sales
skills.prompt: Create a skill that connects to [supermarket]'s MCP server, re-adds my usual groceries from [list or past orders], checks current sales for them, and fills the real cart within a budget of [amount]. Suggest cheaper swaps where there are sales but ask me before swapping. Stop when the cart is filled and show me the cart and total; do not check out.
skills.summary: A developer built a Claude Code skill using Silpo's MCP server to re-add usual groceries, check sales and fill the real cart within a budget, leaving checkout to the human.

skills.name: Fill a supermarket cart with agent mode for pickup
skills.prompt: Go to [local supermarket website], sign in with my saved account, and add these items to my cart: [grocery list]. Choose pickup for [day and time window] at [store location]. Stop before placing the order and show me the cart, substitutions, and total so I can approve it.
skills.summary: Agent mode added groceries to the cart at a local supermarket while the poster worked, for pickup the next morning.

skills.name: Find a toy and start checkout with Operator
skills.prompt: Find a [type of toy] for a [age]-year-old under $[budget] on [retailer website] that meets these requirements: [criteria]. Pick the best match, add it to the cart and walk me through checkout. Pause and show me the item, price and delivery details before entering any payment info or placing the order.
skills.summary: OpenAI's Operator picked a toy matching criteria and opened Target.com but did not complete the purchase, walking the user through checkout.

skills.name: Find a vintage lamp on Etsy
skills.prompt: Browse Etsy for [item, e.g. vintage brass lamp] under [budget], in [style or era], shipping to [country]. Shortlist five options and give me each listing's link, price, shipping time and seller rating. Do not add anything to a cart or check out. Just show me the links so I can open them myself.
skills.summary: ChatGPT Agent worked 50 minutes and reported adding five lamps to the cart, but the user's own cart was empty as it ran on a separate computer.

skills.name: Find and add high-meat cat food to a basket
skills.prompt: On [store website], find the [product type, e.g. cat food] with the highest [criterion, e.g. meat content] under [budget], comparing at least [number] options in a short table with the evidence for each. Add the winner to my basket and stop there. Don't check out, and show me the basket before any further step.
skills.summary: A reviewer had Comet's assistant find the cat food with the most meat and add it to the basket, plus some product comparison and form filling, though imperfectly.

skills.name: Find and buy a same-day-delivery fern as a gift
skills.prompt: Find local shops near [city or zip] that offer same-day delivery of [gift item, e.g. a fern] to [recipient address], and pick a good option under $[budget]. Fill in the checkout form with my details and the gift message '[message]', then stop and show me the order summary and total before clicking buy. After I approve, place the order and report the confirmation and tracking info.
skills.summary: In Agent mode the author had ChatGPT search local plant shops and fill the checkout form, stopping for him to click buy, then reported the order with tracking.

skills.name: Find and test discount codes with ChatGPT agent mode
skills.prompt: I'm about to buy [product] from [store website]. Find public discount codes, add the item to the cart, and test each code at checkout to see which gives the best final price. Stop before entering any payment details or placing the order, and show me a table of each code tried, whether it worked, and the final total.
skills.summary: The poster uses ChatGPT's agent mode for multi-step research and testing of discount codes to get better prices before purchase.

skills.name: Find and test promo codes before checkout
skills.prompt: I'm about to buy [product] from [store or website] and want the lowest price. Search for current public promo codes and discounts, tell me which ones are likely to work, and list the sources. Give me a ranked list of codes to try and the expected final price, and don't purchase anything.
skills.summary: ChatGPT searches for public discounts, tests promo codes and confirms the final checkout price before the user buys.

skills.name: Find coffee makers under $100 and add options to the cart
skills.prompt: Search Amazon for [product type] with [must-have features] under $[budget]. Build a comparison table of the top options with price, ratings and key differences, then add the best [number] to my cart. Stop before checkout and do not buy anything.
skills.summary: Perplexity Comet searched Amazon for coffee makers with a grinder, built a comparison table and added two options to the cart, stopping before purchase.

skills.name: Find good eBay deals on a schedule
skills.prompt: Every [number] hours, search eBay for [item or model] and scrape the new listings with [Firecrawl or another scraper]. Judge each one against my criteria: max price [amount including shipping], condition [condition], seller rating above [number], and typical market price around [amount]. Send me only the listings that look like good deals on [Telegram / other channel], each with a one-sentence reason and the link; do not bid or buy anything.
skills.summary: A community developer built an eBay deal finder where Firecrawl scrapes listings and Hermes runs on a schedule to judge whether each is a good deal against the user's criteria.

skills.name: Find holiday gifts and check stock and sales
skills.prompt: I need gift ideas for [recipient, age, interests] under [budget]. Find [5] options, name retailers that carry each, and check whether each is in stock and on sale now. Give me a short comparison list with price, stock status, and links. Do not buy anything; pause and show me before any checkout step.
skills.summary: A writer used the Gemini app and its agentic feature to find gift ideas and retailers and check stock and sales, noting some features weren't fully ready.

skills.name: Find vegetarian restaurants and save notes via computer use
skills.prompt: Find [number] [type, e.g. vegetarian-friendly] restaurants near [location or landmark]. For each, note the name, address, opening hours, and a one-line description, then save everything to a text file called [filename]. Stop once the file is saved and tell me where it is; don't make any bookings.
skills.summary: The author ran Anthropic's computer-use demo in Docker and had Claude find 5 vegetarian-friendly restaurants near Bond Street and save details to a notepad file.

skills.name: Get competing car quotes from dealerships and negotiate a lower price
skills.prompt: Find [number] dealerships near [zip code] that have a [car make, model, trim] in stock and request out-the-door quotes using my email [email]. When quotes arrive, draft replies that use the lower offers to ask other dealers to beat them. Show me each form and email before submitting or sending, and finish with a ranked comparison of the quotes.
skills.summary: An agent filled out web forms at 8-10 dealerships and emailed competing quotes against each other, reaching a deal that saved over $4,200 in three days.

skills.name: Hand consumer errands to an always-on agent
skills.prompt: Help me with this errand: [e.g. sign up for internet service at my address, create an account at a store, or order dinner from a restaurant]. Do as much as you can and tell me which steps you couldn't finish. Stop and show me the details before any payment, account creation or form submission.
skills.summary: A journalist tested Dot on ISP signup, an Ikea account and food ordering; it finished only some with human help, blocked by browser checks and payment steps.

skills.name: Handle an IKEA return end to end
skills.prompt: I need to return [item] I bought from [store] on [date], order number [number]. Find the return policy, start the return through the store's website or support chat, and schedule a pickup at [address] on [preferred dates]. Pause and show me the details before you confirm the pickup or submit any form, then give me the confirmation and the expected refund amount.
skills.summary: Muse dealt with IKEA customer service and scheduled the pickup, which showed up at the user's door after he had forgotten about it.

skills.name: Have an agent pick and buy a surprise gift
skills.prompt: I want to surprise [person] with a gift under [$ budget]. Their interests are [interests], and they already have [things to avoid]. Browse [store or stores] and pick your top 3 candidates with prices, delivery dates, and why each fits. Stop before adding anything to the cart or buying anything. Show me your choice and wait for my explicit go-ahead before any purchase step.
skills.summary: A user asked GPT to choose a surprise gift, and commenters say the agent went as far as clicking Buy Now on a logged-in Amazon page.

skills.name: Hunt Black Friday TV deals against stated requirements
skills.prompt: Search deal guides and major retailers for current sales on [product, e.g. a TV] that meet these requirements: [size, features, max price]. Return the top [number] deals with price, discount, retailer and buy links, plus two cheaper alternatives. Do not purchase anything.
skills.summary: ChatGPT Agent searched deal guides and retailers for several minutes and returned five discounted TVs with buy links plus two cheaper alternatives.

skills.name: Hunt high-value Pokémon cards on eBay overnight
skills.prompt: Write and run an agent that browses [marketplace, e.g. eBay] listings for [item type, e.g. graded Pokémon cards] under [max price], extracts each listing's [certificate or serial number], and compares it to prices in [price source or file]. Save listings that look underpriced by at least [percent]% to a file called [output file] with the link, price, and reference price. Stop after running it once on [number] listings and show me the results and how to schedule it overnight. Don't buy, bid, or message any sellers.
skills.summary: An engineer built a Codex agent that browses eBay listings, extracts PSA certificate numbers and cross-references known prices while he sleeps.

skills.name: Launch and run an online store with AI agents
skills.prompt: Build me an online store selling [product type] with a product catalog, cart, and checkout, using [Stripe or payment provider] in test mode first. Add simple admin views for orders, stock levels, and customer questions. Stop when I can place a test order end to end, and pause and show me everything before switching on real payments or publishing the site.
skills.summary: The author used an AI store builder to launch a retail shop taking real payments in one sitting, with five agents watching orders, stock and customers.

skills.name: Let AI agents place DoorDash orders
skills.prompt: Help me set up the DoorDash dd-cli beta so you can order food for me from the terminal. Once it is installed, find a [cuisine or dish] option near [my address] under $[budget] and build the order. Pause and show me the items, delivery address and total before placing the order.
skills.summary: DoorDash's dd-cli beta lets agents order food, with a demo of Claude completing a full order end to end.

skills.name: Let AI agents search a store, build carts, and prep checkout
skills.prompt: Go to [store website] and find [items I want, with size, color, quantity] within a budget of [$X]. Add them to the cart, try any available promo codes, and stop at the checkout page. Show me the cart contents, final total, and checkout link, and do not enter payment details or place the order.
skills.summary: A store is set up so Claude or ChatGPT agents can search the catalog, build a cart, and apply promo codes, then hand over a checkout link before payment.

skills.name: Let Claude buy a game autonomously
skills.prompt: Go to [store name] and buy the game [game title] for [platform] if the price is at or below [max price]. Use the saved payment method on my account. Pause and show me the item, price, and total at the final checkout step before you pay, and finish when I've confirmed and you've shown me the order confirmation.
skills.summary: The poster built payment infrastructure so Claude could complete a game purchase on its own when told to, in about 60 seconds.

skills.name: Let an agent make purchases from a pre-funded balance
skills.prompt: I've pre-funded [account or balance name] with [amount]. Find [item to buy] from [site or store] at the best price within that balance, and get everything ready for checkout. If the exact total doesn't match the balance, tell me about options such as a gift card. Pause before any payment and show me the item, total, and shipping address for my approval.
skills.summary: A commenter's agent completed a purchase from a pre-funded balance, buying an $18 gift card to cover a $17.73 order.

skills.name: List a Quest 3 and negotiate with buyers
skills.prompt: List my [item, condition, accessories] on Facebook Marketplace at [asking price] with a clear description and the photos I give you. Handle buyer messages and negotiate, but never accept below my floor of [minimum price] and hold firm on [pickup location or terms]. Show me any offer you want to accept before confirming, and do not share my address or phone number.
skills.summary: Meta Muse listed a Meta Quest 3 on Facebook Marketplace and was instructed to negotiate with buyers using a floor price and push strategy.

skills.name: Monitor Amazon and eBay prices and email on changes
skills.prompt: Build an n8n workflow that reads product URLs from my Google Sheet [sheet name], checks the current Amazon or eBay price three times a day, and compares it to the last saved price. If the price changed, email me to [my email] with old and new prices, and log every check in the sheet. It's done when a test run updates the sheet and a simulated change sends one email.
skills.summary: An n8n workflow checks product URLs from a Google Sheet three times a day, compares prices, emails changes and logs every check.

skills.name: Monitor competitor marketplace prices
skills.prompt: Every [day or week], check these competitor listings on [marketplace names]: [links or search terms]. Record the price, stock status, and any changes in a spreadsheet, and flag anything that dropped more than [percent]. If a site blocks you with a CAPTCHA, skip it, list it as blocked, and send me the summary when done.
skills.summary: The poster uses Grok Bot to check competitor listings and product prices over time, though CAPTCHAs block it on some sites.

skills.name: Negotiate Facebook Marketplace purchases with sellers
skills.prompt: Search Facebook Marketplace near [location] for [item] under [max price]. For listings that look worthwhile, draft a polite lowball offer starting at [percent or amount] with a walk-away price of [max price]. Show me each message and the seller's reply before sending anything, and do not commit to buying or arrange a meetup without my approval.
skills.summary: A user set up an agent to lowball sellers on Facebook Marketplace, and it reportedly negotiated a Jeep Wrangler for $1500 plus a PS5 and three TVs.

skills.name: Negotiate a TV price with a retailer's chat
skills.prompt: Find the best price for [product and model] from retailers in [country], then use the retailer's chat to negotiate a lower price including shipping, aiming for [target price]. Decline upsells like extended warranties unless I approve them. Pause and show me the final price and order details before paying or confirming anything.
skills.summary: ChatGPT Agent negotiated in Dutch with a retailer's chat, handled upsells, and landed an LG OLED TV at €939 including shipping.

skills.name: Negotiate a car purchase between dealers
skills.prompt: I want to buy a [car make, model, trim, year]. Research fair prices, search dealer inventory within [number] miles of [zip code], and contact each dealer for out-the-door quotes. Use the quotes against each other to negotiate the price down, and show me every message draft before you send it. Finish with a summary comparing all quotes and the best deal.
skills.summary: OpenClaw researched prices, searched dealer inventory, filled contact forms and played quotes against each other for $4,200 off; it messaged a wrong dealer once.

skills.name: Order Starbucks by voice from a Tesla while driving
skills.prompt: When I say I want coffee, order my usual from [Starbucks or other cafe] at the location nearest [my route or destination]: [drink, size, customizations]. Read back the drink, pickup location, and total to me out loud and wait for me to say yes before you place the order.
skills.summary: A user had Grok Bot in a Tesla place a Starbucks order, confirming the drink and total by voice before ordering.

skills.name: Order dinner by voice via Grubhub and Uber Eats
skills.prompt: Help me order dinner for [number] people from [Grubhub or Uber Eats] near [delivery address]. Suggest a few options for [cuisine or craving], apply my customizations like [no onions, extra sauce], and let me change items as we go. Read back the full order, delivery address, and total, and wait for my explicit okay before placing it.
skills.summary: A writer ordered dinner conversationally with Alexa+ through linked Grubhub and Uber Eats accounts, including customizing and changing the order.

skills.name: Order family groceries from fridge contents
skills.prompt: Check what's in my connected fridge [brand/app] and build a grocery order for my household of [number] for [store]. Look for discounts and apply any valid codes, and choose a pickup time at [store location] that fits [my schedule]. Before you place the order or pay, show me the full cart, total, and pickup time and wait for my approval.
skills.summary: A parent has Grok Bot check a connected Samsung fridge and order groceries twice a week, hunting discounts, applying codes, and handling pickup timing.

skills.name: Order from a restaurant menu photo with ChatGPT
skills.prompt: I'm attaching a photo of the menu at [restaurant]. I want a meal for [number of people] with a budget of about [amount], and these preferences or restrictions: [dietary needs, dislikes, spice level]. Suggest an order, then write it as a short, clear list I can show the waiter, with any modifications spelled out. Stop when you've given me the final list.
skills.summary: Customers photograph a menu, have ChatGPT compose their order, and show the phone screen to restaurant staff.

skills.name: Order groceries and hunt deals with Comet
skills.prompt: I'm signed in to [grocery store] in another tab. Take this list: [items with quantities] and search for the best deals or sales on each, preferring [brands or dietary limits]. Add the best options to my cart and stop when the cart is complete. Pause and show me the full cart with the total before checkout, and do not pay until I confirm.
skills.summary: A user gave Comet a grocery list and signed in to their grocery account in another tab, and it searched for deals; another has it email daily job leads.

skills.name: Order groceries from Amazon Fresh and Whole Foods
skills.prompt: Build a grocery order from [Amazon Fresh or Whole Foods] for this week's meals: [recipes or meal ideas]. Use my past purchases and respect these dietary preferences: [preferences]. Finish with a complete cart and total, and wait for my approval before checking out.
skills.summary: Alexa+ orders groceries, tracks past purchases and remembers recipes and dietary preferences.

skills.name: Order groceries from health data and a meal plan
skills.prompt: Using my health goals ([goals]), dietary preferences ([preferences]), and this data: [paste lab results, body scan numbers, or nutrition targets], create a one-week meal plan. Then add the ingredients to a cart at [grocery store or delivery service]. You are done when the cart matches the plan; show me the cart and total and wait for my approval before checkout.
skills.summary: Austen Allred's AI automatically orders groceries based on body scans, health data, and preferences, mapped to a meal plan.

skills.name: Order groceries online with a local LLM skill
skills.prompt: Build me a grocery skill that reads my fridge list in [file or note], my past orders from [store], and current stock at [store website]. Then fill a cart with what I'm running low on for [number] days of meals. Pause and show me the cart and total before checkout, and stop once I've approved the order.
skills.summary: The author built a grocery skill for a local Qwen 3.6 27B model that knows their fridge contents, past orders and real-time stock, and it ordered products for them online.

skills.name: Order groceries with computer-use agents
skills.prompt: Open [grocery store or delivery service] and build a cart for this list: [grocery items with quantities]. Use my delivery address [address] and pick the cheapest in-stock option for each item, flagging any substitutions. Stop before checkout and show me the full cart and total so I can approve the order.
skills.summary: The author tried Operator and two other computer-use agents on grocery shopping and found the experience too poor for ordinary consumers.

skills.name: Order healthy meals twice a day automatically
skills.prompt: Find lunch and dinner options for me on [delivery app or restaurant site] delivering to [address], choosing the healthiest choices that fit [dietary goals] and cost under [budget] each. You are done when the meal is in the cart with the delivery time shown. Pause and show me the order and total before paying, and wait for my confirmation.
skills.summary: Flo Crivello's agent has decided and ordered his meals twice a day for two weeks, following instructions to pick the healthiest options.

skills.name: Order ice cream delivery and build schedule spreadsheets
skills.prompt: Order [item, e.g. a pint of ice cream] for delivery to [my address] from [delivery service or store], with a budget of [amount]. Pick the best-reviewed option that fits, and add it to the cart. Stop before entering payment details or placing the order, and show me the cart, total, and delivery time so I can approve it.
skills.summary: Reporters tested Operator: it got ice cream delivered but needed guidance, payment info and purchase approval, and often got spreadsheet details wrong.

skills.name: Order lunch on Uber Eats by tapping a picture
skills.prompt: Build me a simple personal 'Lunch' web app that shows photos of my [number, e.g. 6] usual lunch orders from [restaurant names or favorite dishes]. When I tap a photo, it should start a helper agent that opens Uber Eats in a browser and puts that item in my cart for delivery to [my delivery address]. The job is done when tapping a photo reliably gets the right item to the checkout screen; pause and show me the cart, total, and address before placing any order or paying.
skills.summary: The author had an AI agent build a "Lunch" app where tapping a food photo spawns a subagent that orders the item on Uber Eats, to reduce decision fatigue.

skills.name: Order lunch through an AI agent
skills.prompt: Order me lunch from [restaurant or delivery app] to [address]: [food preferences, budget, dietary restrictions]. Get as far as the final checkout screen and then stop. Show me the items, total, and delivery time, and I will enter the payment details and any one-time codes myself.
skills.summary: Abhishek Upadhya had an AI agent order his lunch, giving it his CVV and OTP, and the food arrived without further intervention.

skills.name: Order office groceries from Slack requests
skills.prompt: Every [Thursday], collect grocery and supply requests posted in the Slack channel [#channel-name] and compile them into one deduplicated list. Post the list to me and wait for my approval, then build the cart at [Instacart store] and post the cart link back in the channel. Do not place the order or spend any money without my explicit go-ahead.
skills.summary: A startup's OpenClaw agent collects Slack requests, compiles a list, gets approval, builds the Instacart cart via ChatGPT's app, and posts the link back.

skills.name: Order pens and search for reservations and resorts
skills.prompt: Find [product, e.g. a 144-pack of pens] on [store, e.g. Amazon or Staples] at the best price with delivery by [date]. If one site blocks you, try another reputable retailer. Stop at the checkout page and show me the item, quantity, total price and delivery address before you pay for anything.
skills.summary: Operator found a 144-pack of pens on Staples after Amazon blocked it; restaurant booking failed and the resort search chose random dates.

skills.name: Order pizza for a group with computer use
skills.prompt: Open DoorDash on my desktop and find pizza places near [address] that deliver. Choose [number] pizzas that suit a group of [number] people with these preferences: [toppings, dietary needs], and add them to the cart. Stop at the checkout screen and show me the cart and total; do not pay.
skills.summary: Anthropic engineers had Claude computer use navigate DoorDash and choose pizzas for a group.

skills.name: Phone local stores to check product stock
skills.prompt: I need to find out which stores near [my city or zip code] have [product name or model] in stock. Look up the stores that carry it, check their websites for availability and the phone number, and give me a table with store, stock status, price, and phone number. Don't place any orders or reserve anything without showing me first.
skills.summary: A Grok-based personal assistant used Bland.ai to call local stores, hold conversations about stock, and return full transcripts with availability.

skills.name: Phone stores to check if items are in stock
skills.prompt: Please call or contact [store names or nearby stores] and ask whether they have [item, size, or model] in stock today. If you cannot place calls, tell me so right away instead of guessing. When finished, give me a list showing each store, its answer, its hours, and its phone number. Do not reserve or buy anything without showing me the details and getting my approval first.
skills.summary: Poster tried Manus on several tasks including calling stores to check stock; every task failed and it made no calls.

skills.name: Plan and order a week of groceries with Claude
skills.prompt: Plan dinners for [number] days for [number] people with these preferences: [diet, budget, dislikes]. Then build the combined grocery list, and add the items to my cart at [grocery store website]. Stop before checkout and show me the cart, substitutions, and total for approval.
skills.summary: The poster used Claude on Mac and iOS to plan and order a week of groceries, with partial success, and will keep using it up to the grocery-list step.

skills.name: Plan meals and fill an Instacart cart
skills.prompt: Plan [number] days of meals for [number] people with these preferences: [diet, allergies, budget]. Combine all the ingredients into one shopping list, then add them to a cart at [Instacart or grocery store]. Stop when the cart is ready and show me the full list and total before doing anything else; do not place the order.
skills.summary: The author used ChatGPT with the Instacart plugin to build a daily meal plan and put the ingredients into a ready-to-order shopping list.

skills.name: Plan meals and place grocery orders from a Google Doc
skills.prompt: Read my meal plan and grocery list in this Google Doc: [link]. Check the items against my pantry list, then add what is missing to my cart at [grocery store] in the browser. Stop at checkout and show me the cart and total so I can confirm payment myself.
skills.summary: Claude and Muse handle meal planning, pantry inventory and recipe tracking, then Muse reads a Google Doc and places the grocery order in a browser, with the poster confirming payment from their phone.

skills.name: Plan meals, build grocery list and order food
skills.prompt: Plan [number] dinners for the week for [number] people with these preferences: [diet, budget, foods to avoid]. Give me the recipes, a grocery list sorted by store section with estimated prices at [local store or area], and export it to a Google Sheet. If I ask you to order, build the cart on [DoorDash/other service] and pause for me to review it and handle payment myself.
skills.summary: ChatGPT Agent made recipes, a categorized grocery list with local prices and a Sheets export, and placed a DoorDash order but handed off for payment.

skills.name: Plan weekly meals and order groceries automatically
skills.prompt: Every [day of week] at [time], check this week's [store name] ad at [URL], and build a dinner meal plan for [number] people that favors discounted items and fits [dietary needs and budget]. Then write a grocery list organized by store section and save both the plan and list to [location]. Stop there and message me the summary; do not place any order without showing me the list and total and getting my approval first.
skills.summary: A single dad had Hermes create meal plans and grocery orders, with a weekly cron job scraping the HEB ad for a meal-planning skill, needing only some steering.

skills.name: Pre-stage household grocery carts from Instacart history
skills.prompt: Look at my [Instacart] order history, work out what my household is likely running low on, and fill a cart for [store] with those items twice a week. Text me a summary of the cart with quantities and the total. Don't place the order. Wait for me to confirm it.
skills.summary: An OpenClaw add-on scrapes Instacart order history, predicts what the household is running out of, fills the cart twice weekly and texts; nothing ships until the user taps Place Order.

skills.name: Research and buy online with approval at payment
skills.prompt: Research options for [thing to buy, or a meal plan with a grocery order for [number] people and a [budget]]. Prepare the order and, before paying, show me a spend request with the merchant, total and a description of what's in it. Wait for my approval before paying. You're done when the order is placed and you've sent me the confirmation.
skills.summary: Grok Bot researches options, prepares orders via Stripe Link and shows a spend request with merchant, total and description before paying; one example covered meal planning and grocery orders.

skills.name: Research buying a yak
skills.prompt: I'm thinking about buying [unusual item, e.g. a yak or a used boat]. Research where to buy one in [my region], typical prices, ongoing costs, and legal or logistical requirements. Summarize your findings in a one-page brief with sources, and stop once you have it; don't contact sellers or make any purchases.
skills.summary: Manus navigated sites, handled pop-ups and summarized findings, but took 15 minutes, used 300 credits, and needed manual takeover when stuck.

skills.name: Research purchases for delivered price and working coupons
skills.prompt: I want to buy [product]. Compare the full delivered price (including shipping and tax for [my zip code]) across [retailers or any major ones], try every coupon code you can find, and read owner reviews for common problems. Give me a table of the best deals with final prices and which coupons worked. Go through checkout to confirm the total, but stop before placing any order and show me what you see.
skills.summary: The poster built an agent that compares real delivered prices, tests every coupon it finds, reads owner feedback and goes through checkout without ordering.

skills.name: Run an online store's inventory, listings and photos
skills.prompt: Each week when I add a new inventory spreadsheet at [Google Sheet or file location], update prices and stock for my store on [Shopify, Etsy, or other platform]. Write original listing descriptions in [tone] for new items and flag any item where the data is unclear. Hold the flagged items and send me a summary at [email] for approval before publishing anything. Finish when all clear items are updated and the flagged list is delivered.
skills.summary: An agent takes a weekly inventory spreadsheet, updates prices and stock, writes original listings, redraws photos as studio shots, and holds uncertain items for approval.

skills.name: Scan Marketplace and handle errands with Meta Muse
skills.prompt: Scan Facebook Marketplace near [city] for [item type] under [price], and shortlist the five best listings based on price, photos, and described condition. For each, note any red flags and draft a polite offer message at about [percent] below asking. Show me the shortlist and drafts and wait for my approval before sending any message.
skills.summary: Commenters say they use Muse to build expense trackers, schedule meetings, send follow-up emails, and scan Facebook Marketplace for toys, negotiate, and check condition.

skills.name: Scan thrift store items and flag good deals
skills.prompt: I'll share photos or video frames from a thrift store. For each item you can identify, look up typical resale prices on [eBay, Etsy, or other sites] and tell me which ones are priced well below resale value. You are done when I have a ranked list of the best deals with the asking price, expected resale price, and your confidence for each.
skills.summary: An agent processes video frames from a thrift store, looks up online prices for items, and alerts the user to good deals.

skills.name: Schedule recurring restocking of household essentials
skills.prompt: Set up scheduled actions to add [household items, e.g. pet food, paper towels, detergent] to my cart every [frequency, e.g. month] on [day]. When done, list every recurring action you created with its schedule. Pause and show me the cart before placing any order.
skills.summary: Users create Scheduled Actions in Alexa for Shopping to add kids' snacks monthly and restock pet food, paper towels and detergent; vendor material.

skills.name: Search Facebook Marketplace and tabulate results in Sheets
skills.prompt: Search Facebook Marketplace near [city] for [item] under [price]. For the first [20] listings, record title, price, location, and link in a new Google Sheet. Finished means the sheet is filled and you tell me the top [3] deals. Do not message any sellers; show me the sheet first.
skills.summary: A user tries to have Claude in Chrome search Marketplace items and log them in a Google Sheet, but constant permission prompts get in the way.

skills.name: Sell your unused items online with an agent
skills.prompt: I want to sell [item, condition, and any flaws] on [marketplace, e.g. Facebook Marketplace or eBay]. Research comparable listings, suggest a price, and draft the listing with a title, description, and photo checklist. Pause and show me the listing before posting it, and show me every buyer reply and your suggested response before sending. Check in every [number] days with a summary and a suggested price drop if there are no sales, and stop when the item is sold or I say so.
skills.summary: The poster tested ChatGPT Agent Mode handling an online sale over about 10 days, including message handling and price nudges, with little hands-on work.

skills.name: Shop Etsy for party supplies within a budget
skills.prompt: Open Etsy and find party supplies for [type of party, e.g. a 6-year-old's dinosaur birthday] with a total budget of [amount]. Look for [items, e.g. banner, tableware, favors, balloons], add the best-value options to my cart, and try any available discount codes. Stop with the cart ready for me to review and do not check out or enter payment details. Show me the items, prices and total before I decide.
skills.summary: Chrome auto browse with Gemini searched Etsy, added items to the cart, applied discount codes and left the cart ready for the user to review.

skills.name: Shop for Raspberry Pi parts on Amazon with Claude
skills.prompt: Search Amazon for the parts I need to build [project, e.g. a Raspberry Pi voice assistant], including [main board] and accessories like [microphone, speaker, power supply, case]. Ask me about options and compatibility where it matters, then add your picks to my basket. Pause before checkout and show me the list with prices; do not buy anything.
skills.summary: Claude searched Amazon for a Raspberry Pi, asked about mic and speaker options, and added items to the basket in about 15 minutes, slower than manual.

skills.name: Shop for a shirt and place the order
skills.prompt: Find me a [item, e.g. white dress shirt] in size [size]. Compare [number] brands on sizing, return policy, shipping minimums, and price, and find the nearest store to [location] that has it. You are done when you've recommended one option and added it to the cart. Show me the cart and total and wait for my approval before placing the order.
skills.summary: An AI agent compared six brands on sizing, return policies, and shipping minimums, found the nearest store, picked a size, and ordered a white dress shirt.

skills.name: Shop for cars on websites with a browser agent
skills.prompt: Shop for a used [make/model/year range] near [city or zip] on [car sites], with a budget of [max price] and under [mileage] miles. Use a persistent logged-in browser profile and pace your clicks like a normal person so sites don't block you. Finish with a shortlist of 5 to 8 listings with price, mileage, and links; don't contact any seller or submit any forms without showing me first.
skills.summary: The poster uses Muse to shop for cars online and finds a persistent logged-in browser profile with normal pacing works best as sites start blocking it.

skills.name: Shop for shorts and handle email via an agent
skills.prompt: Find [item, e.g. running shorts] in size [size] in [color or style] under [price] from [two or three stores] and list the best options with price, reviews and links. Add the one I choose to the cart but stop before checkout, login or payment and show me the cart. Do not buy anything until I confirm.
skills.summary: A TechRadar reviewer had Muse find shorts in their size and request an Amazon login to buy, and also work on their email.

skills.name: Shop on Amazon and build pages with the Claude Chrome extension
skills.prompt: On Amazon, find [product] under [price] with at least [rating] stars, compare the top [number] options on price, reviews and delivery date, and give me a short ranked list with links. Add my pick to the cart if I choose one, but stop before checkout and show me the cart and total. Do not place any order without my confirmation.
skills.summary: A reviewer used the Claude Chrome extension for Amazon shopping, building an interactive model timeline from one prompt, and translating and summarizing pages; one screenshot bug appeared.

skills.name: Shop, play a game and compile course info with Operator
skills.prompt: Go to [shopping site] and find [item, e.g. dark straight-leg jeans] in [size] under [budget], and pick the 3 best-reviewed options. Show me each with price, rating and a link. Stop before adding anything to checkout or entering payment details.
skills.summary: Operator played a deepfake game scoring 6/10, shopped for jeans, and compiled information about online courses from the author's website.

skills.name: Test OpenAI's Agent on online shopping
skills.prompt: Find [item, e.g. black dress shoes in size X] under [$budget] on [retailer other than Amazon] and add the best match to the cart. Tell me your top [3] options with prices and links. Pause before entering any payment details or placing the order, and show me the cart so I can finish checkout myself.
skills.summary: The agent got partway through buying dress shoes before the poster had to enter the card, then hit Amazon bot protection and could not reliably shop, book or reserve.

skills.name: Track competitor prices weekly across five sites
skills.prompt: Every Monday at [time], visit these sites: [list of five URLs] and record the prices for [products or categories]. Compare them to last week's snapshot stored in [spreadsheet or doc], and take timestamped screenshots of anything that changed. You are done when a report of the changes is sent to [my email or Slack channel].
skills.summary: An agent opens five brand sites every Monday, compares against last week's snapshot, captures timestamped screenshots of changes, and sends a report.

skills.name: Track daily price and stock changes on Shopify stores
skills.prompt: Write a small script that reads the public products feed of [store URL, e.g. store.com/products.json] each day and saves a snapshot. Compare each day to the previous one and report new products, removed products, price changes and stock changes in a short summary. Run it once now to create the first snapshot and show me the product count, then set it up to run daily at [time].
skills.summary: An agent reads a Shopify store's public product feed daily and reports new, removed, price and stock changes, e.g. 692 products at allbirds.com.

skills.name: Track pantry stock from receipts and buy groceries
skills.prompt: In the folder [path to receipts] I have grocery receipts. Read them, build a running estimate of what's in my kitchen, and save it as [pantry file name]. Then list what I'm likely low on, suggest [number] recipes using what I have, and prepare a shopping list. You are done when the pantry file and shopping list exist; don't buy anything without showing me the list first.
skills.summary: A custom AI system reads receipts, estimates kitchen stock, checks grocery store availability and prices, buys groceries, and suggests recipes.

skills.name: Track rare coffee beans with a scheduled Dot
skills.prompt: Twice a day, at [times], check [list of roulette retailers or sites] for [type of product, e.g. rare coffee beans like Gesha] available in [country], within a budget of [price per unit or cup]. Send me a short message only when there is something new, listing name, seller, price and link. Don't buy anything; pause and show me the details before any purchase step.
skills.summary: A user had a Dot monitor rare US coffee beans twice a day using context from old chats, and it returned Gesha options priced per cup.

skills.name: Turn a handwritten grocery list into a cart
skills.prompt: I'm attaching a photo of my handwritten grocery list. Transcribe it into a typed list and show it to me so I can check for anything missed. Then find the nearest [store] to [my location or zip code] and add every item to the cart. Stop before checkout and show me the cart, any items you could not find and the total, and wait for my approval before ordering.
skills.summary: ChatGPT Agent transcribed 15 of 16 items from a photo, found the nearest store and added them to the cart, but missed onions and struggled with login.

skills.name: Turn a handwritten list into a grocery order
skills.prompt: I'm going to scan my handwritten shopping list. Read it, match each item to products from [Amazon Fresh or Whole Foods], and build a cart using my past purchases and preferences [e.g. dietary needs] where possible. Flag anything unclear, then pause and show me the full cart, total and delivery window before placing the order.
skills.summary: A TechRadar writer scans a handwritten shopping list into Alexa and places an Amazon Fresh or Whole Foods order from it to avoid crowded stores.

skills.name: Use Operator to book tables, compare products and fill forms
skills.prompt: Help me with this web errand: [book a table for 2 at a restaurant in [city] on [date] at [time] / compare [product type] under [budget] / fill out the form at [website]]. Do the browsing and form-filling for me, and finish with a short summary of what you found or filled in. Pause and show me everything before you submit any form, confirm a booking, or pay, and ask me to log in myself if a login is needed.
skills.summary: The poster tested Operator on web tasks including booking a table, comparing products, filling forms, navigating sites and logging into services.

skills.name: Watch item prices and email on drops
skills.prompt: Set up a recurring price watch on these items: [product links or names] at [retailers]. Check [daily/weekly] and email me at [email] only when the price drops below [target price] or falls by more than [percent]. Don't buy anything; just tell me what you set up and confirm the first price you found for each item.
skills.summary: A commenter set up a ChatGPT price watch on items they want and gets an email only when the price drops.

skills.name: Watch weekly deals and buy regular items
skills.prompt: Each week, watch deals on these items I buy regularly: [list of products] at [stores]. When one is at or below [target price], add it to the cart using my shipping details and the best available discount code. Pause and show me the cart and total before you pay, then after I approve, save the order confirmation and tracking number and tell me when it ships.
skills.summary: One Grok Bot watches deals on regularly bought products, another purchases in a browser with shipping details and discount codes, then reads order confirmations and tracking.

skills.name: Add a filtered report page to a Razor Pages app
skills.prompt: In my [framework, e.g. Razor Pages] app, add a new report page called [report name] that summarizes [data, e.g. charges] and lets me filter by [filters, e.g. date range and status]. Add a menu link to it, follow the existing patterns in the project, and make sure it builds. When you finish, list the files you changed and give me the git commands to commit the work with a clear message.
skills.summary: The poster used Copilot agent mode in Visual Studio 2022 to build a charges summary report page with date and status filters, add a menu option, and write the git commit steps.

skills.name: Add a third-party API integration via Devin PR
skills.prompt: In the repo [repo URL], add an integration with [third-party API] including the endpoint, backend wiring, and config for the API key via [env var or secrets approach]. Follow the existing code style and abstractions in [folder or file] and add tests. Open a pull request listing what you changed and any assumptions, and stop there without merging.
skills.summary: Devin opened a PR with the endpoint and backend wiring that was merged, but missed API key logic, code style and abstraction, needing review fixes.

skills.name: Add agentic forgetting to an agent's memory
skills.prompt: Look at how my agent stores memory in [path or project]. Add a simple forgetting mechanism: give each memory a last-used time and relevance score, and have a scheduled pass archive or delete low-value, stale entries. Write tests showing old unused memories get dropped while frequently used ones stay. Before deleting anything real, show me the list of what would be removed.
skills.summary: Someone implemented a rudimentary version of Tim Kellogg's agentic forgetting approach and reports it works impressively even in its simplest form.

skills.name: Assign GitHub issues to Copilot coding agent
skills.prompt: Assign this GitHub issue to the Copilot coding agent: [issue link]. Before it starts, make sure it works from the [feature branch name] branch and not the default branch, and put that in the task instructions. When it finishes, give me a pull request against [feature branch name] with a short summary of what changed, and don't merge anything until I've reviewed it.
skills.summary: A developer assigned a GitHub issue to Copilot and watched it work, but it started from the default branch instead of the intended feature branch.

skills.name: Assign website tweaks to Copilot coding agent
skills.prompt: In my repo [owner/repo], I'm going to assign you two small website changes: [change 1, e.g. tighten the spacing in the header] and [change 2]. For each one, open a separate draft pull request with a short description of what you changed and why. Don't merge anything; stop once both draft PRs are open and tell me what to review.
skills.summary: An author gave the Copilot coding agent two small changes on their own site; it opened draft PRs and the spacing change was good enough to merge.

skills.name: Attempt to build a navigation app (did not finish)
skills.prompt: I want to build a simple navigation app for [platform] that does [core feature, e.g. route from A to B with turn-by-turn directions] using [map service]. Begin with the smallest working version, test it, and show me what runs before adding anything more. Stop and check with me after each milestone, and tell me before spending a large amount of credits.
skills.summary: A poster tried to build a navigation app with Manus but spent a month of credits and over 8 hours without a working app.

skills.name: Audit a codebase for redundant dependencies and polyfills
skills.prompt: Audit the project at [path to repo] for redundant dependencies and unnecessary polyfills, such as packages that can be replaced by built-in features in [runtime and version, e.g. Node 20]. Produce a report listing each one, why it's redundant, and the suggested replacement. Don't edit package files or install anything until I've reviewed the report.
skills.summary: An MCP server lets an agent check a codebase for redundant dependencies and polyfills, usable remotely or as a local stdio server.

skills.name: Audit a feature's issues and hand them to an engineer's agent
skills.prompt: Review the [feature name] feature in this repo and list every issue you find: bugs, missing edge cases, unclear UX, and test gaps. Write each as a separate issue with a title, steps to reproduce, and suggested fix, and sort them by severity. Stop once the list is complete, and show it to me before filing anything in [issue tracker] or messaging [engineer name].
skills.summary: An AI agent listed all issues with a feature and sent them to an engineer, whose own agent then addressed most of them automatically.

skills.name: Audit hundreds of pull requests with a terminal coding agent
skills.prompt: Using the GitHub CLI, audit the open pull requests in [owner/repo]. For each one, summarize what it changes, flag stale, duplicate, or risky PRs, and give a suggested action. Only reference things you can verify exist in the repo, and say so when you are unsure. Finish with a ranked summary table and do not comment on, merge, or close anything without showing me first.
skills.summary: In an independent test, Muse Code audited 222 pull requests in under five minutes for about ten cents, but also built a plan on a Google project that doesn't exist.

skills.name: Auto-generate a searchable help video library for an app
skills.prompt: Add a /help page to my app [app name or URL] that automatically generates short tutorial videos for [list of features or flows]. For each, write a scene script, record the steps with Playwright, add text-to-speech narration, and stitch the video with ffmpeg. Finish with a searchable library of the videos on the page and show me one working example before generating the rest.
skills.summary: Used Replit Agent to build a /help page that generates tutorial videos via scenes, Playwright recording, TTS narration and ffmpeg stitching.

skills.name: Auto-open fix PRs from Sentry and log alerts
skills.prompt: Monitor [Sentry project] and [log source] for errors matching [trigger conditions]. When one fires, find the likely cause in [repo list] and open a draft PR with a fix and a clear explanation. Never merge anything yourself, and post each PR link to [Slack channel].
skills.summary: A Grok Bot called Sentinel monitors Sentry and logs and opens PRs on several repositories when triggers fire; still very early.

skills.name: Auto-pull proven skills for Cursor on an analytics dashboard
skills.prompt: In my [analytics dashboard] repo, review the event store design, instrumentation, and API security. Add rate limiting and input validation to [API endpoints], and suggest any schema or tracking improvements. Show me a summary of every change as a diff, and run the existing tests to confirm nothing broke before you finish.
skills.summary: On their analytics dashboard, Cursor's agent pulled in skills for event-store design, instrumentation and API security, adding rate limiting and input validation.

skills.name: Automate web configuration from coding sessions
skills.prompt: I'm coding [project] and need this web setup done in [service, e.g. DNS provider or cloud console]: [configuration steps]. Open the site in my logged-in browser and make the changes, then give me the values to paste into my code. Finished means the setup works and you've listed each change made. Pause before saving or deleting anything.
skills.summary: Commenters use Claude in Chrome to carry out web configuration requests that arise from coding sessions and other browser operations.

skills.name: Autonomously test an entire iOS app and report bugs
skills.prompt: Run my iOS app from [project path] in the simulator and drive it through the accessibility tree, tapping through every reachable screen. Report bugs as a structured list with screen, steps to reproduce, expected versus actual behavior, and severity. Stop once every screen has been visited, and don't modify any code.
skills.summary: A tool lets Claude Code drive an iOS app through the accessibility tree, tap every screen, and return a structured bug summary.

skills.name: Break development work into phases for Copilot
skills.prompt: I'm building [project description]. Break the work into [number] phases with explicit tasks in each, and show me the plan first. Then do only Phase 1, stop, and summarize what you did so I can review it before we start the next phase.
skills.summary: The poster splits work into phases with explicit tasks so Copilot's agent works through development steps instead of everything at once.

skills.name: Build SQLite with a swarm of parallel coding agents
skills.prompt: I want to build a small [project, e.g. SQLite-style database engine] in [language] using several parallel agents. First write a spec that splits the work into independent modules ([e.g. parser, storage, query executor]), then run one sub-agent per module in separate worktrees with tests for each. Stop when the modules are merged and a test suite of [number] basic queries passes, and show me what failed along the way.
skills.summary: The author recounts using parallel coding agents to build a SQLite implementation and shares experience from it.

skills.name: Build a C compiler with a team of parallel agents
skills.prompt: I want to build a small [tool, e.g. a Markdown-to-HTML converter in Python] from scratch with a spec-first approach. First write a short spec and a test suite in this folder, then split the work into independent pieces and use sub-agents to implement them in parallel. Stop when all tests pass, and give me a summary of what each sub-agent built and any tests you had to skip.
skills.summary: Anthropic's engineering write-up on tasking Opus 4.6 agent teams with building a C compiler.

skills.name: Build a Chrome extension for presenting webinars
skills.prompt: Build me a Chrome extension that shows my [speaker notes / talking points] in a small always-visible panel while I present [webinars or screen-share talks]. I should be able to paste in and edit notes, and resize or move the panel. You're done when I can load the extension locally in Chrome and see my notes on a test page, then walk me through the steps to publish it to the Chrome Web Store without submitting anything yet.
skills.summary: A Replit forum user built a Chrome extension so they could keep notes in view while presenting webinars, and published it to the Chrome Web Store.

skills.name: Build a Pokemon-style dog collecting app
skills.prompt: Build a catch-em-all style app for [topic, e.g. dog breeds] where rarity is based on real data from [source website, e.g. regional population or registration stats]. Scrape or import the data, let users collect items and view their collection, and deploy it. Finish when the app is live and rarity tiers are visibly tied to the data.
skills.summary: A user had Replit Agent build a catch-em-all dog app whose rarity comes from scraped American Kennel Club regional population data.

skills.name: Build a Pong game and website from scratch
