skills.summary: The author set up a rack-mounted Fairphone 6 so their agent can use it through ADB.

skills.name: Give coding agents compiler-accurate Find Usages for C#
skills.prompt: In my C# solution at [path], find every usage of [class or method name], including interface implementations and overrides, using the compiler's semantic info (for example Roslyn) rather than text search. Give me a list of file and line for each usage, grouped by project. Do not edit any files; stop once the list is complete and tell me how you verified it was accurate.
skills.summary: Graphify C# lets coding agents find symbol usages in C# codebases with compiler-level accuracy.

skills.name: Give coding agents git-native persistent memory
skills.prompt: Set up persistent memory for coding agents in this repository by storing notes in a [folder name, e.g. .agent-memory] directory tracked in git. Create a simple format for recording decisions, conventions, and open tasks, and add instructions so future sessions read it first and update it at the end. Show me the files you plan to commit before you commit anything.
skills.summary: A tool that stores persistent memory for AI coding agents in git so context carries across sessions.

skills.name: Hand narrow code changes to Devin for pull requests
skills.prompt: In the repo [repo URL], fix [small, well-defined issue, e.g. chart axis formatting or an API edge case with null input]. Add or update tests, make sure they pass, and open a pull request with a clear description of the change. Keep the scope narrow and don't refactor unrelated code; stop and ask me if the task looks bigger than described.
skills.summary: A team used Devin for a month on small fixes like chart formatting and API edge cases, with tests and PRs; a complex full-stack task went poorly.

skills.name: Hand off coding sessions between agent accounts at usage limits
skills.prompt: Build me a small local tool that tracks usage across my [number] Codex and Claude Code accounts and warns me when one is close to its limit. When an account hits its limit, it should save a summary of the current session (task, files touched, next steps) so I can paste it into another account and continue. Done means I can run it, see usage per account, and generate a handoff note; show me the plan before it touches any credentials or config files.
skills.summary: A developer built an app that tracks usage across multiple Codex and Claude Code accounts and auto-hands-off conversations when one hits its limit.

skills.name: Hand off coding sessions from local CLI to Devin
skills.prompt: I'm working in [repo name] on [task description]. Start by exploring the repo to understand the structure, the relevant files and the conventions, and summarize what you learned. Then continue the task independently and open a pull request, pausing to show me the diff before you push or open it.
skills.summary: The poster starts in Devin CLI so it explores the repo and builds context, then hands the session off to continue independently.

skills.name: Have Claude read GitHub code and post drafts
skills.prompt: Read the code in [GitHub repo or local folder] and draft [content, e.g. a README update, release notes, or a post] based on what it does. Save the draft to [file or location] so I can review it. Don't post or publish anything, and don't edit other files, until I approve.
skills.summary: A commenter lets Claude read code from GitHub and post drafts for them, and uses Claude Code in the desktop app for file editing and running commands.

skills.name: Have Copilot coding agent write and push code
skills.prompt: In [owner/repo], implement [feature or task]. Work on a new branch named [branch-name], not main, and before pushing anything, show me the branch you'll push to and a summary of the changes. Once I approve, push and open a pull request, then stop and tell me what you pushed and where.
skills.summary: A developer found the agent good at context and code, but it pushed to a branch leaving main empty and spent hours checking after being told to proceed.

skills.name: Have Copilot write all of a day's pushed code
skills.prompt: Help me implement [feature or fix] in my [repo/project] using Copilot for every code change. Work in small steps, and after each step list the files you touched and what changed so I can review the diff before moving on. Flag any change that alters existing behavior rather than just adding to it, and finish when [the feature works and tests pass].
skills.summary: A commenter had Copilot write every line pushed in a day; it mostly worked but one wrong change needed human review.

skills.name: Have a coding agent build and deploy n8n workflows
skills.prompt: I run n8n at [n8n URL] and want you to build a workflow that [describe the job, e.g. sends a Slack summary of new support tickets each morning]. Write any scripts and configs needed, then deploy the workflow through n8n's REST API using my API key in [env variable]. Deploy it inactive first and show me the workflow before activating. Finish with a test run and a short explanation of how it works.
skills.summary: The poster has an AI agent write the workflow, scripts and configs and deploy them through n8n's REST API instead of building nodes by hand.

skills.name: Investigate broken builds and merge fixes
skills.prompt: Our build on [repo/branch] is broken. Check recent commits, PRs, and the CI logs at [log URL] to find the cause and the change that introduced it. Write up what you found, and if the fix is small, prepare it as a PR. Show me the diff before opening or merging anything.
skills.summary: OpenAI's internal OpenClaw agent Androidclaw uses Git, GitHub and logs to investigate broken builds, trace problems to incidents, and sometimes prepare and merge fixes.

skills.name: Iterate on app projects while Claude handles change requests
skills.prompt: I'm working on [project type, e.g. a text editor] built with [language or framework]. Here is the current code: [paste code]. Please make these changes: [list of change requests]. Return the updated code with a short summary of what changed so I can test it.
skills.summary: The poster has Claude make change requests on ongoing projects, including a video editor, a graphic adventure game engine and a text editor, while testing in the meantime.

skills.name: Iterate on tasks with Copilot CLI autopilot and fleet
skills.prompt: Using Copilot CLI in [repo path], work on [task] in autopilot mode and keep iterating until [definition of done, e.g. all tests pass]. If the task has clearly separate parts, such as [part A] and [part B], use /fleet to split them across parallel subagents; otherwise stay with a single agent. When you finish, summarize what was done and flag anything you weren't sure about.
skills.summary: The author used autopilot to iterate until done and /fleet to split work across parallel subagents, noting overhead on small tasks.

skills.name: Keep coding agents running autonomously for long stretches
skills.prompt: I want a background agent to work on [large task, e.g. migrating all API handlers to the new validation library] in my repo [repo] for an extended stretch. Break it into small checkable steps, work through them one by one, run tests after each, and commit after each step that passes. Stop when all handlers are done or after [number, e.g. 3] consecutive failures, and leave me a progress log.
skills.summary: Cursor's write-up on scaling long-running autonomous coding.

skills.name: Let Claude Code run a Chrome extension project
skills.prompt: Act as the CEO of my project [project name], a free [type of tool], for the next week. Look at the current state in [folder or repo] and propose three priorities for the week with reasons. Then build the first one in the code and write a short update on what changed. Anything public, like a post, a release, or a rename, needs my approval first, so show me the draft and wait.
skills.summary: The author gave Claude Code the CEO role for a free Chrome extension. In week one it had him rename it and built the next version, but it still needs his approval before each post.

skills.name: Let Copilot Agent Mode handle coding, then constrain it
skills.prompt: In my [language/framework] project, use agent mode only for [one narrow task, e.g. writing unit tests for the utils folder]. Don't change files outside [folder or file names]. After each change, explain in plain language what you did and why, so I can follow the code, and stop when [the task is complete, e.g. all tests pass].
skills.summary: A developer let Copilot Agent Mode do all the coding, found they understood their code less, and moved to using it more narrowly.

skills.name: Let Copilot agent mode iterate on involved coding tasks
skills.prompt: In agent mode, complete this task in my [repo]: [describe the task]. Pick the files you need, run the commands to build and test, and keep iterating on any failures until [tests pass or the feature works]. Don't touch [files or folders to avoid], and give me a summary of every file you changed at the end.
skills.summary: A commenter uses Copilot agent mode to pick files, run commands, and iterate until involved coding work is done.

skills.name: Let a custom agent change its own repository
skills.prompt: My agent project lives in the repo at [path to repo]. Add a way for the agent to propose and make a small change to its own code, such as [small improvement, e.g. add a new tool or fix a typo], on a separate branch with tests run first. Finish when it has produced one commit on that branch, and don't merge or push until I've reviewed the diff.
skills.summary: Author's custom-built agent made its first code change to its own repository.

skills.name: Let an agent extend its own code inside a Docker sandbox
skills.prompt: Help me set up a Docker sandbox where an agent can add new capabilities to its own source code in [repo path]. Each change should run the tests, be committed if they pass, and be rolled back if they fail, with a log of what happened. Finish by having it add [first capability, e.g. a web search tool] and show me the commit and test results; pause before any change that touches files outside the sandbox.
skills.summary: An agent built on Claude and Agno implements capabilities in its own source code in Docker, with changes validated, committed, or rolled back; it reached 21+ capabilities.

skills.name: Let terminal agents make phone calls
skills.prompt: In my project at [folder path], build a small command-line tool using Twilio that lets a terminal agent place a phone call, say a scripted purpose like [reason for call], and record the conversation outcome. Add a simple local dashboard where I can see and answer questions the agent couldn't handle. Include a dry-run mode that prints the call instead of placing it, and test with that before any real call.
skills.summary: A CLI tool built on Twilio gives terminal agents a voice to make calls, with a dashboard for questions they can't answer.

skills.name: Lint, fix, commit and push code from the terminal
skills.prompt: In my project at [path to repo], run [linter command] and fix any errors it reports, then re-run it until it passes. Review the staged changes and draft a clear commit message, then pause and show me the diff and message before you commit. After I approve, commit and push to a new branch named [branch name].
skills.summary: Scout runs a linter, fixes a syntax error, re-runs it, reviews staged changes, writes a commit message and pushes to a new branch, shown as a walkthrough.

skills.name: Maintain a profitable Stripe-backed app with Replit
skills.prompt: Review my existing app [app name or project] and look for duplicated code, messy organization and security gaps, such as missing bot protection on forms like reCAPTCHA. Give me a prioritized list of proposed fixes first. Then make the changes I approve and confirm that checkout and the other core flows still work. Do not touch payment settings or live data without asking me.
skills.summary: A commenter's Replit-built app reached about £20k in sales, and they use the agent to hunt duplications, organize code and add security like reCAPTCHA.

skills.name: Manage Canvas courses in plain English
skills.prompt: Build me a small tool that connects to [LMS, e.g. Canvas] using my API token stored in [environment variable] so I can manage my courses in plain English. It should be able to list my courses, find students with missing submissions in [course], and export the gradebook to CSV. Test it with read-only actions first, and before it schedules or posts any announcement, show me the text and ask for my confirmation.
skills.summary: The author built a Canvas LMS tool with Claude Code that lets educators list courses, find missing submissions, monitor forums, schedule announcements and export the gradebook.

skills.name: Manage NixOS server configs with Claude Code
skills.prompt: Help me maintain the NixOS config repo at [path to repo] for my machines [machine names]. Make this change: [describe change, such as adding a service or updating a package]. You may edit files and run dry builds, but never run nixos-rebuild switch. Show me the full diff and a plain-language explanation so I can review and apply it myself.
skills.summary: The author uses Claude Code to maintain the NixOS config repo for their self-hosted machines, blocked from running nixos-rebuild switch and reviewing each change before applying it manually.

skills.name: Manage several websites across WordPress, Astro and Eleventy
skills.prompt: Look at the site projects in [folder paths] built with [WordPress, Astro, Eleventy, etc.] and do [task, such as update dependencies, fix broken links, or add a new page]. Work on one site at a time and run each site's build to confirm it still works. Summarize what changed per site, and ask me before deploying, pushing to production, or deleting anything.
skills.summary: The poster uses OpenClaw, alongside Claude Code and Codex, to manage and work across about five websites.

skills.name: Migrate 180 microservices to a new framework version
skills.prompt: Write a self-correcting migration agent that updates [list of services/repos] from [old framework version] to [new framework version], running build and tests after each change and fixing failures automatically. Have it report progress per service and pause before opening any pull requests for my review.
skills.summary: Brex built Cursor-based self-correcting agents that let one engineer migrate 180 microservices to a newer Micronaut version in about a month.

skills.name: Migrate WordPress posts to MDX
skills.prompt: Pull all posts and pages from my WordPress site at [site URL] using the REST API and convert each one to an MDX file with frontmatter (title, date, slug, tags, [other fields]). Save them in [folder path] in my project. Finish by giving me a count of posts and pages converted and a list of any that had formatting problems you couldn't fix cleanly.
skills.summary: Claude Code pulled posts from the WordPress REST API and converted them to MDX with frontmatter, migrating 367 posts and 5 pages in one session.

skills.name: Migrate a SaaS from AWS to DigitalOcean
skills.prompt: Act as my pair programmer to migrate my app from [current host, e.g. AWS] to [new host, e.g. DigitalOcean]. First inspect the repo and write a step-by-step plan covering provisioning, database migration, SSL, DNS cutover, and rollback. Work through it with me one step at a time, and pause and show me the command or change before anything that touches production, DNS, or deletes data.
skills.summary: A developer used Claude Code as a pair programmer for provisioning, database seeding, SSL, DNS cutover and production debugging, finishing in about four hours with zero downtime by his account.

skills.name: Migrate a large web application with Copilot Agents
skills.prompt: I need to migrate my web application in [repo name] from [current framework or version] to [target framework or version]. Start by scanning the codebase and writing a step-by-step migration plan that groups the work into small chunks, then complete the first chunk on a new branch and open a pull request. Stop after that first PR with a list of remaining steps and any risky areas you found, and wait for my go-ahead before starting the next chunk.
skills.summary: A developer found Copilot Chat struggled with a large web app migration, so switched to Copilot Agents, which handled the codebase better; the migration was still early.

skills.name: Migrate a legacy product stack with Claude Code
skills.prompt: I want a proof-of-concept migration of [legacy product] from [current stack, e.g. 4 repos, MySQL, old framework version] to [target stack, e.g. 2 repos, PostgreSQL, current framework]. Start by reading the codebases and writing a phased migration plan with risks, then execute the first phase on a new branch with tests passing. Pause for my review before merging anything or running changes against any real database.
skills.summary: An engineer ran a proof-of-concept that consolidated 4 repos into 2, moved MySQL to PostgreSQL, upgraded frameworks and replaced the auth model, in about 15 work days.

skills.name: Migrate a password reset flow to modern libraries
skills.prompt: In this repo, migrate the password reset flow in [path or module] from [legacy library or approach] to [modern library]. First write a short plan and list the files you intend to touch, then wait for my approval. Keep changes limited to the reset flow, run the existing tests after each step, and stop when the tests pass and you have summarized the diff. Pause and ask before deleting any files or changing unrelated code.
skills.summary: A developer had Claude Code migrate a legacy web app's password reset flow; it needed close supervision, drifted off task, and ended up slower than doing it by hand.

skills.name: Migrate a website from a CMS to raw code and Markdown
skills.prompt: I want to move my website at [repo or folder] off [CMS name] and into plain code with Markdown files for content. First export the existing content from [CMS or export location], then use subagents to convert pages and posts into Markdown and update the templates and routes to read from those files. Finished means the site builds locally, the pages match the originals, and you give me a list of anything you could not migrate. Show me the plan before you delete any CMS code or integrations.
skills.summary: Lee Robinson used Cursor agents to move cursor.com off its CMS in three days for $260 in tokens, with subagents handling a broad refactor.

skills.name: Migrate an Electron app from Vue 2 to Vue 3
skills.prompt: I'm giving you access to my [repo name], an Electron app built on Vue 2. Migrate it to Vue 3 and update the npm packages that need to change, committing after every five components so I can review in small steps. Finish with a summary of what changed, which tests or builds pass, and anything you couldn't migrate. Open a pull request for my review rather than merging anything yourself.
skills.summary: Kearney gave Devin repo access to migrate a production Electron app to Vue 3 and update npm packages, committing after every five components.

skills.name: Migrate toolchain, architecture and site design with Claude Code
skills.prompt: In my repo at [path], switch the linting and formatting toolchain to [e.g. oxlint and oxfmt], and fix everything that breaks. Run the build, tests, and lint after each change and loop until they all pass. Work on a separate branch, summarize what you changed, and stop when everything is green without merging.
skills.summary: A developer had Claude Code switch a monorepo to oxlint/oxfmt, restructure the architecture and redesign a site, validating in a loop; the redesign took days instead of weeks.

skills.name: Monitor and organize multiple coding agents in one terminal
skills.prompt: Help me set up a terminal workflow to run and monitor several coding agents at once in my project at [project path]. Create a separate git worktree for each of these tasks: [task 1], [task 2], [task 3], start an agent session in each, and give me a single script or tmux layout that shows which worktree each agent is working in and its current status. You're done when I can start the layout with one command and see all sessions side by side; pause and show me before deleting any worktree or branch.
skills.summary: Corgi is a terminal multiplexer that shows what each coding agent is doing and launches Codex/Claude Code sessions, reusing the agents to label links and worktrees.

skills.name: Monitor tasks and open pull requests with long-running agents
skills.prompt: In my repo [repo name], read the open tasks in [issue tracker or task file] and for the one I pick, make the code change on a new branch, run the tests, and open a pull request with a clear description. Start by listing the tasks you could handle and wait for my choice, and do not merge anything. Finish when the pull request is open and tests pass.
skills.summary: A commenter runs a persistent script that watches tasks and uses Cursor to open pull requests, building a documentation summarizer and a data pipeline.

skills.name: One-shot a CLI coding agent on top of a Python LLM library
skills.prompt: Using [Python LLM library, e.g. Simon Willison's llm] as a base, build a CLI coding agent that can read files, edit files and run shell commands in the current directory. Keep it to a single script with a clear README and a confirmation prompt before any command that writes or deletes. Finish by running it on a small demo task in [scratch folder] and showing me the transcript.
skills.summary: Simon Willison had the Fable model more or less one-shot a CLI coding agent built on his LLM Python library.

skills.name: Optimize CUDA kernels with agents that benchmark and profile
skills.prompt: Optimize the CUDA kernel in [file path] for [operation, e.g. matrix multiply]. Build a test harness that checks correctness, benchmark the baseline, profile it with Nsight, and try improvements one at a time, keeping only those that pass the correctness check. Stop when you have a faster version and a table of each change with its speedup.
skills.summary: AI agents run a C++ CUDA test harness, get benchmarks, and profile with Nsight to optimize kernels, built with LangGraph.

skills.name: Orchestrate a multi-phase RAG migration
skills.prompt: I'm migrating [system, e.g. my search and RAG pipeline] from [current setup] to [target cloud service]. Read the codebase in this folder and break the migration into phases with clear checkpoints, risks, and rollback steps. Finish with a written plan in MIGRATION.md; don't change any code or run any cloud commands until I approve each phase.
skills.summary: A walkthrough of using Gemini CLI to coordinate a complex, multi-phase cloud migration project.

skills.name: Pair-program with LLMs on personal projects
skills.prompt: Act as my pair-programming partner on my project at [path to repo]. I want to [describe the feature or fix]. Start by suggesting a short plan and the files you'd touch, then work in small steps on a new branch, explaining each change. Stop when the change works and tests pass, and show me the diff before committing or pushing anything.
skills.summary: The author uses Claude web and Jules (Gemini with GitHub integration) as pair-programming partners, navigating while coding locally and submitting back.

skills.name: Patch annoying software behavior by pointing an agent at it
skills.prompt: There is a behavior in [app or tool name] that annoys me: [describe the bug or missing feature]. Look at the source or install files at [path or repo], find where it comes from, and propose a small patch or hook to fix it. Show me the diff and explain how to test it before changing any files, and stop once the fix works and I can undo it.
skills.summary: Author had an agent debug a Hyper-V vmconnect fullscreen bug with a hook system, and pointed Codex at the Codex app to add features.

skills.name: Plan with PRDs and delegate tasks to cheaper agents
skills.prompt: I want to build [feature or project] in [repo path]. First write a short PRD covering goals, scope, and acceptance criteria, then split it into small, independent tasks in a TASKS.md file with clear done criteria for each. Stop and show me the PRD and task list so I can review it before anything is implemented, so I can hand the tasks to a cheaper model.
skills.summary: A developer uses a high-level agent to write a PRD, splits it into a task list, and hands the work to cheaper agents in a production workflow.

skills.name: Point a computer-using bot at any repo
skills.prompt: Use your computer and browser to work on this repository: [repo URL]. Your task is [bug, feature, or cleanup description]. Clone it, set it up, make the change on a new branch, run the tests, and summarize what you did. Pause and show me the diff before pushing or opening a pull request, and stop when the branch is ready for my review.
skills.summary: A commenter says Grok Bot can use a computer and browser and be told to work on any given repo, unlike a repo-specific cloud agent.

skills.name: Port Claude Code hooks to pi extensions
skills.prompt: Read the hooks in my folder [path to .claude/hooks or settings] and rebuild each one as an extension for [new agent or tool name], following its extension docs at [docs URL]. Keep the same behavior for each hook and write a short test or example run for each. Stop when every hook has an equivalent, and list any that can't be ported exactly.
skills.summary: After leaving Claude, the author pointed an agent at their Claude hooks folder and had it rebuild them as a pi extension, which it did quickly.

skills.name: Port Claude Code skills to Codex
skills.prompt: I have a set of Claude Code skills in [folder path]. Convert them to work with Codex, putting the results in [destination folder], and keep the originals untouched. When done, give me a list of which skills transferred cleanly and which broke or need manual fixes, with the reason for each.
skills.summary: The author moved 201 Claude Code skills to Codex in an afternoon using a skill inside Claude Code, and reports what transferred and what broke.

skills.name: Port a Chrome extension to Safari
skills.prompt: I want to port the Chrome extension [extension name] to [Safari or another browser]. Here is the source code or repo link: [paste or link]. Convert it, list any APIs that don't work in the new browser and how you handled them, and give me step-by-step instructions to build and install it locally. You're done when I can load it and the main features work; tell me before changing anything that affects my data.
skills.summary: The author had ChatGPT take the Session Buddy extension source from Chrome, port it to Safari and install it, taking about 20 minutes.

skills.name: Port the Copilot runtime to Rust agentically
skills.prompt: I want to port [component or module] in [repo path] from [source language] to Rust using an agentic workflow. Start by reading the code and proposing a phased porting plan with test checkpoints, and wait for my approval. Then port one module at a time, keeping the existing tests passing, and finish with a summary of what's ported, what's left, and an estimate of effort.
skills.summary: Microsoft reportedly used agents to port its Copilot runtime to Rust for $120K, according to the headline.

skills.name: Prototype product features as a non-coding PM
skills.prompt: I'm not a developer. Look through my prototype in [repo or folder] and list what's missing for a working version of [feature idea]. Draw ASCII wireframes of the screens, then write a step-by-step plan and implement it, using parallel agents in separate worktrees if it helps. You're done when I can run the feature locally and you've explained in plain language how to try it. Show me the plan and wait for my approval before changing any code.
skills.summary: A founder used Cursor agents to find prototype gaps, draw ASCII wireframes, and plan and implement a feature with parallel agents in worktrees.

skills.name: Publish four Android apps to Google Play built with Replit
skills.prompt: Help me turn my [app name] project into an Android app ready for Google Play. Write the GitHub Actions workflow YAML files to build a signed release bundle, and explain which secrets and store listing details I need to supply. Don't publish or submit anything without showing me first. You're done when a workflow run produces a build I can upload.
skills.summary: A user built four apps with Replit and published them to Google Play, with Replit writing the GitHub workflow YAML files for builds.

skills.name: Queue maintenance and bug fixes for Cursor background agents
skills.prompt: Using the GitHub repo [owner/repo], start background agents for each item in this queue: [bug 1], [maintenance task], [small feature]. For each one, clone into a sandbox, create a separate branch, make the change, run the tests, and open a draft pull request describing what changed. Stop when every item has a draft PR, and do not merge any of them.
skills.summary: A developer authorized the GitHub app so Cursor background agents cloned repos into sandboxes, branched, and worked through a day's queue of maintenance, features and bug fixes.

skills.name: Rebuild a platform and add RAG features in one day
skills.prompt: Take my existing app at [project link or name] and add these features: [feature 1], [feature 2], [feature 3]. Keep current behavior working, test each feature after adding it, and tell me what changed. Pause and show me the plan before you modify the database or deploy to the live version.
skills.summary: A user had Replit Agent rebuild a full-stack platform, add 7 features to a live RAG app, and make a demo video in about 12 hours.

skills.name: Recompile a 1991 assembly PC game with Claude Code
skills.prompt: I have the source code of an old [language, e.g. 386 assembly] project at [path to folder] that I last built in [year]. Work out which assembler, linker and tools it needs, set up a way to build it on my [OS], and fix errors until it compiles and runs. Explain each change you make, and ask me before you delete or overwrite any original files.
skills.summary: The author uses Claude Code CLI with Sonnet to get the source of their 1991 386+ assembly game compiling again.

skills.name: Redesign an admin feature with multiple design options
skills.prompt: In my codebase at [repo path], redesign the [admin feature name] screen. Produce five distinct design options, each in its own file or branch under [folder], with a short note on the tradeoffs of each. Don't touch the existing implementation. You're done when all five run or preview and I can compare them.
skills.summary: A user asked Codex to redesign an admin feature and produce five designs, and liked all of them.

skills.name: Refactor a million-line repo with 1,393 subagents
skills.prompt: Audit my repo at [path or repo name] for dead code, duplicated logic, and over-complicated modules. Split the cleanup into independent chunks, work on each in a separate branch, and run [test command] after every change. Finish with one pull request summary showing lines removed and test results, and pause for my review before merging or deleting anything.
skills.summary: A Nous Research developer had Hermes dispatch 1,393 subagents over about 19 hours to clean up its own repo, cutting non-test Python source by 34.4% in a merged PR.

skills.name: Replace token-heavy Jira and GitLab MCPs with CLI skills
skills.prompt: I use the [Jira, GitLab, or other] command line tool and want to replace its token-heavy MCP server with a lightweight skill. Run --help on the CLI and its subcommands, then write a Markdown skill file listing the common actions I need, such as [create ticket, list merge requests, comment], with exact example commands. Stop when the skill works on one real read-only task, and ask me before running any command that creates, changes or deletes anything.
skills.summary: The author had Claude run --help on Atlassian and GitLab CLIs, saved the actions as Markdown, and built lightweight agent plugins that cut token use.

skills.name: Resolve a Slack-reported issue with a coding agent
skills.prompt: Here is an issue from my team: [paste issue text or link] in the repo at [repo path or URL]. Find the cause, make the fix, run the tests, and open a pull request with a short summary of what changed and how you checked it. You're done when tests pass and the summary is ready for me to review. Don't merge or deploy anything, and pause to show me the diff before pushing.
skills.summary: A Codex agent resolved an issue passed to it in about 40 minutes, and an ops agent verified the fix back in Slack.

skills.name: Resolve git merge conflicts and push a fix
skills.prompt: My repo at [path to repo] has merge conflicts after merging [branch A] into [branch B]. Compare both sides of each conflicted file, explain what each side changed, and propose a merged version for me to review. Once I approve, run [test command] to confirm nothing broke, then pause and show me the commit and push details before pushing to [branch name].
skills.summary: A tutorial shows Scout comparing both sides of merge conflicts, proposing a merged file for review, then committing and pushing to a branch.

skills.name: Restyle a pull request to match repo house style
skills.prompt: Read the contributing guide and recent merged code in this repo to learn its house style, then review my pull request on branch [branch name] and make the code changes needed to match it, such as naming, structure and error handling, not just comments. Show me the diff and a list of the style rules you applied, and run the tests and linter. Do not push or commit until I approve.
skills.summary: A developer asked Claude to update a PR to the repo's house style, but it only rewrote comments to be lowercase and less useful, making no code changes.

skills.name: Reverse engineer legacy systems without source code
skills.prompt: I have a legacy system in [folder path] and no documentation. Read through the code, configs, and database schemas and write a blueprint in a markdown file covering what the system does, its main workflows, data flows, and business rules. Mark anything you are unsure about as unverified. Do not modify any files other than the blueprint. Stop when every major module is described.
skills.summary: Thoughtworks consultants used Gemini 2.5 Pro in a two-week pilot to produce validated blueprints of legacy systems' functionality.

skills.name: Review AI-written code with a layered agent review process
skills.prompt: Review the pull request on branch [branch name] in this repo in layers. First check it against the intent described in [PR description or ticket link], then look for bugs, missing tests and security issues, and finally check style against our conventions in [file or doc]. Finish with a list of issues sorted by severity and a verdict on whether it is safe to merge; do not change any code or push anything.
skills.summary: Anthropic's Claude Code team describes how it changed its code review process so Claude can write most of Claude Code's code.

skills.name: Review GitHub pull requests automatically
skills.prompt: Build an n8n workflow triggered when a new pull request opens in my GitHub repo [owner/repo]. It should fetch the diff, ask an AI model to review it for bugs, readability and missing tests, then post the review as a comment and add a label such as [label names]. You're done when a test PR gets a useful review comment; pause and show me the comment and label before anything is posted to GitHub.
skills.summary: An n8n AI agent triggers on each new PR, fetches diffs, calls an LLM for a review, and posts comments and labels back on the PR.

skills.name: Review GitHub pull requests for bugs and security
skills.prompt: Review the pull request at [PR URL] and return a structured report with sections for bugs, security issues, and code quality, each with file and line references and a severity. Then turn this into a reusable routine that checks [repo name] for new PRs every [interval] and sends me a short summary. Show me the routine and wait for approval before posting any comments on GitHub.
skills.summary: A Hermes tutorial reads a PR diff and returns a structured review of bugs, security and code quality, then turns it into a skill that watches repos and sends summaries.

skills.name: Review Linux kernel patches
skills.prompt: Act as a code reviewer for this patch or diff: [paste diff or give branch name] in the repo at [path]. Check for bugs, memory or concurrency problems, missing error handling, and unclear naming, citing exact lines. Finish with a prioritized list of findings and a one-paragraph verdict on whether it's ready to merge.
skills.summary: Google engineers launched Sashiko, an agentic AI code reviewer for the Linux kernel.

skills.name: Rewrite a README after a rearchitecture
skills.prompt: My project at [path to repo] was recently rearchitected. Scan the code and rewrite the README with accurate setup steps, configuration, and API details, checking each command against the real code. Leave clearly marked placeholders for design rationale and project purpose that I will fill in. Put the change on a new branch and show me the diff before opening a PR.
skills.summary: Devin scanned a rearchitected codebase and delivered a new README as a PR with accurate setup and API details, but struggled with design rationale and purpose.

skills.name: Rewrite a runtime from TypeScript to Rust with agents
skills.prompt: I want to migrate [module or component] in [owner/repo] from [current language] to [target language]. First write a plan that splits the work into small, independently reviewable pull requests, and show it to me before starting. Then work through them one at a time, with each PR passing the existing tests, and list any behavior differences you find.
skills.summary: GitHub engineers used Copilot tools to have agents write most of an 800,000-line Rust rewrite of the Copilot runtime across 128 PRs, fixing a few regressions.

skills.name: Route Linear tickets to PRs across multiple repos
skills.prompt: Set up a flow where I send a task by [Telegram or another chat app] and you create a Linear ticket for it in [team name]. Route each ticket to the right repo from [list of repos] and the right model, and have the coding agent open a pull request for review. Stop when one test task has gone from message to open PR, and never merge anything without my approval.
skills.summary: A developer sends tasks via Telegram/OpenClaw into Linear, where Cyrus routes each to the right repo and model and opens PRs for review.

skills.name: Run Claude Code in an isolated VM that opens PRs
skills.prompt: Help me set up a locked-down virtual machine for running you on my project [repo name]. Give it only the permissions it needs: reading the code, getting secrets from [secrets manager], and opening issues and pull requests on [Git host], with no ability to merge. Walk me through the setup step by step, and finish by having it open a small test pull request. Pause and show me each command that changes my system or credentials before you run it.
skills.summary: The author runs Claude Code in a restricted VM with secrets served from Infisical. It can only create issues and PRs on Forgejo, and merges are manual before CI deploys.

skills.name: Run Claude Code on local models via Ollama
skills.prompt: Help me set up Claude Code to run against a local model through Ollama on my [Mac/Windows/Linux] machine, using [IntelliJ/my editor] as my IDE. Walk me through installing Ollama, pulling a suitable coding model for my hardware ([RAM/GPU]), and pointing Claude Code at it. You're done when Claude Code answers a simple request about a file in [my project folder] using the local model. Show me any config files or commands before you change or run them.
skills.summary: A guide to setting up Claude Code in IntelliJ and connecting it to local models through Ollama for coding work.

skills.name: Run Codex with low-touch planning and port reservation
skills.prompt: I've written a plan for [task] in [repo path]: [paste or point to plan file]. Carry it out mostly on your own, and before starting any dev server or test that needs a network port, pick a free port, reserve it, and pass it in through [env var or config setting] so it doesn't clash with other running jobs. When done, summarize what you changed and which checks passed so I can review, and ask me before pushing or deleting anything.
skills.summary: A commenter has Codex execute mostly on its own with human planning and review, including a portbroker that reserves and injects a port.

skills.name: Run OpenClaw agents for Terraform infra and GitOps from Telegram
skills.prompt: Set up separate agents on my [Telegram or chat app] for [infrastructure setup, code review, and deployment]. Using my [GitHub repo], have the infra agent write Terraform for [cloud provider and resources], have the review agent comment on pull requests, and have the deploy agent run a GitOps pipeline for [environment]. Finished means a working pipeline from merged PR to deployed change. Pause and show me the plan before applying any Terraform, merging, or deleting anything.
skills.summary: Several OpenClaw agents with separate identities set up Terraform infrastructure, did coding work, code reviews, merges and built a CD and GitOps system.

skills.name: Run Terraform plan and apply through an MCP agent
skills.prompt: Connect to my Terraform project and database via MCP, run a terraform plan against [resource/environment], and summarize what will change. Pause and show me the exact plan before running apply, since this will modify infrastructure.
skills.summary: The author had Cursor run Terraform against Postgres via MCP; the apply hit a permissions error and he finished from the terminal.

skills.name: Run a coding agent on a live Excalidraw canvas
skills.prompt: Help me set up a workflow where a coding agent can read and edit a diagram in [Excalidraw file path or URL] as part of working on [project]. Start by generating an architecture diagram of the code in this repo, then update it when I describe a change like [example change]. Done means the diagram file is saved in the repo and matches the code, and ask me before overwriting any existing file.
skills.summary: Drawgent is a coding agent that works on a live Excalidraw canvas.

skills.name: Run a fleet of engineer bots that fix CI and ship PRs
skills.prompt: Watch [repo URL] for failing CI runs and security alerts, and launch a separate agent for each one to diagnose it and fix it in a branch. Open a pull request for each fix, request review from [team or person], and post a status summary of everything handled. Do not merge or deploy anything; leave that for me in the morning.
skills.summary: A SpaceXAI engineer runs five specialized Grok bots that launch cloud agents, fix failing CI and security issues, trigger reviews, and ship PRs overnight, handling over 200 agents at once.

skills.name: Run a multi-bot team that opens draft PRs
skills.prompt: Set up a team of bots for my repo [repo URL]: one maps the codebase, one classifies the task from [issue tracker or label], one builds a minimal change, one runs tests and lint, one reviews, and one checks security. Each task should end in a draft pull request with a summary of what changed and the test results. Never merge or push to the main branch; leave every PR as a draft for me to review.
skills.summary: A Grok setup of research, classifier, builder, tester, reviewer, and security bots maps repos, makes minimal changes, runs tests and lint, and opens draft PRs; the author reports over 1,000 PRs.

skills.name: Run a persistent project manager agent for a software project
skills.prompt: Act as a persistent project manager for my software project [project name and repo link]. Keep one ongoing session where you track the task list, check on progress each [day/week], and give me a short status of what is done, blocked, and next. Before you assign work to another agent, message anyone, or change the repo, show me exactly what you plan to do and wait for my approval.
skills.summary: A user tried setting up their Dot as a persistent project manager coordinating a large software project, but it has not reliably maintained the single agent session it was meant to coordinate through.

skills.name: Run a planner and cheap executor subagent coding pipeline
skills.prompt: In [repo path], set up a two-stage workflow for this task: [task description]. First, use the strongest model to write a step-by-step plan with small, well-specified subtasks and acceptance tests. Then hand each subtask to a cheaper, smaller model as an executor subagent, and have the planner review each result. Stop when all acceptance tests pass, and give me a summary of the plan, the changes, and any subtasks that needed rework.
skills.summary: The commenter uses Codex with GPT-5.5 as planner and a GPT-5.4 Mini agent as executor so cheaper models handle tasks that would otherwise cost too much.

skills.name: Run a self-hosted, sandboxed software factory
skills.prompt: Help me design a sandboxed pipeline where coding agents build [project idea] inside Docker containers with no access to my personal files or credentials. Write the container setup, a task queue folder, and a script that runs one agent on one task and saves the result as a branch. Finish when I can run one example task end to end, and show me the plan before running anything that touches the network.
skills.summary: One developer's build log of an almost fully self-hosted, sandboxed agentic pipeline for producing software.

skills.name: Run a task-manager sub-agent with atomic commits
skills.prompt: Create a Claude Code sub-agent called task-manager for [project]. It should fetch the next open task from [task file or tracker], hand it to me to work on, mark it complete when done, and require an atomic commit with a commit ID before closing any task. Finish by running it on one sample task and showing me the result.
skills.summary: A poster built a Claude Code sub-agent that fetches the next task, marks it complete, and enforces atomic commits with a mandatory commit id.

skills.name: Run agent builds and tests on remote Windows VMs
skills.prompt: I'm working in [project folder] on my [Mac/Linux] machine, but builds and tests must run on a remote Windows machine. You can reach it with ssh at [user@host] and use WSL there. Sync the code to [remote path], run [build command] and [test command] over ssh, and report which tests passed and failed with the relevant error output. Do not delete or overwrite anything on the remote machine outside [remote path], and show me any command that would do so before running it.
skills.summary: A developer gives coding agents ssh access to WSL instances on remote Windows VMs to run builds and tests instead of on their Mac laptop.

skills.name: Run agents that work Jira tickets, review PRs and send updates
skills.prompt: Watch my Jira project [project key] for tickets assigned to [me / label]. For each one, read it, make the code change in [repo], and open a pull request that links the ticket. Pause and show me the PR and any status update you plan to post to [Slack channel] before posting, and stop once each ticket has a PR.
skills.summary: Luke runs several Hermes agents that read Jira tickets, write code, review PRs, track costs, summarize docs and send updates.

skills.name: Run an AI software factory that opens, reviews, and merges PRs
skills.prompt: Set up a workflow for the repository [repo name] where an agent picks up issues labeled [label], opens a pull request with a fix and tests, and a second agent reviews it. Write the configuration and a short guide for how it runs. Do not enable automatic merging yet; show me the merge rules you propose and wait for my approval.
skills.summary: A guide to building agents that open, review, and merge pull requests.

skills.name: Run builds, tests and PR creation with shell commands
skills.prompt: In [path to repo], run the build with [build command], the tests with [test command] and the linter with [lint command], then summarize what passed and failed. Fix simple failures, and list my open PRs using the gh CLI. If everything is green, draft a PR title and description for [branch name] and pause to show me before creating it.
skills.summary: A guide shows Scout running build, test, lint and gh commands, listing or creating PRs, and handing diff reviews and test runs to background sub-agents.

skills.name: Run coding agents like a medical team to fix bugs
skills.prompt: Treat the bugs in this repo like patients in a hospital. For each bug in [issue list or file], have one agent triage and reproduce it, another diagnose the root cause, and another write a fix with a test, then have a separate reviewer check the fix. Finish with a summary table of each bug, its diagnosis, the fix and test status, and pause for my approval before committing or pushing anything.
skills.summary: Over five months, the author treated bugs like patients and organized coding agents as a hospital-style team to diagnose and fix them.

skills.name: Run each coding agent session in a cgroup that is killed on completion
skills.prompt: In my repo at [path], write a small agent spawner script for [Linux distro or systemd setup] that launches each coding agent session in its own cgroup and kills every leftover process in that cgroup when the task finishes or fails. Also add a scheduled job that deletes stale files older than [number] hours in [tmp directory]. Finish by running a test session that leaves a background process behind and showing me that it gets cleaned up. Before deleting any files or killing processes outside the test, show me what would be removed and wait for my approval.
skills.summary: A developer built an agent spawner that launches each coding agent session in its own cgroup and kills leftover processes when the task completes, plus a job that clears stale tmp files.

skills.name: Run longer coding sessions with Copilot Agent Mode
skills.prompt: Use agent mode with Claude Sonnet as the model to build [a small but complete feature or app, e.g. a CRUD page for X] in my project in [folder or repo]. Work in stages: first propose a plan and file list, then implement it, run the app or tests, and fix any errors you hit. Finish when the feature works end to end, and give me a summary of the files you changed and how to run it.
skills.summary: A developer moved from Copilot syntax questions to agent-mode sessions, switched to Claude Sonnet as the model, and tried building more complete things.

skills.name: Run multi-file refactors and sysadmin tasks on network machines
skills.prompt: On [machine or repo path], carry out this task: [precisely defined refactor or sysadmin job, e.g. rename function X across all files and update tests]. Work through all affected files, run [test or verification command], and report what changed. Pause and show me the plan before running anything destructive such as deleting files, restarting services, or changing system config.
skills.summary: A user uses Codex for multi-file refactors and precisely defined tasks on their network PCs and servers, then walks away.

skills.name: Run multi-stage PR reviews with parallel sub-agents
skills.prompt: Review the pull request at [PR URL or branch name] in stages: use separate sub-agents to check correctness, security, tests, and style, then run a validation pass that discards findings you can't back up with a specific line of code. Finish with one ranked list of issues, each with file, line, and a suggested fix. Don't post any comments to the PR; just show me the list.
skills.summary: A Claude Code plugin that reviews pull requests in stages with sub-agents and validation passes, with optional ensemble review via Codex.

skills.name: Run parallel coding agents from Markdown specs in tmux
skills.prompt: Set up a tmux session with [number, e.g. 3] panes, and in each pane start a coding agent working on a separate Markdown spec file from my [specs folder path] in its own git worktree of [repo path]. Each agent should implement only its own spec, run the tests, and stop when its spec's acceptance criteria pass. Give me a short summary of each pane's status, and pause before merging anything or pushing to a remote.
skills.summary: A workflow post on running multiple coding agents in parallel using tmux and Markdown specs, based on the title.

skills.name: Run parallel local coding agent sessions
skills.prompt: I want to work on [N] separate tasks in my repo at [path] at the same time. For each task, create its own git worktree and branch, work on it independently, run the tests, and summarize what changed. The tasks are: [task 1], [task 2], [task 3]. Stop when each branch has a passing diff ready for my review, and do not merge anything.
skills.summary: A developer runs up to 10 coding agent sessions at once, using Claude Code and local models on RTX 3090s with cached contexts for daily development work.

skills.name: Run production deploys and port scans from Telegram with OpenClaw
skills.prompt: Work as my ops assistant over [Telegram] with read-only access to [production server]. When I ask, scan [VPS IP/host] for exposed ports and report findings, and propose deploy changes as pull requests on [repo] only. Do not restart services or change anything live until I approve each step.
skills.summary: A security professional uses an OpenClaw agent with read-only prod access, PR-only changes and manual approval for restarts to deploy changes and scan a VPS for exposed ports.

skills.name: Run sandboxed Claude Code fleet sharing files via MCP
skills.prompt: Help me design a small fleet of sandboxed Claude Code instances that share files through an MCP server exposing a virtual filesystem. Build a minimal prototype with [number] agents, a shared file store backed by [local folder or S3 bucket], and an audit log of every file read and write. Stop when two agents can pass a file to each other and I can read the log, and ask before touching any cloud resources or credentials.
skills.summary: A developer runs a fleet of sandboxed Claude Code instances that share files through MCP tools on a virtual filesystem, with an orchestrator handling AWS storage and audit logs.

skills.name: Run terminal commands via Copilot CLI subagents
skills.prompt: Use the Copilot CLI to tackle [large task, e.g. update all API endpoints to use the new auth helper] in my [repo]. Split it into independent pieces, use /fleet or subagents to run them in parallel, and have each one run its own terminal commands and tests. Show me the split plan before starting, and when done, give me a combined summary of changes and test results, and don't commit or push anything without asking.
skills.summary: A commenter uses Copilot CLI agents that execute terminal commands, including the /fleet command and subagent-style workflows.

skills.name: Run terminal commands with Copilot agent mode
skills.prompt: In my project at [path], run [build or test command] in the terminal and fix any failures. If you can't read the terminal output, tell me instead of guessing, and don't change code that is already working. Stop when the command passes, and give me a list of every file you changed.
skills.summary: Users report the agent sometimes fails to read terminal output and may undo correct code; workarounds include switching shells.

skills.name: Scaffold a new service end to end with agents
skills.prompt: Scaffold a new service called [service name] including Terraform, Kubernetes manifests, and CI config, validating each file as you go. Open a draft pull request with the changes, but show me exactly what will be created or deleted before running any cleanup or deletion commands.
skills.summary: Cursor agents create Terraform, k8s manifests and CI, validate them and open a draft PR; one cleanup run wrongly deleted Terraform files.

skills.name: Scaffold a second module from an existing one's structure
skills.prompt: Create a new module called [new module name] in [repo name], modeled on the existing module [existing module path]. Before writing anything, open and read every file in that module and list its structure, naming conventions, and patterns back to me. Then scaffold the new module to match, and finish by confirming that it builds and that its structure mirrors the original.
skills.summary: A commenter asked Cursor to create a second module following another module's structure, but it failed because it did not read the relevant files.

skills.name: Scan an app for UX improvements with computer use
skills.prompt: Run my app at [how to start it] and use computer use to click through the main flows: [list of 2-3 key screens or tasks]. Note anything confusing, inconsistent, or slow from a user's point of view. Finish with a prioritized list of [5-10] UX improvements, each with the screen it applies to, and don't change any code until I pick which to do.
skills.summary: A user tried Claude Code's computer-use feature on Windows to scan their app for UX improvements, and asks whether it works well there.

skills.name: Scan every git commit for secrets and injection flaws
skills.prompt: Set up a git pre-commit hook in [repo path] that runs Claude Code to review each staged diff for hardcoded secrets, injection flaws (SQL, command, XSS), and risky database migrations. If it finds a problem, block the commit and print the file, line, and a suggested fix. Show me the hook script and test it on a sample bad commit before installing it permanently.
skills.summary: A free tool runs 11 Claude Code CLI agents on each commit to catch secrets, injection flaws, and bad migrations before code lands.

skills.name: Screen interview code submissions with a Codex review agent
skills.prompt: Write an agents.md for [repo or take-home project] that tells you how to screen candidate submissions: flag any submission that changes or adds more than [number] files, doesn't follow [requirement], or lacks tests. Then review the submission in [folder path] against it and give me a pass or reject recommendation with reasons. You're done when I have a short review I can use; don't contact the candidate or post anything anywhere.
skills.summary: A commenter uses Codex with a targeted agents.md for front-line code reviews, rejecting submissions with too many files changed or added.

skills.name: Self-host services on a home server
skills.prompt: Help me set up [service, e.g. Jellyfin or Nextcloud] on my home server at [hostname or IP] using Docker Compose. Inspect what's already installed, write the compose file and reverse proxy config, and explain each step. Finish when the service is reachable at [URL] and I have a backup plan noted. Pause and show me any command that deletes data, opens ports, or changes firewall rules before you run it.
skills.summary: A write-up on how CLI agents make running your own home server easier and more fun.

skills.name: Set up nightly GitHub backups with one sentence
skills.prompt: Back up [folder path] to my GitHub repo [repo URL] every night at [time] in [my timezone]. Create the scheduled job, handle any UTC versus local time differences, and add an hourly self-check that confirms the last push succeeded and alerts me on [Telegram / other channel] if it did not. Before the first push, show me what files will be included and wait for my OK, then run a test and verify the commit appears on GitHub.
skills.summary: Hermes took a single plain-English instruction, found its GitHub skills, created and verified a nightly push cron job, and added an hourly self-check to handle UTC versus central time.

skills.name: Set up weekly changelogs and fix docs from GitHub issues
skills.prompt: In my docs repo at [path to repo], read the open GitHub issues labeled [label] and make the doc changes each one asks for, one branch per issue. Also draft this week's changelog from [source, e.g. merged PRs since last Friday] following the format in [example changelog file]. Pause and show me each diff before opening any PRs.
skills.summary: Neon's docs team has Devin create the weekly changelog from a playbook and open or revise doc PRs from GitHub issues, for repetitive work only.

skills.name: Shepherd PRs to merge automatically
skills.prompt: Every 30 minutes, check open pull requests in [repo]. Send failing PRs back to a coding agent to fix, and review the clean ones. Only auto-merge a PR if you are highly confident and it is low-risk, such as [examples]; otherwise ping me with a summary. Pause and ask me before merging anything that touches [sensitive areas].
skills.summary: Bots check PRs every 30 minutes, send failures back to a cloud agent, review clean PRs and auto-merge high-confidence, low-risk ones.

skills.name: Ship a backlog landing page from a ticket spec
skills.prompt: Using this spec: [short description of the page, such as sections, copy and pricing tiers], build the landing page in my repo [repo name] on a new branch and open a pull request. Match the existing styles and components in the codebase. You're done when the page renders locally with no lint errors and the PR description lists what you changed. Show me the diff summary before you open the PR.
skills.summary: Cursor's background agent built a pricing landing page from a short spec in about 5 minutes on a new branch and opened a PR.

skills.name: Ship a first iOS app to the App Store with Replit
skills.prompt: Help me build my first iOS app that [describe the app idea]. Plan the minimum features, build them step by step, and then walk me through preparing it for App Store submission, including icons, screenshots, privacy details, and the review checklist. Stop and show me before any submission or payment step.
skills.summary: The poster built their first app on Replit with ChatGPT help and got it approved on the App Store.

skills.name: Ship a product in 72 hours with a bot team
skills.prompt: Build [product description] from an empty repo [repo URL] using a team of bots, with one agent per feature and others reproducing and fixing bugs. Open small PRs, and merge them yourselves only when tests and review checks pass. Stop and ask me before running any database migration or deploying, showing me exactly what will run.
skills.summary: Three SpaceX engineers used a Grok Bot team to go from an empty repo to a product with 433 PRs, with agents reproducing bugs and merging autonomously except for human gates on migrations and deploys.

skills.name: Ship more pull requests with Devin across tools
skills.prompt: Take this task from my backlog: [issue link or description] in repo [repo]. Implement it, run the tests, and open a pull request with a clear summary. Stop when the PR is open and wait for my review before merging anything.
skills.summary: Ryan Carson uses Devin from iPhone, Slack, browser, GitHub and Linear for real work and reports higher PR shipping velocity.

skills.name: Spec features with AI and hand off to coding agent
skills.prompt: I want to add [feature] to this project. First interview me with questions until you can write a clear spec, and save it as SPEC.md. Then implement it and write tests that check the behavior. Finished means the tests pass and you give me a short list of steps to try the feature myself. Ask before deleting files or changing the database.
skills.summary: Author discusses a spec with an AI agent or ChatGPT, then hands it to an agent to code, and tests the outcome instead of reading every line.

skills.name: Speed up Rust code by having agents iteratively optimize it
skills.prompt: Optimize the performance of the Rust code in [path or function name]. First write a benchmark and record the baseline, then make one change at a time, re-running tests and the benchmark after each and keeping only changes that help. Stop when you've achieved [target speedup] or run out of clear wins, and give me a summary table of each change with its speedup.
skills.summary: The post covers asking coding agents to make Rust code faster through repeated iteration.

skills.name: Spend leftover AI quota on reviewable PRs
skills.prompt: Read my goals in [path to goals file] and my task list in [path or link to task list]. Pick up to [number] small, well-defined tasks I could use help with, such as call prep notes, prototypes, or small fixes, and do each on its own branch and open it as a pull request in [repo] with a short description of what you did and why. Do not merge anything, and stop once you have opened the PRs and given me a list of them.
skills.summary: RemainderBot uses a founder's goals and task lists to write PRs with spare Claude and Codex quota, producing 111 PRs including call prep and prototypes.

skills.name: Spin up a second agent as an independent QA reviewer
skills.prompt: After you finish implementing [feature or fix] in [project folder], set up a second, independent AI agent in a sandbox to act as a QA reviewer and test your work. Have it check [what to verify, e.g. edge cases, failing tests, UI behavior] and report problems back to you. Do not read, copy, or change any of my credentials, and finish with a summary of the QA findings and fixes.
skills.summary: Codex found the user's Claude login, installed Claude Code in a sandbox, and used it as a QA agent without being told how, leaving credentials untouched.

skills.name: Split a React Native to Swift migration across agents
skills.prompt: I'm migrating [repo] from [old framework, e.g. React Native] to [new framework, e.g. Swift]. Split the work into [number] independent pieces, such as [list modules], and run a separate child agent on each in parallel. Finish when each piece has a PR with passing tests and you've given me a summary of how they fit together; don't merge anything without my approval.
skills.summary: Cognition's Jared Zoneraich uses Devin fan-out so child agents work in parallel on a migration split into six pieces.

skills.name: Split frontend and backend work across Claude Code and Codex
skills.prompt: I'm building [project] and want to split the work: you handle the frontend in [frontend folder] and another agent handles the backend in [backend folder]. First write a short shared contract describing the API endpoints and data shapes at [file path]. Then build the frontend against it, and stop when it works with a mock of the backend. Tell me what the backend must match.
skills.summary: A poster ran Claude Code and Codex in parallel for 15 days, with Claude Code on the frontend and another agent on the backend.

skills.name: Split work between ChatGPT architect and Codex executor
skills.prompt: I'm using ChatGPT as the planner and reviewer for [project or repo path], and you're the executor. Read the plan I paste below, carry it out step by step in the local repo, and run [tests or build command] after each step. When finished, give me a short summary of what changed, the files touched, and any test results that I can paste back to ChatGPT for review. Pause and ask me before deleting files or pushing anything. Plan: [paste plan from ChatGPT]
skills.summary: The poster built a bridge where ChatGPT plans and reviews while Codex does the local execution work.

skills.name: Take ideas to implementation with a planning-command pipeline
skills.prompt: Set up a planning pipeline for my project in [repo or product name] as custom slash commands: one to capture intent, one for impact analysis, one for planning, one for execution, and one for review. Make the execution step run [my lint and test commands] and stop if they fail. Test it on this small feature: [feature idea]. Stop when the feature has gone through all five steps and I have a reviewed diff, and do not commit or push without asking me.

skills.name: Test API endpoints in Postman and report results
skills.prompt: Open [Postman workspace or collection URL] and, for each endpoint in [collection name], generate realistic test payloads based on the API docs at [docs URL]. Run the requests and record the status code, response time, and any errors. Finish with a short report listing which endpoints passed and failed and why. Don't modify or delete any existing requests, and use only the [staging or test] environment.
skills.summary: @ai_for_success used Comet to generate test payloads from context, run API endpoint tests in Postman and produce a final report.

skills.name: Test Devin on integrations, migration and security review
skills.prompt: Take on three tasks in my repo [repo name]: add an integration with [observability tool], migrate [a module or tool] to [target tool or version], and review the code for security vulnerabilities. For each one, tell me how you verified your results, and clearly mark any finding you could not confirm. Open separate pull requests for the work and do not merge anything.
skills.summary: Answer.AI tried Devin on an observability integration, an nbdev migration and a vulnerability review; it found some real issues, hallucinated others, and failed the migration.

skills.name: Test Devin on pulling Notion data into Sheets
skills.prompt: Pull the data from my Notion database [database name or link] into a new Google Sheet, with one column per Notion property and one row per entry. Keep the Sheet in a shared location I can open, and tell me the link when the row count in the Sheet matches the Notion database. Ask me before overwriting or deleting anything that already exists.
skills.summary: Answer.AI testers found Devin completed only 3 of 20 tasks, succeeding at moving Notion data to Google Sheets and building a planet tracker.

skills.name: Test features on screen and merge fixed PRs
skills.prompt: Check out the pull request [PR link] for [repo], run the app, and click through the new feature [feature description] while recording the screen and narrating what you see. If you find bugs, fix them and push to the branch. Show me the recording and summary, and wait for my go-ahead before merging.

skills.name: Test how well coding agents can onboard to your product
skills.prompt: Act as a new developer trying to onboard to [my product or API] using only its public docs at [docs URL]. Try to complete the quickstart in a fresh temporary folder, recording every step, error, and point where you got stuck. Finish with a scorecard out of 10, a list of the top five doc or setup fixes, and a log of what you tried. Do not use any real credentials without asking me first.
skills.summary: ax-check.com runs coding agents in sandboxes to try onboarding to a product, then returns a scorecard, suggested fixes, and full session traces.

skills.name: Test local web apps and fix errors in one session
skills.prompt: Start my app locally with [start command], then open it in Chrome at [localhost URL] and click through [feature or flow]. Read the browser console and network errors, find the cause in the code, and fix it. Repeat until the flow works with no console errors. Then summarize what you changed. Don't commit or push anything without asking me.
skills.summary: Claude Code with Claude in Chrome writes code, opens localhost, clicks through the UI, reads console errors and fixes them without the developer touching the browser.

skills.name: Triage AWS costs with a slimmer MCP server
skills.prompt: Review my MCP server in [path to project] that exposes [number] tools for [e.g. AWS cost data]. Propose a slimmer design that merges overlapping tools into as few as possible, trims the schemas, and still answers questions like [example question]. Show me the plan and the before and after tool counts before editing any files, then implement it and compare the number of tool calls on that question.
skills.summary: Author rebuilt an AWS cost-triage MCP server from 15 tools to 4, cutting a question from 7 tool calls to 2 with schemas 88% smaller.

skills.name: Triage P2 bugs into draft PRs with demo videos
skills.prompt: Connect to GitHub repo [repo] and Slack channel [#bugs]. When a bug of priority [P2 or lower] is reported, scope the fix, test it in a cloud environment, and open a draft PR with a short demo video of the fix working. Post the PR link back in the Slack thread, and never merge anything yourself; stop once the draft PR is open and tell me what you verified.
skills.summary: A Dot connected to GitHub and Slack watches #bugs, scopes and tests a fix in a cloud environment, and opens a draft PR with a short demo video.

skills.name: Triage failed GitHub Actions runs and self-heal flaky tests
skills.prompt: Review failed GitHub Actions runs on [repo] from the last [7 days]. Classify each as real bug, flaky test, or infra issue, post a summary to [Slack channel], and open an issue for each real bug. Don't change any test assertions or merge anything; show me proposed fixes for flaky tests first.
skills.summary: A QA engineer's OpenClaw agent reads failed CI logs, classifies failures, posts analysis to GitHub and Slack and opens issues; flakiness fell from 8% to 0.8%, though it once wrongly altered an assertion.

skills.name: Triage issues and open fix PRs with a GitHub bot
skills.prompt: Help me set up a GitHub bot for [owner/repo] that triages new issues with labels, reviews pull requests, answers questions with citations to the repo's docs or code, and flags low-effort AI-generated contributions. For clear small bugs it should open a patch PR for human review only. Build it, test it on a few existing issues in dry-run mode, and show me the output before it posts any comments or opens any PRs.
skills.summary: A cookbook shows a GitHub bot that triages issues, reviews PRs, answers questions with citations, flags AI-slop contributions, and opens patch PRs for human review.

skills.name: Troubleshoot a production-only performance issue
skills.prompt: Our [framework, e.g. NestJS] app is slow in production but not locally, specifically [endpoint or page]. Read the code and database queries involved, identify the slowest or most repeated ones, and recommend indexes or query changes with an explanation of why. You're done when you have a ranked list of fixes with the exact migration or code change for each. Don't run anything against the production database; show me the changes first.
skills.summary: A developer used Cursor and Warp agents to analyze NestJS database queries and recommend indexes for a production performance problem.

skills.name: Try Devin for pull requests on a company codebase
skills.prompt: In [repo name], take this ticket: [ticket description or link]. Make the change, run the existing tests, and open a pull request with a clear description of what you changed and why. Show me the plan and the diff before you push, and list anything you were unsure about so I can review it quickly.
skills.summary: A commenter's team tried Devin but found PRs slow and still needing review, so it felt like a junior developer.

skills.name: Turn GitHub issues into draft pull requests with long-running agents
skills.prompt: Read the open issues in my GitHub repo [repo URL] and pick the [number] most well-defined ones labeled [label or topic]. For each, make a branch and prepare a draft pull request with a first-pass fix, tests if the repo has them, and a short description of what you did and what you're unsure about. Don't merge or push anything beyond draft PRs, and show me the list of PRs you plan to open before you open them.
skills.summary: The author used Dots for read-heavy long-horizon tasks like reading GitHub issues and making PRs, which were typically poor but gave a starting point.

skills.name: Turn Sentry bug reports into fix pull requests
skills.prompt: Take the Sentry issue [issue link or ID] in my repo [repo name] and find the root cause using the stack trace and recent commits. Write a minimal fix with a test that reproduces the bug, then prepare a pull request describing the cause and the change. Finished means the tests pass and the PR is ready on a new branch. Show me the diff and PR description before you open the pull request or push anything.
skills.summary: Sentry's Seer passes root cause analysis and issue context to a Cursor Cloud Agent, which writes the fix and opens a pull request in the user's repo.

skills.name: Turn Slack and Linear tasks into PRs and fix CI
skills.prompt: Take the task in [Slack thread or Linear ticket link] and implement it in my repo [repo name], then open a pull request describing the change. If CI or lint checks fail, keep fixing them and pushing until every check passes, and stop there. Pause and show me the PR summary before requesting reviewers or merging anything.
skills.summary: Cognition staff assign Devin work in Slack or Linear; it posts PRs, fixes bugs flagged by review bots and works CI and lint failures until checks pass.

skills.name: Turn Slack feedback into PRs and debug infra
skills.prompt: Read the feedback in [Slack channel] from the last [timeframe], group it into bugs and requests, and pick the top [number] issues you can fix in [repo]. Open a pull request for each, and for any production debugging use read-only access. Show me your triage list and the PRs before posting replies or merging.

skills.name: Turn a website into a mobile app
skills.prompt: Turn my website at [URL] into a mobile app for [iOS/Android/both]. Match the site's branding, with these main screens: [list, e.g. home, products, contact], and show me a preview I can test. Stop when the app runs in preview and you have a checklist of what I need for store submission, and ask me before spending credits on any big redesign or submitting anything to a store.
skills.summary: The author used Replit Agent 4 over about two days and roughly $40 to turn a website into a mobile app with design, preview, and App Store prep, then submitted it for review.

skills.name: Turn customer feedback into tested pull requests
skills.prompt: Watch [feedback source, e.g. support inbox, forum, or survey sheet] for requests that recur at least [number] times. Stop after [number] PRs and show me the list before merging or pushing anything beyond drafts.
skills.summary: In OpenAI's own launch example, a Dot watches feedback for recurring requests, scopes small fixes, builds and tests them, and returns PRs with demo videos.

skills.name: Turn daily X bookmarks into working tech prototypes
skills.prompt: Every morning, review my saved bookmarks on [X or another bookmarking service], pick one new technology or tool I haven't tried, and draft a prompt for a small prototype that shows it off. skills.name: Turn one goal into an ordered plan of coding-agent tasks

skills.name: Turn tickets into merged pull requests

skills.name: Turn tickets into merged pull requests with one-shot coding agents
